💡 Key Takeaways
  • Battlefield 6 is about to receive a new upgrade.
  • That honour goes to a couple of the high-level changes Battlefield Studios has included with the new patch, which range from a major pass on audio to a fix for a particularly annoying bug that’s been seemingly introduced with a recent patch.
  • Industry observers note that thew new content takes the form of a limited-time version of the game’s Empire State map, which covers it in snow and tweaks its layout slightly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield 6 is about to receive a new upgrade. Version 1.1.3.0 is set to arrive tomorrow, December 9 to kick off the third and final phase of the game’s first season. Winter Offensive brings some holiday-themed new content to the game, but it’s not the most interesting part of the patch.

That honour goes to a couple of the high-level changes Battlefield Studios has included with the new patch, which range from a major pass on audio to a fix for a particularly annoying bug that’s been seemingly introduced with a recent patch.

Industry observers note that thew new content takes the form of a limited-time version of the game’s Empire State map, which covers it in snow and tweaks its layout slightly. To go along with that there are new limited-time modes for both multiplayer and Redsec’s Gauntlet. The event mode will be available in Conquest, and Domination.

The Ice Climbing Axe is the only newly introduced weapon in this drop. The battle pass gets a new Winter Offensive bonus path, just like we’ve seen with previous seasonal stages. This is how you unlock the axe, too.

Easily the most interesting change in this upgrade is the range of improvements to audio across the board. First, footstep audio received a big pass that should make it easier to hear enemy footsteps, easier to locate them, and across different surfaces.

Recent findings suggest that some of the bugs that caused certain sounds to simply vanish have been fixed. This was especially prevalent in battle royale matches. BF Studios explained in the patch notes that it has adjusted memory priorities for in-game sounds in order to prioritise the most crucial ones. This is not the end of the road on audio, however, as the developer continues to work on making the soundscape more stable and reliable.

Some of those audio changes are the result of recent testing done in Battlefield Labs, which is also responsible for another exciting addition in this latest patch: improvements to hit registration.

While BF6 has had solid and stable netcode, certain situations would sometimes create uncertainty about how you died, and why certain actions seemingly failed to perform at that particular moment.

The focus in this update is to improve the reliability of how actions in close-quarter combat are translated, which includes firing before fully going into ADS, quick aim changes and more.

Speaking of close-range, the patch also brings another pass to soldier visibility to make it easier for enemies to stand out from the background. This is particularly relevant in areas with low contrast, or busy environments with lots of particle and visual effects.

It has been revealed that 1.1.3.0 also brings yet another set of weapon handling and gunplay tweaks, this time focusing on accuracy complications with first shots. You can also expect more tweaks to attachment behaviour with regards to recoil.

Something else worth highlighting is that vehicle gameplay is getting several smaller tweaks that have to do with how they interact with the world, how their HUDs behave and more. Finally, your settings should no longer be reset after applying an patch. BF Studios states there are still some instances where that might happen, but the concern should be fixed for the majority of players.

You can read the full change log on the Battlefield blog.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, one baby black bear who spent time at Anan Creek in southeastern Alaska’s Tongass National Forest demonstrated off those climbing chops in style.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

They may be small, but bear cubs have a pretty steep learning curve. In Alaska, brown bear (Ursus americanus) cubs have a roughly 50 percent survival rate within their first year, while the black bear (Ursus americanus) cub survival rate can range from 51 to 88 percent, depending on where they live. Cubs must learn how to fish, forage, find shelter, and climb trees to escape predators. Fortunately, biology helps out a bit with climbing. Bears have claws that curve and help them go up the tree and then back down safely.

According to recent reports, one baby black bear who spent time at Anan Creek in southeastern Alaska’s Tongass National Forest demonstrated off those climbing chops in style. The park’s rangers have officially awarded this bear with the 2026 Cutest Climber Award.

“This little cub slipped on his way down but caught himself and hustled right after mom,” the rangers write. “An adorable reminder that even when you lose your footing, you can recover and keep going. A tiny, furry lesson in resilience provided by the bears of Anan.”.

Tongass National Forest’s rangers  are right now awarding the Anan Bear Awards to the 39 bears spotted at the Anan Wildlife Observatory in Alaska over the summer.

Tongass is the largest national forest in the United States, and covers most of southeastern Alaska, including the state’s capital city of Juneau. The area includes Mendanhall Glacier (a popular destination for tourists on Alaskan cruises), numerous hiking trails, eagles soaring above, and plenty of bears on the hunt for food. One of the hotspots is Anan Creek, home to one of the largest runs of pink salmon in Southeast Alaska. As such, the creek is a very popular dinner spot among black and brown bears.

Industry observers note that according to Friends of Anan, 39 bears are known to feast on the salmon at Anan Creek. The population includes 31 black bears and eight brown bears. Similar to  their chunky counterparts farther to the north in Katmai National Park, the bears return each summer to feast on salmon and teach their cubs how to fish in order to survive. And also like the fat bears of Katmai, every bear here has their own habits and quirks.

Sources indicate that the U.S. Forest Service tracks and documents every bear spotted at Anan, while explore.org’s cameras broadcast live streams of their antics.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Honda’s automatic engine start-stop feature is under new federal scrutiny, after the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration received hundreds of complaints that engines failed to restart automatically from a complete stop at a traffic light on certain models, prompting the agency to commence an investigation.

In a recent development, the federal probe, declared on Friday, November 13, includes 1.3 million units of the 2024-2026 Honda Passport, Odyssey, Pilot, and Ridgeline. The inquiry also includes 2024-2026 Acura MDX units. NHTSA’s Office of Defects Investigation received 701 complaints related to the Auto Start/Stop feature.

Industry observers note that “To help improve fuel efficiency, the Auto Start/Stop system will automatically shut off the engine when a vehicle comes to a complete stop. The engine is intended to automatically restart when a driver releases the brake pedal. However, the complaints allege that the engines are failing to restart once they have been shut off by this system,” the investigation announcement reads.

Industry observers note that while automatic start-stop systems were created to improve fuel economy, Honda seems to be having a recurring problem with the feature. Federal safety regulators previously opened a probe into Honda’s automatic start-stop system in 2025. That investigation included 2.2 million late-model Honda Pilot, Odyssey, Passport, and Ridgeline models, as well as Acura MDX and TLX units. However, the fresh investigation includes 2026 model-year units. Inquiry documents allege that the two issue populations have different root causes and respond differently to repairs.

In a recent development, there have been no injuries related to this matter, according to the feds. EPA boss Lee Zeldin noted the agency was investigating improvements or eliminating the technology last year; whether it sticks around in the long run, however, an engineering analysis of the stop-start system should bring Honda and NHTSA together to identify an effective solution to this recurring problem soon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

All the time, live service titles are forced to pump out content to avoid stagnating over time, anything to catch the attention of new players and reignite the passion of old returning faces. Sometimes, games feel the need to really shake things up, especially if they’re on the older side of release dates. Today, it seems, League of Legends is joining this number.

Revealed at the tail end of Worlds 2026, Riot has showcased what it calls “League of Legends: New Dawn”, a total revamp of League’s client, mechanics, and visuals to bring it up to snuff with the modern age.

All these changes and more have been requested by the community for years, but now that they’re right around the corner, a vocal segment seems incredibly unimpressed.

It has been revealed that league of Legends is a title that has slowly but surely been pulled down by the weight of its ancient code, forcing the dev team at Riot to totally rewrite decent chunks of the client inside and out to make upcoming proper content. This hiccup has been the excuse for missing features and slow updates for ages, and it looks like Riot is finally ready to put their foot down.

With a new proper rival in the MOBA space via Valve’s Deadlock, Riot has had a bit of a fire lit under them, pushing them to speed up development in this massive overhaul. New runes, new lobby animations, and a fully reworked map are just some of the new content coming in this proper total overhaul of the game, looking to lead League into a New Dawn for the coming years.

According to recent reports, it seems like every member of the classic League roster is also getting a full visual overhaul, bringing them up to the quality showcased by recent releases like Locke and Zaahen. Compounded with the rumors of a sequel series to Arcane in the works, it seems like Riot is focusing hard on celebrating and bringing focus back to base League of Legends, rather than highlighting the universe with different titles.

Sometimes, games feel the need to really shake things up, especially if they’re on the older side of release dates.

Recent findings suggest that riot stayed vague on a lot of the actual reworked mechanics, but with 2 minutes of footage out and a promise of more coming in January, current players and fans who have fallen off the wagon both have a reason to keep an eye out. They say League comes for every PC gamer eventually, and a few good changes could make its tendrils all the harder to avoid.

It has been revealed that A sizable amount of the community response to the announcement has actually been rather negative, tossing shade towards the game for looking too “mobile game-y” after its vibrant new coat of paint. This marks a phenomenon I’ve seen throughout longtime free-to-play titles: a confusing mix of wanting developer attention without actually wanting much changed.

In a recent development, the Counter-Strike community is another proponent of this practice, clearly wanting Valve’s attention through skins and patches, without actually wanting any real part of the CS tempo changed. Now, for longtime fans, this can be understandable; after all, nobody wants their favorite game suddenly changed into something totally different. However, every live service title, no matter the age, needs upcoming blood.

The aging visuals and code of League have clearly been the largest stopgap to its constant evolution, and the promises set forth by Riot for League of Legends: Latest Dawn are seriously hopeful, opening the door for new players and those who have grown tired of the shakiest part of the MOBA giant. Years of work and slow improvement are clear through every inch of the visuals, I just need to see how it plays!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that BYD just got some good news in its Defender-copycat court battle with JLR. After JLR had BYD’s Netherlands offices raided and documents seized, a Dutch court has now handed BYD an early win, ordering JLR to destroy the documents or face a penalty.

After BYD opened orders for the Ti 7 in Europe and the UK in late July, many (including us at Electrek) compared it to the iconic Land Rover Defender, with its boxy, rugged (yet still elegant) SUV design.

BYD even described it as having “an unapologetically boxy profile” that delivers “the imposing, chunky design that finds favour among SUV buyers, yet delivers a contemporary look.”.

In August, authorities on behalf of the British luxury automaker raided BYD’s offices in the Netherlands without prior warning and seized digital records.

On November 11, a Dutch court in The Hague ruled against JLR and ordered the firm to destroy the seized documents, which included launch prepares and other technical data, so they wouldn’t fall into anyone else’s hands.

JLR must destroy the documents within 24 hours of the ruling or face a fine of €50,000 ($55,000) for every hour it is delayed, with a maximum penalty of up to €500,000 ($553,000).

Sources indicate that within 24 hours of destroying it, JLR must also provide BYD with third-party confirmation that it has been destroyed. The court also rejected the British automaker’s request to pay a €500,000 ($553,000) fine.

According to Autoweek Netherlands, the ruling is based on the fact that JLR doesn’t need the documents, noting that the Ti 7 has not yet been sold in the European Union.

BYD won the ruling, and JLR is prohibited from taking any further legal action under the initial seizure order, but JLR has already begun summary proceedings over the infringement in Rotterdam and The Hague.

JLR claims that the Ti 7 SUV is a “slavish imitation” and infringes on the intellectual property of the Land Rover Defender and that BYD stripped down the Defender to reverse-engineer some of its technology.

Before the raid, BYD claims it fully cooperated with JLR’s requests. BYD’s lawyers called the British automakers’ raid a “fishing expedition” and claimed that “too many files were seized.”.

According to recent reports, the Ti 7 is on sale starting at £47,995 ($64,000) in the UK, on the road. That’s over £20,000 ($26,500) less than the plug-in Defender 110, which starts at £71,840 ($95,500) in the UK.

It has a seven-seat arrangement, which BYD said was specifically designed for the European and UK markets.

As the first vehicle in the UK based on its DM-p (Dual Mode performance) powertrain, BYD said the Ti 7 “vastly exceeds the closest competition,” seemingly another jab at the Defender.

"JLR believes BYD stripped down the Defender to reverse engineer some of its technology".

It has been revealed that reverse engineering isn't illegal. Patent infringement is illegal.

Competition strip down each other's product all the time. As long as they don't use the "exact" same technology, it isn't a copy right concern.

The setup uses three electric motors and a 1.5-liter turbocharged engine, delivering a combined 402 hp (408 PS), enabling it to accelerate from 0 to 62 mph in 4.8 seconds.

Sources indicate that the engine primarily powers a 35.6 kWh BYD Blade Battery, which provides a pure-electric WLTP driving range of up to 74 miles. In the city, it has an electric range of up to 102 miles.

Available exclusively in the UK in the flagship Excellence AWD trim, BYD claims that the Ti 7 offers “a level of equipment that exceeds anything that its rivals can offer at this price point.”.

We should learn more about the BYD and JLR legal battle soon. Check back for updates, as this story is still ongoing.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • “The fleet was designed around three-month tours, and that was considered to be a long time to be stuck underwater in a metal box with no contact with the outside world,” nuclear submarine expert David Cullen told The Guardian on November 15.
  • Industry observers note that the 17,526-ton, nearly 500-foot-long HMS Vengeance is one of Britain’s four Vanguard-class submarines constructed to carry monstrous Trident nuclear missiles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A nuclear submarine recently returned to Scotland after setting a Royal Navy record of 217 days underwater. The HMS Vengeance’s seven-month deployment overtook the 205-day milestone set by the HMS Vanguard in April. But with the Vengeance crew finally back home, critics now argue the two submarines’ lengthy back-to-back voyages are causes for concern, not celebration.

“The fleet was designed around three-month tours, and that was considered to be a long time to be stuck underwater in a metal box with no contact with the outside world,” nuclear submarine expert David Cullen told The Guardian on November 15.

Industry observers note that the 17,526-ton, nearly 500-foot-long HMS Vengeance is one of Britain’s four Vanguard-class submarines constructed to carry monstrous Trident nuclear missiles. First launched in 1998, the vessel features 16 missile tubes, each loaded with one Trident containing up to a dozen, 100-kiloton multiple independently targetable reentry vehicles (MIRVs). The MIRV is specifically engineered to simultaneously deploy a payload of individual nuclear weapons aimed at a list of targets. The Royal Navy continuously keeps at least one Vanguard submarine at sea, which hypothetically allows the United Kingdom to still conduct nuclear strikes in the event its land-based systems are compromised during a nuclear war.

In a recent development, vanguard submarines were originally built to host around 140 crewmembers during three-to-four month deployments. Although a 100-day excursion was once considered rare, underwater stints are now often double the length of time, forcing sailors to stack extra provisions along already cramped corridors and inside any additional nooks. The U.K. government attributes the extended missions to budgetary cuts that have dramatically slowed down the pace of multimillion-dollar vessel maintenance projects.

It has been revealed that deployment aboard a submarine like the Vengeance is considered one of the navy’s most psychologically difficult assignments. The nuclear sub remains underwater in total radio silence for the entire length of a patrol to keep its position secret. The vessel can travel to a depth of around 984 feet, but it may occasionally ascend to shallower waters to communicate via a transmission buoy or floating wire antenna. Crewmembers may receive a weekly, 120-word “Familygram” message, but each dispatch is previewed by naval officials. These readers retain the right to censor any bad news or information they feel may compromise sailors’ effectiveness. Regardless of what a sailor ultimately reads, they are strictly prohibited from responding.

Sources indicate that the toll on crew is steep, but it’s particularly difficult for the women comprising roughly 10-percent of the navy. In 2022, whistleblower Sophie Brook generated international headlines after reporting a “constant campaign of sexual bullying” while serving as one of the Royal Navy’s first female submariners. In 2024, First Sea Lord Adm. Sir Ben Key called the crew misogyny “intolerable” and apologized to the growing number of women who subsequently came forward with their own stories. The Royal Navy’s investigations ultimately resulted in the firing, demotion, and disciplining of dozens of servicemen—including Key’s own termination.

In a recent development, key’s successor, Gen. Sir Gwyn Jenkins, said he had “nothing but tremendous respect” for Trident crews earlier this month, while admitting the need to “improve our submarine maintenance.”.

The Vanguard fleet was designed for about 25 years of service, but will likely accumulate roughly four decades of sailing by the time its first replacement is ready. That submarine, the HMS Dreadnought, isn’t expected to sail until around 2032.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the Bronco Raptor takes the already highly capable Bronco platform and cranks up the intensity across the board: the twin-turbo 3.0-liter V-6 is good for 418 ponies, the beefed-up suspension features Fox adaptive dampers and a slightly wider track, and it rolls on standard 37-inch BFGoodrich K02 all-terrain tires. If that sounds like the ideal recipe for blasting through the desert, performing low-level aerial maneuvers, and breaking trails, well, that’s the point.

But arguably the most impressive thing about the Bronco Raptor is how well it settles down in less demanding situations—like your drive home from the off-road park. There’s room for five, it comes equipped with contemporary technology and infotainment, and it looks the business whether you’re in the urban jungle or the real one.

Expert Tip: The Bronco Raptor packs a lot of physical and visual punch, but at a cost. Savvy shoppers can build an impressively capable off-road beast on the bones of the base Bronco for thousands less by picking the right options.

The 2027 Bronco Raptor is largely unchanged; minor standard updates include ambient footwell lighting and a 5G modem.

Car and Driver calculates your car's value in three free and easy steps - using the same Black Book® data dealers use to appraise vehicles.

Ford didn't put a V-8 in the Bronco Raptor, but it did manage to coax 418 horsepower from the twin-turbo 3.0-liter V-6 under the hood. The engine pairs exclusively with a 10-speed automatic transmission and an advanced four-wheel-drive system that works in concert with selectable drive modes named with the clever acronym "G.O.A.T." (Goes Over Any Type of Terrain).

The Bronco Raptor has a beefier suspension setup than the standard SUV, with a wider track, Fox adaptive dampers from the F-150 Raptor, and standard 37-inch BFGoodrich K02 all-terrain tires—all of which endow it with better high-speed stability for fast desert running, high-jumping sand dunes, and powering through rough off-road trails.

During our test drive, we were impressed with the Bronco Raptor's off-road prowess, both when bounding over bumpy terrain at speed and while crawling through rocky passes with the low-range gearing engaged.

According to recent reports, in Comparison: While the Bronco Raptor’s twin-turbo 3.0-liter V-6 doesn't have the same shove as the F-150 Raptor's boosted 3.5-liter, it has enough punch to get the Bronco Raptor to 60 mph in 5.6 seconds. The F-150 Raptor hits the mark in 5.2 seconds.

In Comparison: The last Jeep Wrangler 392 we tested left the Bronco Raptor in the dust, hitting 60 mph in 4.0 seconds.

Recent findings suggest that in Comparison: The Raptor can tow more than the regular Bronco—which has a maximum tow rating of 3500 pounds—but it’s still no match for Jeep’s and Toyota’s 4x4s. A V-8 Wrangler can tug a 5,000-pound trailer behind its bumper, while the 4Runner is good for 6000 pounds.

In a recent development, the Ford Bronco Raptor earns EPA ratings of 15 mpg city, 16 mpg highway, and 15 mpg combined. On our 75-mph highway fuel-economy route, the Bronco Raptor surprised us by returning 17 mpg—one mpg more than expected. For more information about the Bronco Raptor's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.

In Comparison: Compared to the 470-hp 6.4-liter V-8 Jeep Wrangler 392, the Bronco Raptor has a marginal two-mpg advantage in city driving; both are EPA-rated for 16-mpg highway.

In a recent development, first Row: The extra-capable Raptor shares its purposeful interior design and its dimensions with the regular Bronco and comes standard with rubberized flooring, marine-grade vinyl upholstery, and a set of overhead auxiliary toggle switches. Those who want a more luxurious cabin can opt for leather-trimmed seats.

Recent findings suggest that second Row: The Bronco Raptor is a four-door-only proposition, and the second row offers more leg-, shoulder, and hip room than the two-door versions. Two adults will be perfectly happy sitting in the back of the Bronco Raptor, but even with the additional space, three would be a squeeze.

Cargo Capacity: The cargo hold is pretty sizable, with a claimed volume of 38.3 cubic feet behind the second row. It can fit all the SUV’s removable doors behind the back seats, but we recommend using the available protective bags to keep them safe, and they consume every inch of the cargo area when doing so.

Recent findings suggest that the Bronco Raptor has a 12.0-inch vertically oriented touchscreen, running Ford's latest Sync 4 software. The infotainment system supports wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto functions, too. A one-time purchase activates seven years of unlimited Wi-Fi hotspot service, connected navigation, audio and video streaming, Alexa voice assistant, and other entertainment options. There's a rack built into the top of its dashboard for mounting smartphones and GoPros, which can be plugged into nearby 12-volt outlets; there’s also a 120-volt household outlet.

The Bronco Raptor comes standard with lots of driver-assistance technology, from blind-spot monitoring to lane-keeping assist to adaptive cruise control.

For information about the Bronco Raptor’s crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.

Recent findings suggest that ford offers competitive limited and powertrain warranties. However, the manufacturer doesn’t provide complimentary scheduled maintenance, whereas Jeep does.

  • Cybercab pricing starts at $29,990, a price that includes the first month of the autonomy subscription required to operate the vehicle; every subsequent month, however, consumers will need to pay $299 for that subscription.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Elon Musk once promised the fully autonomous, steering-wheel- and pedal-free Tesla Cybercab would arrive before the year 2027, and start at less than $30,000. Prominent tech influencer Marques Brownlee promised back in 2024 to shave his head if Tesla delivered on that cost and timeline. It appears that the automaker, very technically, has done so, as Tesla unveiled on X on Friday evening that “select customers” can now purchase a Cybercab through an early-access, limited-release program.

Cybercab pricing starts at $29,990, a price that includes the first month of the autonomy subscription required to operate the vehicle; every subsequent month, however, consumers will need to pay $299 for that subscription. Customers can reserve a Cybercab with a non-refundable $1000 deposit. Deliveries in Austin, Texas will begin in December 2026.

It has been revealed that but, as the saying goes, there’s a catch. The first one here is that owners can only operate the Tesla Cybercab in areas where it has been approved for use. According to Tesla’s website, that currently includes major cities in two states: Austin, San Antonio, Dallas-Fort Worth, and Houston in Texas, and Tampa Bay, Orlando, and Miami in Florida. Tesla’s website lists Las Vegas, Phoenix, and Jacksonville as “coming soon.”.

In a recent development, another restriction is that Tesla is not selling the Cybercab to fleet operators—the most obvious customer—just yet. Customers in this initial batch may purchase one Cybercab, and only for personal use. However, Tesla does have an interest form that potential fleet operators can fill out on its website.

The Cybercab and autonomous driving in general represent potentially game-changing technology—a major reason automakers and major tech companies have invested heavily and worked on it for more than a decade. In theory, Tesla and third-party operators could offer incredibly low ride-sharing prices, with no driver who needs to be compensated with humane wages. Prices would be low enough not just to undercut rideshare providers such as Uber and Lyft, but potentially to undermine personal vehicle ownership itself.

In a recent development, but achieving that Tesla-driven utopia may be a far-off prospect. To change the game, the technology must work. As Jeremy Clarkson and others have noted, Tesla’s Cybercab ride-sharing service still has several kinks to work out. Broad regulatory approval remains a relatively distant prospect. And even if the technology works and meets safety standards, customers still have to buy in.

10 JRPGs Launching in 2027 You Should Keep on Your Radar

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The pandemic sure threw a wrench into many developers' looks, which was understandable.
  • Furthermore, JRPG fans have been well served since then.
  • In a recent development, terranigma brings back a classic from the SNES, a JRPG that formed part of the legendary Quintet Trilogy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The pandemic sure threw a wrench into many developers' looks, which was understandable. However, as soon as the situation began to normalize, many games that were delayed or suffered internal setbacks started getting revealed with official release dates. It feels like ever since 2023 we have been living through a run of great releases, with banger after banger.

Furthermore, JRPG fans have been well served since then. A fresh title keeps coming out, whether from indie developers, veterans who left their former companies to start their own studios, or fresh remasters and remakes popping up. I, for one, would love some peace and downtime to just play casually, and I thought 2027 would bring that relief, but I was mistaken. The year hasn't even begun, and my backlog is already clogging up again. Let us take a look at a few upcoming JRPGs in 2027 that you should definitely keep on your radar.

In a recent development, terranigma brings back a classic from the SNES, a JRPG that formed part of the legendary Quintet Trilogy. It functions more as a direct port than a full remaster, but it remains extremely welcome nonetheless. Terranigma never originally introduced in North America, only in Japan and Europe, meaning many players from back in the day never had the chance to experience this action RPG.

In a recent development, in Terranigma, we play as Ark on a mission to restore Earth. And by Earth, I mean our actual planet, as all the continents are based on real-world geography that we gradually bring back to life. To do this, Ark uses a real-time combat system driven by level-ups and spells you buy along the way. The most enjoyable aspect of Terranigma is witnessing the world-building sidequests unfold as you visit villages and restore them. It is a fantastic treat for anyone looking to revisit or experience a past JRPG gem through an official release.

Against all odds and to my utmost surprise, SaGa is becoming one of the longest-running and most sprawling series in the Square Enix catalog. I know it is unorthodox and not everyone enjoys its unconventional design, but I love seeing Square keeping the franchise alive, especially through its remakes. Following Romancing SaGa 2: Revenge of the Seven, Square Enix is delivering a full remake of the third entry titled Romancing SaGa 3: Destinies United.

The remake will include similar enhancements to Revenge of the Seven, such as a revamped turn-based system that heavily emphasizes targeting enemy elemental weaknesses, while retaining core SaGa staples like Glimmer mechanics and open-ended progression where players shape the narrative path. I don't know if it will be as brutally difficult as the original Romancing SaGa 3, which was notorious for softlocking players with its complex progression systems. Still, it will certainly be a feast for fans of the series.

Continuing with upcoming remakes, Atlus is bringing another project to the table: Persona 4 Revival. As the name implies, this is a ground-up remake of the fourth Persona entry, fully modernized with current-gen graphics, overhauled combat mechanics, a re-orchestrated soundtrack, latest social activities, extra story events, and expanded dungeon crawling elements inside the TV World.

The best part is being able to revisit what many consider the best Persona game (a statement that could honestly apply to almost any entry in the franchise). Returning to the town of Inaba, we play as the canonically named student Yu Narukami. While keeping up with his daily routine of school life, part-time jobs, and social simulation, he will also need to unravel the mysteries of the TV World alongside fan-favorite Teddie.

Atelier is one of the longest-running JRPG series, with a fanbase more dedicated than a football club. While the overall narrative remains anthological across the franchise, Atelier is organized into distinct subseries. Following the Secret subseries featuring Atelier Ryza, we have the Memories subseries, which kicked off with Atelier Yumia and now continues with Atelier Karia: The Night Kingdom & the Guide of Memories.

In a recent development, atelier Karia continues the adventure in Aladiss, this time venturing into the underground world of Noctrem. This entry puts players in control of Karia, an amnesiac alchemist. Combat builds upon the real-time foundation established in Yumia, with Karia introducing a strategic layer that lets players pause combat to execute command skills or parry incoming enemy attacks. I won't say playing Atelier Yumia beforehand is strictly mandatory, but if you want full context, it might be the ideal route.

It's no exaggeration to say that Eternal Anima is one of my most anticipated JRPGs of 2027. The game was unveiled during a Nintendo Direct, and while I initially fell in love with its charming pixel art, it first looked like just another solid indie release. That changed once I looked into the talent behind the project, including industry veterans like Kazushige Nojima, a legendary Final Fantasy writer, and director Katsuhisa Higuchi, who worked as a battle programmer on several Final Fantasy titles and directed Monster Hunter Stories 2.

Early previews for Eternal Anima are singing high praise, spotlighting its refreshing turn-based combat, its time-travel mechanics (a narrative trope I never get tired of), and how seamlessly both elements interlock. The story follows Wade alongside an eclectic party gathered from different timelines. Combat features a mechanic called Future Sight that previews enemy moves, showing who they blueprint to target and the exact damage output, which elevates tactical planning and should be a joy to experiment with. I will be sitting in the front row waiting for Eternal Anima.

Final Fantasy VII Revelation needs no introduction and stands as one of the world's most anticipated JRPGs of 2027. We can wait for The Game Awards to hand out the Most Anticipated Game trophy, and if Final Fantasy VII Revelation doesn't take it home, feel free to call me out in the comments. Serving as the conclusion to the Final Fantasy VII remake trilogy, it appears to have refined everything that made its predecessors spectacular, pushing combat, exploration, and player freedom to latest heights.

According to recent reports, narratively, it will conclude the main arc, though whether it introduces major plot twists remains to be seen. We do know the Weapons are present and look more imposing than ever. Combat introduces two new playable party members, Vincent and Cid, along with the new FITs system, which acts like a Job framework to give each character a broader tactical arsenal. As for traversal, with the Highwind at our disposal, Square Enix stated that world exploration is completely open, leaving route decisions entirely up to the player. Certain regions will have higher level thresholds, nudging players to tackle them later, but the overall scope looks immensely promising. Final Fantasy VII Revelation, the year is yours.

Sources indicate that we now shift to games targeted for 2027 that lack specific day-and-date release slots, which leaves them open to potential schedule shifts. That stated, if one developer rarely delays its titles, it is Nintendo. Because of that track record, when Nintendo revealed Xenoblade Genesis for 2027, I knew with confidence I would be playing it next year.

Industry observers note that xenoblade Genesis marks the latest chapter in the Xenoblade saga. Whether it functions as a direct narrative sequel to the Chronicles arc remains unconfirmed, but it continues under the direction of Monolith Soft and series creator Tetsuya Takahashi. The reveal trailer omitted gameplay, focusing instead on narrative cutscenes that showcased story beats and main characters. The artistic direction initially drew mixed reactions from some fans for leaning closer to Fire Emblem than traditional Xenoblade, but I personally loved every bit of it, including the medieval aesthetic.

Sources indicate that knowing Monolith Soft, Xenoblade Genesis will feature a colossal world, an overhauled battle system, unorthodox progression mechanics, and endless features that will sink hundreds of hours into this fresh universe. Did I mention Yoko Shimomura is composing the soundtrack? That alone means it's a fantastic time to enhancement my Spotify playlists.

In this latest JRPG, players take control of Asch and Finé as they set out to prevent a world-ending catastrophe known as the Lightfall. Rev. NOiR. is an action RPG, but it features a tactical time-stop mechanic similar to Final Fantasy VII Remake, letting you pause combat to glitch skill commands through a visually stylish menu. Deep gameplay details remain sparse for now, but as mentioned, I'm choosing to trust the project and will be ready on day one once Rev.Noir. locks in its official release date.

Recent findings suggest that here is another franchise that requires zero introduction. Pokémon Winds & Waves is being touted as the first truly high-fidelity graphical Pokémon title, which would certainly be a milestone achievement for Game Freak. Given its oceanic setting packed with islands and open seas, it has every tool required to expand the open-world framework of Pokémon Scarlet and Violet to unprecedented heights, complete with fresh traversal mechanics.

Recent findings suggest that no specifics have been revealed regarding the battle mechanics. However, it will likely preserve the turn-based structure of its mainline predecessor while leaving real-time action gameplay to the Legends spinoff series. For anyone jumping into Pokémon Winds & Waves, three traditional elemental starter companions await: the puppy Pombon, the gecko Gecqua, and the bean chick Browt. I will almost certainly end up picking Gecqua.

Recent findings suggest that I want to start by noting that, according to the developers and director Tetsuya Nomura himself, Kingdom Hearts IV will definitely launch in 2027 and won't face delays. Square Enix confirmed that internal development is progressing smoothly, setting up the long-awaited return of Sora's adventure in Quadratum, complete with fresh characters (along with returning faces for those who played the mobile entries) and a fresh selection of Disney worlds.

In a recent development, in terms of core design and gameplay structure, we can expect a polished take on the series' classic loop: Sora travels from world to world, adapts to local rules, meets regional protagonists, and aids them in their struggles. It is a charming formula, and I would not have it any other way. Officially, only the world of Coco has been formally revealed, though a leak stemming from Steam achievements unveiled several others. I won't share those details here to keep you safe from spoilers, but if you want to look them up, do so at your own risk.

#5185. Peeping woodcocks are evolutionary oddballs

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (519 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Popsci ↗ Open Full Page

Peeping woodcocks are evolutionary oddballs

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (519 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As far as birds go, the eight known species of woodcock (genus Scolopax) look like they specifically evolved to go viral on the internet.
  • Industry observers note that woodcocks are part of the larger sandpiper family, but unlike their migratory relatives, most only travel extremely short seasonal distances.
  • It has been revealed that “The distribution of woodcocks and snipes around the world is really unusual,” John Bates, the curator of birds at the Field Museum’s Negaunee Integrative Research Center in Chicago, mentioned in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As far as birds go, the eight known species of woodcock (genus Scolopax) look like they specifically evolved to go viral on the internet. You’ve probably seen at least a few videos of the birds on social media darting across beaches and being incredibly vocal. As if their small, squat bodies and comically long beaks weren’t enough, they also vocalize with distinctively cartoonish peeping tweets during their mating displays.

Industry observers note that woodcocks are part of the larger sandpiper family, but unlike their migratory relatives, most only travel extremely short seasonal distances. Six of the eight species are only found on specific islands, and some of them don’t even migrate at all. So how did these evolutionary oddballs even get their start—and stop migrating? To piece together their unique avian story, biologists analyzed the DNA of all eight woodcock species and 22 species of snipe.

It has been revealed that “The distribution of woodcocks and snipes around the world is really unusual,” John Bates, the curator of birds at the Field Museum’s Negaunee Integrative Research Center in Chicago, mentioned in a statement. “They’re not terribly aerodynamic, and yet they’ve clearly gotten around.”.

It has been revealed that bates and his colleagues published the results of their work today in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS). The years-long endeavor involved not only examining preserved woodcock specimens housed in the Field Museum, but a fossilized sandpiper previously excavated from a cave site in Haiti. The remains found on the island of Hispaniola are around 1,000 years old, but that is still extremely young in the grand history of shorebirds.

The earliest members of the sandpiper family began in the northern hemisphere before slowly migrating to islands along lower latitudes. Those birds subsequently migrated much shorter distances after settling in the warmer climates. However, they didn’t remain sedentary. Based on the DNA analysis detailed in their study, Bates and his team theorize that snipes from Africa eventually traveled across the Atlantic Ocean, then evolved into fresh species in South America. From there, more of the birds made their way over the Pacific Ocean to New Zealand.

Industry observers note that their examinations also cleared up a bit of confusion. Biologists initially believed the fossilized sandpiper from Haiti was a woodcock, but the most recent data now highlights that it’s a snipe.

In a recent development, “Snipes and woodcocks have been around for 20 to 25 million years,” Bates explained. “Over that time, as new species have evolved and moved around the world, their migratory patterns have changed, too.”.

These changes are likely to continue amid today’s dramatic climate shifts, but that may pose a problem for the beloved woodcocks.

“These are definitely birds that would be affected by changing habitats and changing climates,” remarked Bates. “Some of these woodcocks are found only in the mountain forests on islands between Asia and Australia, and if those forests get cut down, the birds are going to be gone too.”.

  • The upcoming version picks up a new front bumper, new hood, new side panels, new rear arches, and a new rear fascia.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It might sound a bit vapid to us in the hoi polloi, but even those who can afford super-rare, super-low-volume production supercars still want to stand out from their peers. As a result, plenty of design houses offer aftermarket body kits and tuning for supercars and super-SUVs, but more often than not, they look somewhat ... atrocious. Novitec, however, is firmly bucking that trend with a new subtle upgrade for the Ferrari 12Cilindri—and it leveraged a classic designer to help pull it off.

According to recent reports, that designer is Vittorio Strosek, a man who has played a role in classic reimaginings of cars from Lamborghini, Porsche, McLaren, Bugatti, and more. Now, he's collaborating with Novitec to put a fresh face on the 12Cilindri. The result is a car that looks noticeably different than the original, without losing much of what makes that Ferrari so desirable.

The upcoming version picks up a new front bumper, new hood, new side panels, new rear arches, and a new rear fascia. Sure, it's clearly still a 12Cilindri, but it's also clearly different when set side by side with the version that rolls out of the factory gates; the Novitec car ends up being 2.8 inches wider at the front and 5.1 inches wider at the rear. The hood outlet exposes the red intake manifolds, and the entire package allegedly reduces front lift and improves rear downforce. Novitec also added Vossen wheels measuring 21 inches up front and 22 inches in the back.

Let's break down a few of the finer details here. Perhaps most obviously, the black panel at the front of the car is long gone. Instead, the section matches the body color. Then, on the fenders, you'll find latest vents that help to evacuate air that could otherwise be trapped in the wheel wells. The deep V cutouts on the hood are gone, in favor of a singular intake in the middle.

Sources indicate that the side of the car is also dramatically different. There are vents and intakes at the front and rear, where the normal car has neither; then, at the very back, the rear window is gone in favor of louvers. The sections that are black in the normal car also end up with panels that match the body. (I’d say the ducktail spoiler looks good too.) Overall, it's a cohesive design that manages to stand out without being overtly gaudy. As aftermarket supercar body kits go, this is one of the better ones out there.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that modern driving games like Snowrunner or Gran Turismo harness massive computing power to accurately model the physics of piloting a vehicle at speed. Sometimes, however, you just want an overexcited announcer to shout “Awesome!” while you sail a Jeep Gladiator over a crest, misjudge the landing, and impact an immovable sandstone massif at 85 mph.

Such is the appeal of Moab Run, a latest retro-themed off-roading game from none other than Jeep itself. Playable on mobile or in a browser window, the game channels the best of 1990s-era 3-D games like Sega Rally or Offroad Challenge, infusing it with playable examples of the very real special-edition Wranglers Jeep has debuted over the past year or so.

See all results for new 2027 Jeep Wrangler for sale near 20147.

Sources indicate that at launch, you can play seven of these Wranglers, from the synthwave-look Rewind to the military cosplay Sarge, with the full dozen coming to future game expansions. There’s also at the moment just the one course set in Utah at present, but two other tracks will become playable in due course.

Controls are very basic: accelerate, brake, and steer, with an option to powerslide and build up boost for bigger jumps. Jeep includes a somewhat hilarious disclaimer up front: “Do not attempt to recreate these actions in real life,” because, again, 85 mph into sandstone is not so fun in the non-digital world.

As befits a tech giant that’s all about off-roading, the roads in Moab Run are basically just a guideline. You can switch between various overlapping routes, climb sandstone ridges to pick up collectible star points, or just ignore things completely and fly off the road into a canyon river. There are also hidden collectible ducks scattered across the map, because of course there are. It’s a Jeep Thing.

You can’t damage the Wranglers, you seemingly can’t get stuck, and if you purposely drive in the wrong direction, all that’ll happen is a large green arrow will appear to point to where you’re supposed to go. It’s basically a penalty-free way to blow off some steam, and the opposite of what technical real-world off-roading is like.

In a recent development, also, it’s free. If you fancy getting in a little Jeep Wranglin’ action during your coffee break, Moab Run will do the trick. Go hunt down those hidden ducks, and aim for the hangtime challenge award.

Dracoola is absolutely amazing. He can lifesteal by default from 1*, which is huge. He gets better with each star, obviously, but if you manage to get him to 5*, he is a beast. He's my absolute favourite.

Recent findings suggest that seraph is great for the increased chances of encountering Valkyrie at the start. She can be good when it comes to unlocking upcoming, higher-grade abilities, so it's no wonder she's an S-tier character (and also premium).

Sources indicate that I like Nyanja very much because of the increased Movement Speed. It has Swift Wind by default, which is nice when you want to keep yourself safe from enemy waves - it's also extremely fun to play.

In a recent development, among the gear, these are some of the best you can get. I strongly recommend going for the Griffin set if possible, since its effect is very good for most builds. The Griffin set is one of my favourites, and it grants additional stats based on the number of nearby enemies.

Recent findings suggest that the Decisiveness set revolves around Crit. It is good for most builds, just like the Griffin set.

The Dragon Knight set is not that impressive, even though it's of high quality. Its skill effects are nothing too amazing - it mainly focuses on explosions. In my opinion, you should aim for something a lot better, unless you want to make a build that fits the Dragon Knight set.

Industry observers note that you can try out whatever build you like - just remember to make a build that you will actually have fun with. I always love melee builds that have a lot of Lifesteal - hence why I like Dracoola so much. If you fancy something else, you can change it up a little.

There is no definite Archero 2 tier list when it comes to abilities here. Each player will pick whichever skills they like the most and try to make them work. Eventually, even if you have a million sprites and 100 orbs, if you aren't having fun, there is no point playing that build.

sonnen’s upcoming smart breakers help your home battery last longer

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that A home battery can do more during a blackout if it isn’t busy running nonessential, energy-hungry appliances.
  • The companies announced today that they’re integrating ADAPT Energy’s controls and Eaton AbleEdge smart breakers into the SOLRITE–sonnen virtual power plant (VPP).
  • The announcement doesn’t specify pricing, how many homes will receive it, or when existing customers can get it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A home battery can do more during a blackout if it isn’t busy running nonessential, energy-hungry appliances. sonnen and SOLRITE Energy are putting that same principle to work for the grid, adding smart breakers that can temporarily switch off selected household loads while batteries help meet electricity demand.

The companies announced today that they’re integrating ADAPT Energy’s controls and Eaton AbleEdge smart breakers into the SOLRITE–sonnen virtual power plant (VPP). The setup combines sonnenHub with breakers that manage power-hungry equipment, both during outages and when the grid needs help.

The announcement doesn’t specify pricing, how many homes will receive it, or when existing customers can get it.

In a recent development, A VPP connects home batteries into a network so they can work together as a larger energy resource. This addition gives SOLRITE another way to respond: in addition to controlling the batteries, it can reduce the amount of electricity that participating homes use.

Recent findings suggest that sonnen and SOLRITE used the example of a pool pump, as it’s energy-intensive, nonessential, and runs for longer periods. When an event begins, ADAPT temporarily switches off the pool pump while the sonnen battery sends electricity to the grid.

It has been revealed that with less battery power going toward the pump, more can flow to the grid. Across participating homes, that gives the VPP more flexibility than relying on battery dispatch alone.

Industry observers note that homeowners have to opt in to that grid participation, and ADAPT will switch off only pre-approved household loads. Joining the VPP program doesn’t give the operator blanket permission to turn off anything in the house.

“Instead of putting the pressure on homeowners to change the way their home is wired, and to manually manipulate loads during an outage, we’re putting intelligence into their energy system, which provides a seamless and automatic backup power experience for their home,” said Troy Morgan, president of PanTech Design, the developer of ADAPT Energy.

The breakers also tackle a practical problem with home backup: Significant appliances can drain a battery rapidly, and the surge of power some equipment needs to start can overload a backup system just as an outage begins.

It has been revealed that ADAPT coordinates the smart breakers with the sonnen battery to automatically switch off large loads during backup operation. When grid power returns, it restores them, so homeowners don’t have to go around resetting individual circuits.

It has been revealed that that also gives homeowners more flexibility later. According to the companies, changing which smart-breaker-controlled loads are switched off during an outage doesn’t require rewiring those circuits.

Industry observers note that the installation benefit matters, too. Some backup setups require electricians to move selected circuits into a separate panel. This system manages compatible circuits where their breakers already sit, which the companies say reduces installation complexity and inspection work.

Whole-home backup still has limits. Automatically managing large loads helps the available battery capacity go further; it doesn’t mean every appliance can run at once throughout an outage.

According to recent reports, SOLRITE finances, builds, and owns residential solar-plus-storage projects through what it calls Virtual Power Plant Agreements, with no upfront cost to homeowners. It indicates it operates in Texas, California, Connecticut, Massachusetts, and Illinois, with more markets planned.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that texas-based startup (and resurrector of an old name) REO Trucks unveiled its revamped and renewed mission and previewed its first vehicle this past summer, but as of Monday, the American startup has some trucks to show us. Or, at least some renderings of some vehicles, alongside some real illustrations by frankstephenson design.

In a recent development, all three vehicles REO intends to release are detailed and pictured here. The T4X is the work truck; the T4C is the crew cab pickup; and the S4C is a family SUV. All three ride on the same steel ladder frame, and are even identical in every way from the B-pillar forward. It’s beyond the B-pillar where each, naturally, differ based on their specific use cases.

Industry observers note that the T4X will be the first to go on sale (targeting late 2028) according to the brand, and it has a two-seat cab with a steel drop-side flatbed. Said bed measures 79.1 inches long and 70.6 inches wide. The tailgate has some neat features with integrated cup holders, recesses for phones or tablets, and bottle openers on either side.

The T4C crew cab trades some of the bed length for passenger space, as it seats up to five people. That noted, the bed is still fairly long, at 54.1 inches in length.

Meanwhile, the S4C seats six, and notably has a shorter rear overhang than the trucks to help with the departure angle for off-roading. The cargo area can be accessed via a side-hinged tailgate, and the rear glass even drops down into the door.

These are the unique body style features REO is detailing for now, but they all have much more in common than they do differences. For example, each REO vehicle will be equipped with a naturally aspirated four-cylinder engine that the company states is designed for longevity, drive-ability and towing more than outright performance. A six-speed manual transmission comes standard, while a six-speed automatic gearbox will be optional. Every REO is also fitted with part-time four-wheel drive, allowing you to select 2WD or 4WD High/Low via a floor-mounted lever. A locking rear differential will be optional for those who want it.

Industry observers note that expect a bumpy ride, because in addition to the body-on-frame construction, all REOs will have solid axles front and rear. Disc brakes will be fitted up front, but drums are used in the back. You’ll steer with hydraulic assistance, and 17-inch steel wheels will be wrapped by all-season tires. Should off-roading be in your future, a “Ransom Package” will be optional, adding off-road tires with unique off-road wheels, upgraded dampers/leaf springs, and a 2.5-inch suspension lift. (You’ll also get orange accents that designate it as the Ransom Package model.).

Industry observers note that photos of the interior aren’t available, but REO indicates physical controls will “take prominence.” Unlike the Slate Truck, power windows come standard, but the seats are manually adjustable. There will still be screens, though, as REO says it comes with a digital cluster and display for navigation and media.

It has been revealed that as of now, the T4X is slated to start at $21,500 and be sold in a direct-sales model (no dealers). The T4C is meant to starts at $25,000, and the S4C at $28,500. The firm says it aims to assemble all three in Texas. While the T4X is meant to reach buyers in late 2028, neither the crew cab pickup nor the SUV have predicted on-sale dates yet; if you want one, REO is taking refundable $25 deposits.

Selecting additional options can push the truck’s price past $120K.

See all results for new 2027 Tesla Cybertruck for sale near 43212.

As Not a Tesla App first pointed out, the Cyberbeast’s base price has risen by $10,000 since the start of the year, including $7500 since last week. Regardless of the price hikes, a $100,000 vehicle is still out of reach for most people, and that’s also likely the case for the now-discontinued Dual Motor AWD variant, which last started at nearly $85K with all the mandatory fees. Of course, even casual observers will agree that Tesla’s decision to trim the Cybertruck lineup to the single most expensive model is a way to maximize profits during the waning months of its life.

For those who can afford a latest Cyberbeast, its hefty price tag brings impressive acceleration numbers, with the last version we tested hitting 60 mph in just 2.6 seconds (matching Tesla’s claim). However, the 834-hp tri-motor electric truck didn’t meet its 320-mile range estimate, with its battery running out of juice after 250 miles in our 75-mph real-world highway test. Pro tip: Keeping the Cybertruck’s roll-top bed cover closed saved us 25 miles of range at sustained highway speeds.

These are a few of the things we’ll have to remember it by. And if you’re feeling bummed that you can’t afford the last batch of upcoming Cybertrucks, just remember that there are pre-owned models aplenty.

According to recent reports, eric Stafford’s automobile addiction began before he could walk, and it has fueled his passion to write news, reviews, and more for Car and Driver since 2016. His aspiration growing up was to become a millionaire with a Jay Leno–like car collection. Apparently, getting rich is harder than social-media influencers make it seem, so he avoided financial success entirely to become an automotive journalist and drive upcoming cars for a living. After earning a journalism degree at Central Michigan University and working at a daily newspaper, the years of basically burning money on failed project cars and lemon-flavored jalopies finally paid off when Car and Driver hired him. His garage currently includes a 2010 Acura RDX, a manual '97 Chevy Camaro Z/28, and a '90 Honda CRX Si.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Engwe has impressed us repeatedly with its value e-bikes at lower-than-believable prices.
  • The Engwe M20 3.0 is a specs monster and blows away the original version of the bike released in 2023:.
  • At just over 100lbs, it is a bit hard to move around, but once assembled, it feels like a pretty impressive piece of machinery.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Engwe has impressed us repeatedly with its value e-bikes at lower-than-believable prices. But lately, the brand is climbing the value chain with impressive e-bikes that aren’t just great value but also pack strong specs and impressive features. The Engwe M20 3.0 is a great example….

The Engwe M20 3.0 is a specs monster and blows away the original version of the bike released in 2023:.

The M20 is fairly easy to assemble. At just over 100lbs, it is a bit hard to move around, but once assembled, it feels like a pretty impressive piece of machinery. I love the street tires on here instead of pretending to be an off-roader. Dual bright headlights and brake light with turn signals really give this thing some street cred. Adding to the safety roster, Engwe upgraded the quad-piston brakes with sporty red calipers and 202 mm rotors. This is not a value bike. The rear suspension is tight, which is great for 2 riders but might feel stiff out of the box for light riders. The seat is *chef’s kiss* even for 2 riders. Very soft and comfortable but not too soft. It even has a little ‘gas tank’ storage area aft the seat, which is keyed and enough to hold a few sandwiches, some riding gloves, or a small purse.

Recent findings suggest that one gripe: There are 3 sets of keys on here, the aforementioned storage area and one set each for each battery. We’d love to see these things keyed together.

The bike/moped/moto came with a huge 1.2 kW battery (or 2 in our case – unless you have a 80-mile commute, 1 should be plenty) that must be charged individually. But with a 60V 8A charger, each one only takes about 2-3 hours to charge, which is impressive.

I did not expect to like the ride of this thing as much as I did. We can dispense with the pleasantries here; it came set to Class 2 mode with a 20mph top speed and stickers to match; a quick Google search will show you how to open this up to 40mph open mode. I take responsibility for my own actions.

The first thing you’ll notice here is that the motor is whisper-quiet, and with the street tires, there is very little road noise, even at 35mph. The half throttle is plenty responsive, a lot more so than the cadence sensor on the pedals, which are vestigial at best here. Those massive brakes are a bit softer than I’d prefer, but given a good squeeze, those 203mm rotors and quad-piston hydraulic brakes are going to stop you, the 100lb bike, and your passenger/cargo fairly quickly.

My girlfriend and I got pulled over for the first time in my e-biking life as I was picking her up at the coffee shop. The cop was immediately apologetic because “he thought we were kids” and not the 50-year-olds under the helmets he encountered. Then he noticed the pedals and said that we’re all clear and that what we were on looked like a motorcycle and that a couple of e-moto kids had gotten into accidents recently, one hit by a drunk driver and who is still in a coma. While he was already letting us go, I pointed out the Class 2 sticker on the bike, and he gave me the thumbs-up as we sped off at 30mph. This M20 passed the local police test with flying colors. I can’t guarantee you’ll have the same experience in your jurisdiction.

Sources indicate that most of my gripes on this e-bike are inherent to the form factor. It is heavy at over 100 lbs, but you’d expect that with a 3.3kW motor, 2.4kW of batteries, and room for two. That noted, don’t buy this bike if you need to take it up stairs or plan to pedal it without assist. In fact, this isn’t a bikepath bike or a put it on the back of your car bike. And, don’t buy this bike if you like to pedal. It’s too major and fast. This is a 35 mph roads bike. Also 3 sets of keys?

I did not expect to love this bike as much as I have. It is the perfect train station bike for me, and as a bonus, it is a great way to take my girlfriend to the coffee shop on the weekends. It has fat tires, great suspension, a cushy seat, and strong, smooth acceleration and confidence-inspiring braking. It looks cool enough for the cops to think I’m a kid picking up his girlfriend, and it has so much range that I probably won’t need to charge it monthly. At $1399-$1699 (10% off) depending on battery config, this is less than half the price of some of the pricier and admittedly more stylish Super73 options out there.

It has been revealed that I understand that some will fault Engwe for selling a 3.3kW motor e-bike as a class 2 e-bike. But I genuinely feel safer on the road, being able to go at the 35mph speed that cars are going rather than forcing them to go around me. Plus, it isn’t like every single car on the road goes over the speed limit. So why not bikes too?

The Engwe M20 3.0 is over the limit but in all of the best possible ways.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that there’s been a lot of anticipation for Battlefield 6’s version 1.1.3.0 patch. The patch kicks off the third and final phase of the game’s first season, adding some latest holiday-themed content. More the new content itself, the update’s biggest additions are almost entirely gameplay-related.

Unfortunately, for as much as the changes in 1.1.3.0 have been well received, the launch has been marred by a series of technical issues, some of which are a little unusual.

In a recent development, immediately after patch 1.1.3.0 went live, players on PC started reporting massive stutters that would occur every few seconds. The glitch is especially pronounced in Redsec Battle Royale, but much deadlier in traditional multiplayer.

According to recent reports, battlefield Studios rapidly acknowledged it, pointing out a workaround that appears to be working for players on Steam. According to those players, going offline on Steam’s friends menu has fixed stuttering for them.

The problem remains for other players on PC, however, and the developer said it’s working on a proper fix.

In a recent development, perhaps the most disrupting problem the patch has caused is one that prevents players from being able to interact with the game’s menu. Tiles become unresponsive, or outright unselectable when you try to hover near them.

According to recent reports, ironically, the top set of tiles designed to make it easy for players to swiftly jump into the new content has been the most affected. Restarting the game sometimes fixes the glitch, and some players report that it only happens upon first launch after installing the update.

Recent findings suggest that but Battlefield Studios later clarified that, unsurprisingly, there’s an actual reason behind the bug. Once again, a fix is being investigated, and the developer will offer an update once some progress has been made.

A little further down the list of importance is an issue that stops players from being able to skip tiers within the fresh Winter Offensive bonus path in the game’s battle pass. BF Studios took out the feature entirely while it works on a fix, so while you can continue making progress in the bonus path, you won’t be able to skip tiers.

This is all a shame to see. Outside of all the problems, the meat of the upcoming update has been almost universally praised. The visibility improvements, and netcode updates have been celebrated. Many players were also happy to see meaningful updates to footstep audio and overall clarity.

It’s also unusual for a Battlefield 6 patch to run into so many challenges at launch. The sentiment around 1.1.3.0 so far is that it’s the game’s best and worst update yet. Hopefully those issues will be fixed before the development team breaks for the holidays.

#5173. Latest Update: Pearley: How the Saab 99 Turbo Changed the World

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1186 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Roadandtrack ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Pearley: How the Saab 99 Turbo Changed the World

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1186 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Roadandtrack

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It didn’t seem so at the time, but 1977 would prove to be among the most key years in automotive history.
  • Yeah, Saab isn’t around today; there were turbocharged cars built before it; and the 99 never sold in overwhelming numbers (at least not here in America).
  • Recent findings suggest that the 99 was already ancient by 1977.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It didn’t seem so at the time, but 1977 would prove to be among the most key years in automotive history. Commercially, this was the model year when General Motors “downsized” its full-size cars from gargantuan to merely huge. Their immense sales success meant the era of land dreadnoughts was over. It was the first model year for the BMW 3-Series name in America and the first for the Porsche 924, that tech giant’s first front-engine car. In Formula One, Colin Chapman introduced ground effects aerodynamics to the series with the revolutionary Lotus 78. Culturally, 1977 was the year of Smokey and the Bandit, which continues to define what a silly car chase movie must be. But quite sneakily, with 50 years of hindsight, the most important development of 1977 was the introduction of the Saab 99 Turbo.

Yeah, Saab isn’t around today; there were turbocharged cars built before it; and the 99 never sold in overwhelming numbers (at least not here in America). But almost every car for sale today derives at least some of its essence from that eccentric Swedish front-driver. “Saab’s use of a turbocharger differs considerably from that of other car makers, such as Porsche,” reported John Lamm in Road & Track’s October 1977 road test. “[I]n that Saab’s goal is maximum torque at mid-range engine speeds rather than dramatic boost at high output.”.

Recent findings suggest that the 99 was already ancient by 1977. Originally shown in 1967 as Saab’s first stretch beyond dinky cars with weird two-stroke engines, it went into production in 1968 as a 1969 model and was, by Saab’s standards, a hit. But it was still weird—wraparound windshield, odd ducky styling, and yeah, the ignition key was down behind the shifter—and at a time when front-wheel drive was rare, it was front-drive.

Saab’s buyers had a certain academic and liberal edge, too. According to researchers at the University of Connecticut and reported by Time magazine in 1976, a staggering 98 percent of Saab owners voted for Democratic candidate George McGovern over Republican incumbent Richard Nixon in the 1972 presidential election. In that election, Nixon carried 60.7 percent of the vote, and won 49 of the 50 states. Saab owners weren’t like everyone else.

Sources indicate that the 99’s “Slant-4” four-cylinder engine was based on the V-8 installed in the British Triumph Stag. By 1972, Saab had taken over production of the engine itself, and had modified the design to be robust and reliable, but there was nothing exotic about what Saab now called the B engine. It had an iron block and a single overhead cam aluminum head. Simple stuff. And in the 1976 99 EMS, the sportiest model in the line, the 2.0-liter eight-valve engine was rated at 115 horsepower channeled through a four-speed manual transmission.

Sources indicate that saab didn’t have the resources to develop a new engine, but it had plenty of turbocharging experience with its Scania large truck division. “The immediate problem,” explained R&T’s Thos. L. Bryant after driving the new 99 Turbo in Sweden for the December 1976 concern, “was to get low-speed torque for the drivability while at the same time limiting high engine speed power for durability.” To achieve that goal, Saab used small turbochargers and advanced electronic engine controls.

Saab already used Bosch K-Jetronic fuel injection on the B engine, and while it wasn’t a wholly electronic system, it was good at advanced fuel metering. And it was the same system Porsche used on the 911 Turbo. Also, Saab developed its own electronic Automatic Performance Control (APC) that used a knock sensor in the block and pressure sensors in the intake manifold to trigger a wastegate and limit turbo boost when the engine couldn’t take any more.

Sources indicate that saab didn’t hide the small, quick-spooling Garrett T3 turbocharger in the 99, putting it forward of the engine. And what was downstream of it was nearly as important. Saab breakthrough emissions tech, known as “Lambda,” ensured that performance could be compatible with stricter emissions controls and catalytic converters. “Basically, Lambda is a 3-component catalyst designed to handle NOx as well as CO and HC,” explained Bryant. “The normal catalytic converter takes care of the last two pollutants fairly well, but NOx usually requires lower compression ratios and exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) to keep it from being passed out through the tailpipe.”.

Lambda added three pieces alongside the fuel injection system: There was an oxygen sensor to monitor air-fuel mixture; an electronic control system that tweaked the air-fuel mixture to keep it close to the ideal stoichiometric value; and a switch on the throttle housing to override the metering system under full-load conditions. It was effective enough so that the engine could meet California’s 1977 emissions without using an Exhaust Gas Recirculation (EGR) valve.

Altogether, those elements and many subtler tweaks meant the 99 Turbo had 135 horsepower aboard. Not a lot by 2026 standards, but a sweet chunk back then. “In all of our discussions about the Saab Turbo,” R&T reported in the October 1977 test, “the one comment that continually surfaced was. ‘It’s so much fun to drive!’ Obviously, with a net horsepower rating up 20 hp to 135 at 5000 rpm (net torque is 160 at 3500 rpm versus 123 lb-ft for the non-turbocharged Saab and that is the more revealing improvement), the Saab Turbo is not going to give the breathtaking acceleration of a Porsche Turbo Carrera, but the performance increase is substantial and worthwhile.” R&T measured the 99 Turbo waltzing to 60 mph in 9.5 seconds, and running the quarter-mile in 17.5 seconds at 80.5 mph. In the context of the time, a solid performance.

The 99 Turbo wasn’t perfect, but showcased how effective turbocharging and electronic engine controls could be. At the same moment GM was using dumb carburetors on its new 1977 turbocharged Buick V-6, Saab was showing how it could be done. Buick would eventually adopt fuel injection and better electronic engine controls to allow its blown V-6 to mature into a legend with the Grand National and GNX. But Saab was there first.Saab died a sad death after some corporate conniptions. But look around at the turbocharged engines that dominate today. All those engines, powering everything from the Honda Civic Type R to the Kia Telluride, are descendants of the Saab 99 Turbo, which went on sale 50 years ago. As one anonymous staff member noted in that first road test, “This to me is one of the waves of the future: small engine with turbocharger for fuel economy and performance coupled with low exhaust emissions. Neat!”.

Sources indicate that john Pearley Huffman has been writing about cars since 1990 and is getting okay at it. Besides Road & Track, his work has appeared in Car and Driver, the Latest York Times, and more than 100 automotive publications and websites. A graduate of UC Santa Barbara, he still lives near that campus with his wife and two children. He owns a pair of Toyota Tundras and two dogs. He used to have a Nova and a Camaro.
