Latest Update: 10 Deltarune Moments That Feel Totally Different When You Replay Earlier Chapters

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1507 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that deltarune is a game that thrives not only on its narrative, but also on the individual mysteries set up by every cliffhanger and loose thread.
  • Thanks to fantastic use of irony and follow-through, some of the smallest moments in Deltarune’s earlier chapters have been completely recontextualized, and we’ll be talking about the wildest here.
  • Sources indicate that as we wait for chapter 6, it’s vital to lay out everything we know and everything that’s become clearer since the game’s initial demo release.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that deltarune is a game that thrives not only on its narrative, but also on the individual mysteries set up by every cliffhanger and loose thread. As in any good story, major revelations have not only affected fans’ expectations for the future, but also their understanding of earlier events.

Thanks to fantastic use of irony and follow-through, some of the smallest moments in Deltarune’s earlier chapters have been completely recontextualized, and we’ll be talking about the wildest here.

Sources indicate that as we wait for chapter 6, it’s vital to lay out everything we know and everything that’s become clearer since the game’s initial demo release. They say hindsight is 20/20, so let’s see how it serves us going forward.

Recent findings suggest that ralsei’s recitation of the Prophecy is one of the first major setup moments in Deltarune, both as a fairly cliché story setup and a direct threat for the party to fight back against later. Since chapter 4, the Prophecy’s legitimacy and exact wording have been under heavy scrutiny.

Knowing that Ralsei knows everything destined to happen down to the minute details makes his narration and people-pleasing more unsettling than charming. Susie’s heavy relevance to the darkest parts of its story sets her romantic yearning for Noelle up as a major red flag, ripe for getting ripped down by the grimmer chapters to come.

It has been revealed that susie’s portion of the Prophecy is vague enough that it might not even be about her, whether that’s through a misstep by Ralsei or deliberate sabotage from an outside force. The Prophecy itself is far from set in stone, ironically, and subverting it is already becoming a major objective of the party.

Throughout King’s fight at the tail end of the chapter, he spends most of his dialogue praising the Roaring Knight, assigning all his work and progress to their support. This was the very first mention we got of the Knight, and at the time most assumed they were some kind of fixture of the card kingdom.

We’ve gathered much more info on the Roaring Knight since, but King’s speech is the only case we have of them actually interacting with someone without hostility.

According to recent reports, in every other appearance, they’ve been a snarling aggressor with cruel laughter as their only method of communication. Hearing that they not only aligned with King but inspired him does a lot for their threat, establishing them as more than just a beast.

The weird route was already unsettling enough when it dropped during Deltarune’s second chapter, adding a touch of that No Mercy dread Undertale was infamous for. Despite this, the route felt rather self-contained until chapter 4 gave players a chance to lock it in.

Now that chapter 5 has arrived and given us a massive follow-through, playing through chapter 2’s Weird Route feels even worse. Knowing how far it goes and seeing exactly what goes on to shatter Noelle’s psyche make the metanarrative pain hit all the harder.

Recent findings suggest that spamton’s Shadow Crystal fight is a massive tonal shift from the rest of the chapter on the main route, especially at the very end. The battle takes a lot of notes from Undertale’s Mettaton battles, with Spamton straight up taking on a form extremely similar to Mettaton NEO.

The actual text of the battle is all about Spamton trying to transcend his limits, which all sounds very familiar to anyone who has seen chapter 5’s Weird Route dialogue. Combined with the constant discussion of Heaven and his angelic design, Spamton’s fight feels very different from what we originally thought.

According to recent reports, angels specifically are feeling more and more relevant the longer the game goes, both to symbolize the player and the larger figures controlling the Prophecy. For a goofy salesman, Spamton feels far more relevant than ever expected.

Industry observers note that the Shelter, the massive bunker at the southernmost tip of Hometown’s map, has been mysterious since Deltarune’s very first chapter, with each release slowly giving us more and more details about it. Over time, we’ve learned plenty. It is likely the site of whatever terrible accident happened to Dess; multiple members of the town are acting to keep it sealed, and most recently, Kris has access to it.

It has been revealed that thanks to these facts, it is largely assumed to be some kind of central base for the Knight and whoever is assisting it in the Light World. This makes Kris’s access to it when they break our control all the more interesting. Kris is clearly willing to do something drastic, including working with those who directly oppose the party.

After the most recent reveal of the strange flower seeds Kris pocketed and likely took back to the bunker, it feels like we’re watching them teetering over a ledge with no way to help. If they’d even let us.

Recent findings suggest that tenna is a massive source of comedy in chapter 3, but he’s also the source of a very off-putting little tantrum towards the tail end of the chapter, right before his boss fight. In it, he laments not only the state of the Dreemurr family but specifically Kris, pointing out just how differently they’ve been acting over the course of the night.

According to recent reports, we know that the source of this difference is the player’s interference, but that dichotomy is a major stress point, both for Kris and the player. Who knows what Kris really acts like and whether or not close friends like Susie, who met them after the swap, will actually care about them?

On our end, we really don’t know what Kris is capable of or what they’re willing to do when the chips are down, and it adds a layer of dread to the entire scene.

After all the buildup and vague hints towards the Knight, their sudden reveal in chapter 3 was a massive surprise, and the small amount of characterization we’ve gotten for them has painted a picture of their true motives.

Recent findings suggest that most interestingly, the scene that plays when you beat the Knight, where they seemingly knight Kris, has been given extra weight by how clearly Kris is standing in their corner. After fighting off the Flowers and pocketing the highly toxic seeds at the tail end of chapter 5, Kris is willing to go above and beyond, even considering harming themselves to align with the Knight’s goal.

This is a horrifying setup for what chapters 6 and 7 could bring, especially with 5 being marketed as “one last happy adventure.”.

Working your way through Noelle’s house at the start of chapter 4 was a great peek into her psyche after not getting much for her in chapter 3, while also allowing us to put together a bit more info on Dess Holiday herself.

Not only did we get plenty of extra scenes between Susie and Noelle, but we also got some more direct moments to see how exactly Kris acts without the Soul piloting them, making it clear that they can survive without it, at least for limited periods.

Most importantly, finally meeting Hometown’s mayor, Carol Holiday, added a tension that immediately made her a candidate for the Knight to many players. I won’t say I fully buy that theory, but she is officially on the table as an incredibly potent threat, alluding to both knowledge of and cooperation with Kris’s goal.

Industry observers note that chapter 4’s dark world was shockingly somber at times, setting a future tone while finalizing quite a few rules for how light world monsters and Darkners can overlap. Namely, through Gerson’s inclusion, we learned that dead Darkners, at least monsters, can manifest in Dark Worlds if items with their dust are within a fountain’s range.

This opens the door for any missing or dead characters to potentially show up in the future, or for items connected deeply to certain characters to manifest either as them or similarly to them. I fully believe this is how we’ll get some extra context on Rudy after his “falling down” early in chapter 5, and that it will lead to massive drama going forward.

From the earliest launch of Deltarune, fans have assumed the strange voice that speaks to us during the character creator was Gaster, based on the speech pattern that it uses and the dialogue from the Deltarune Twitter.

Following his extra dialogue in chapters 3 and 4, I grew extremely confident in that theory, and facts from both the normal and Weird Routes of chapter 5 have fully convinced me that we will meet the Man Who Speaks in Hands before Deltarune is through. Given what happens to Onionsan via one of Gaster’s Goners and his clear significance in the “B-Side” cutscene in the Weird Route, he is by far our biggest mystery and one that fully recontextualizes every bit of dialogue we get from him.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Perhaps more key than the patch itself, however, is the announcement the developer made around it.
  • Sources indicate that starting off with patch 1.6.0, it takes out a particular zipline on Stella Montis, the game’s most recent addition ot the map roster.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the time has arrived for another Arc Raiders revision, and Embark has certainly delivered. Today’s patch, version 1.6.0, is among the smallest the game has received so far, focusing almost exclusively on disabling map exploits.

Perhaps more key than the patch itself, however, is the announcement the developer made around it.

Sources indicate that starting off with patch 1.6.0, it takes out a particular zipline on Stella Montis, the game’s most recent addition ot the map roster. Some players used said zipline to get out of bounds, something the game has been battling on several of its maps.

Industry observers note that on Blue Gate, the patch fixes a collision glitch that allowed players to vault through a wall, and fall to their death. The map fixes continue with another on Spaceport Launch Tower, which takes out a gap in collision that players have been able to shoot through.

It has been revealed that the last change in this update affects gameplay feel around Arc enemies. Certain materials in the game’s world weren’t blocking their vision - or fire - when they should have, and this has now been fixed.

Alongside today’s patch, Embark also confirmed that going forward, we’re going to see fewer patches for Arc Raiders. The game has been getting updates almost every Thursday since it debuted in late October.

Now that most of the major problems have been fixed, the studio is shifting to a slower patching cadence. Critical fixes will still be issued as soon as they’re developed, but don’t expect a patch each week going forward.

Embark also revealed that patch releases and in-game store rotations will now occur on Tuesdays. You should also expect the next few weeks to be quiet, as members of the team go on holiday breaks.

According to recent reports, but, before everyone goes away, the game is going to get one more significant update. The last item on Arc Raiders’ roadmap, revealed in early November, is the Cold Snap event. This is on track for Tuesday, bringing some new content alongside a few other fixes.

Apple CarPlay Just Got A Big AI Upgrade Thanks To Google

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Something that would have been unimaginable five years ago is now reality.
  • Starting today, Gemini people on iOS devices can open the app on CarPlay and pick up where they left off on their smartphone.
  • Sources indicate that according to Google, Gemini on CarPlay was designed to work like a conversational driving companion that minimizes distraction.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Something that would have been unimaginable five years ago is now reality. Google’s Gemini AI voice assistant can now be used on Apple CarPlay by iPhone owners, breaking some of the barriers that have traditionally been in place between the two tech giants.

Starting today, Gemini people on iOS devices can open the app on CarPlay and pick up where they left off on their smartphone. The AI-powered chatbot can take multi-point questions and offer natural-sounding answers. It can also browse through the user’s emails and other productivity apps to come up with relevant answers—if the user has enabled the necessary permissions.

Sources indicate that according to Google, Gemini on CarPlay was designed to work like a conversational driving companion that minimizes distraction. To start Gemini, the driver has to press the app icon on the car screen’s app drawer or side rail—it doesn’t wake up via voice commands. That mentioned, after it’s front and center, Gemini can talk back and forth at the driver’s pace, even if it’s interrupted while it’s answering a question.

The American tech tech giant noted in an official blog post that Gemini on CarPlay can help the driver get ready for the day ahead. They can ask what’s on their calendar, when they need to leave for their next appointment, or talk through what they want to say before they arrive at a meeting.

In a recent development, an inbox recap is also possible, as Gemini can connect to Google Workspace apps like Gmail and Google Calendar. Exploring local spots and landmarks while driving is also part of the chatbot’s feature list. All conversations on CarPlay are automatically synced to the Gemini app on the iPhone, so the driver can recap chats after they park.

Recent findings suggest that gemini on Apple CarPlay is rolling out globally to all Gemini consumers on iOS now. All supported Gemini Live languages are included. To get Gemini to pop up on CarPlay, the latest version of the app needs to be installed on the iPhone, microphone permissions need to be enabled, and Gemini Live needs to have been used at least once on the phone. If all of these prerequisites are met, the next time the iPhone is connected to CarPlay, the Gemini app will appear on the display, ready for a upcoming conversation or to pick up an old one.

It has been revealed that the Gemini app’s CarPlay integration is just the latest move from Google to flood iPhones with its AI-enabled chatbot. Last month, the Alphabet-owned tech company embedded Gemini into the CarPlay mode of its Maps GPS navigation app.

Breaking: Tested: The 2026 Lexus ES Hybrid Evolves, but It Has a Familiar Feel

📅 27 May 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1423 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Caranddriver

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • 11/12/26 ENHANCEMENT: This review has been updated with instrumented test results.
  • In a recent development, although Lexus is no stranger to sporty models, this luxury brand made its name on quiet, plush sedans that prioritize refinement above all else.
  • In a recent development, on the surface, that appears to change with the new eighth-generation Lexus ES.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

11/12/26 ENHANCEMENT: This review has been updated with instrumented test results.

In a recent development, although Lexus is no stranger to sporty models, this luxury brand made its name on quiet, plush sedans that prioritize refinement above all else. And the ES is the one that has persisted. This comfy cruiser was the bestselling Lexus for many years, and it continues to attract a loyal set of buyers. Understandably, Lexus has been reluctant to change the ES formula much throughout its seven generations thus far.

In a recent development, on the surface, that appears to change with the new eighth-generation Lexus ES. Not only does the ES look quite different inside and out for 2026, but it also offers an electric powertrain for the first time. The ES hybrid continues, however, and after driving the latest version, it’s clear that this sedan's core mission hasn't changed as much as you might think.

In a recent development, lexus first offered the ES as a hybrid for 2013, and the previous-generation gas-electric model made up around 40 percent of ES sales last year. Given that take rate, it makes sense that the old nonhybrid V-6 has been axed. The electric ES, which we review separately, is a significant departure for this model line, but Lexus expects the hybrid to make up 80 percent of ES sales in the U.S. So, for now at least, the EV will be a niche product, and the gas-electric model will be the volume seller.

See all results for fresh 2026 Lexus ES for sale near 07055.

With a longer wheelbase, a significantly taller profile, and a more imposing shape, the latest ES stretches to the larger end of the mid-size luxury-sedan segment. Lexus engineers say they tried to “eliminate the negatives” of the sedan shape with this model, such as the more difficult ingress and egress of a lower seating height. In other words, it follows the tall-sedan format of the Toyota Crown but attempts to disguise its stature with more angular styling and a swoopy roofline that tapers toward the short trunk lid. There are some awkward angles, but overall, the design works and is still recognizable as a Lexus.

According to recent reports, the ES hybrid gets the latest Toyota hybrid powertrain, which the company refers to as the sixth-generation setup. It has a different power unit and transmission than before, and it’s configured to prioritize the electric motors for propulsion more. The 2.5-liter gasoline four-cylinder engine doesn’t change much, but total combined output of 244 horsepower is up from the previous ES300h’s 215 horses. That’s apparently enough for Lexus to bump the badge up to ES350h. All-wheel drive is optional on the hybrid ES for the first time, courtesy of an additional electric motor on the rear axle, though it doesn’t change output figures compared with the front-wheel-drive configuration.

The all-wheel-drive ES350h we tested got to 60 mph in 6.6 seconds, which is a significant improvement over the previous, front-wheel-drive ES300h F Sport’s 7.9-second run. That’s despite a significant weight gain, as our test car tipped the scales at 4145 pounds, 352 more than the 2023 ES300h we last tested.

See all results for upcoming 2026 Lexus ES for sale near 07055.

While this four-cylinder powertrain isn’t quite as smooth or sonorous as the old nonhybrid ES350’s V-6, the upgraded gas-electric setup is appreciably more refined than the old hybrid was. The gas engine is well isolated from the cabin and only makes itself known under hard acceleration; the hushed 67 decibels and 21 sones of noise we recorded inside at 70 mph is perfectly acceptable here. The electric motors go about their business seamlessly, with imperceptible switching between gas and electric power, and while the embiggened ES doesn’t quite feel eager, it accelerates with sufficient gusto and generally is responsive to throttle inputs. EPA ratings sit at 46 mpg combined with front-wheel drive and 44 mpg with all-wheel drive—strong numbers for this large of a sedan. We averaged 37 mpg overall, and the ES matched its 42-mpg EPA highway estimate in our 75-mph real-world fuel-economy test. But that’s not quite as good as the previous model, a 2019 ES300h which managed 45 mpg in the same test.

Sources indicate that importantly, the ride quality is fantastic. The suspension is tuned to be soft, as you’d expect for a boulevardier like this, but we appreciate the nicely controlled body motions. And the all-season tires have plenty of sidewall for soaking up potholes and rough sections of road (relatively small 19-inch wheels are the only choice on the hybrid model for now). This isn’t a vehicle for hard cornering, and the eco-conscious rubber doesn’t provide much grip when you push it around corners, but the steering wheel feels good in your hands and provides satisfactory on-center feel and natural effort buildup. We recorded a ho-hum 0.84 g of grip around our skidpad and a 170-foot stop from 70 mph.

Recent findings suggest that upon first glance at the cabin, you might worry that Lexus has too eagerly adopted the button-free, touch-capacitive interiors that are becoming too commonplace. And while there are definitely fewer buttons and knobs than before, and more controls integrated into the large 14.0-inch touchscreen, Lexus has done a good job balancing function with form. There’s still a volume knob, for instance, and although most climate functions are now on a lower part of the screen, there are a few crucial tactile buttons for adjusting the temperature and turning on the defrosters. The steering-wheel controls look like they’re touch-sensitive, but they’re thankfully tactile too. And the secondary functions such as mirror controls, seat adjustments, and windows are all still conventional and intuitive.

The material finishes and build quality live up to Lexus’s high standard. But it is worth noting that the hybrid comes in Premium and Premium+ trims, which means it doesn’t offer some of the most high-end features and accoutrements of the electric model’s Luxury trim. Pricing for the ES350h ($51,095 to start) is up $6380 over the previous ES300h, but you do get more car—namely in the physical sense—and the ES still costs significantly less than a BMW 5-series or a Mercedes-Benz E-class. Our Premium-trim test car featured a few options and still came in at under $55,000.

Lexus is notoriously risk-averse with its most popular models, and ultimately the firm’s conservatism has paid off with this new ES. It’s more modern-looking inside and out and offers more technology than before, but Lexus wisely didn’t make many changes to the core tenets that have made the ES a success. It still offers a comfortable ride and a cosseting interior, and these qualities combined with the hybrid powertrain’s quiet operation and impressive fuel efficiency should continue to please the ES faithful.

#5165. Tech Report: 10 Open-World Games You Can Finish in 10 Hours & Under

📅 15 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1990 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: 10 Open-World Games You Can Finish in 10 Hours & Under

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1990 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, when any gamer hears about open world games, they immediately (safely) assume that the game would proceed to take hours upon hours to complete.
  • In fact, some of these games can be completed in less than 10 hours.
  • Recent findings suggest that for players who are wanting a one-and-done experience with an open world game, being able to beat it within the same day or two days maximum, these games scratch that itch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, when any gamer hears about open world games, they immediately (safely) assume that the game would proceed to take hours upon hours to complete. However, that’s not always the case with open world games.

In fact, some of these games can be completed in less than 10 hours.

Recent findings suggest that for players who are wanting a one-and-done experience with an open world game, being able to beat it within the same day or two days maximum, these games scratch that itch. You’re able to hop in and complete the game practically quicker than you can download it, and it’s just the right amount of content to tide you over until the next game.

While others are diving into open world games to sink hundreds upon hundreds of hours into them, you can rest assured that these games won’t eat up your schedule.

The thing about Outer Wilds is that the world itself is the final boss, with players only having a limited amount of time in order to save the universe – but it’s not done on its own. The game’s DLC, Echoes of the Eye, is about 10 and half hours long, obviously shorter for faster players.

In a recent development, the DLC doesn’t replace anything in the game, but it’s rather a separate and self-contained location, more than ready for players to dive in and unravel its secrets. This way, if players are wanting a taste of Outer Wilds without going through the whole game, they can easily do so.

Industry observers note that this is especially the case if you’ve already beaten the game/solved the mystery of the main story. Since there isn’t really any replayability, the DLC offers a whole latest mystery altogether – in a way, it’s like you’re playing the game for the first time all over again, and it can be solved pretty quickly.

Thankfully, there are also even more DLCs if you want more mystery, but they aren’t anywhere near as condensed as Echoes of the Eye.

There’s something particularly special about Shadow of the Colossus: the game is labelled as an open world, but many players would walk away from it thinking that it’s a semi-open world due to just how empty the world itself is.

In a recent development, of course, that’s typically a bad thing for open worlds, but the unique thing about Shadow of the Colossus is that it would not work without that emptiness. Combine this with a linear order for the bosses themselves (which are platforming puzzles as well), a vague yet compelling story and a genuinely cool premise, and you’ve got a game that’s as fun as it is challenging.

Sources indicate that one of my students refers to the game as “Rated T for Teen Mario,” and I'm bound to agree, if that helps get the idea across. And just like Mario, the game can be beaten pretty swiftly: about 7 hours, in fact.

With that in mind, if this is a game that interests you, be prepared to spend most of those 7 hours climbing rather than fighting; you’re going to love it regardless.

Right now, The Legend of Zelda once again has the gaming community in a complete buzz thanks to the fantastic reception to the Ocarina of Time Remake.

The series is continuously revolutionary, constantly evolving and redefining the open world genre as we know it. However, many tend to forget that open world Zelda didn’t start with Breath of the Wild, it started with the very first entry in the entire franchise.

Sources indicate that the nice part about the game is that it’s not long at all (especially when compared to its sequels that will come over the next few decades) – averaging only at about 8 hours to beat the game. Players who want a traditional Zelda experience in a short amount of time can’t find any other game that would be a better fit.

And as the game comes up on its 40th anniversary, it’s all the more reason to dive into where it all began.

Obviously, both Red Dead Redemption games are massive, telling all kinds of stories jam-packed in a rich world of historical fiction, so it would take a while to beat either entry. However, the first game’s DLC, Undead Nightmare, is a fantastic stand-alone story that only takes about 6 and a half hours to complete.

Industry observers note that undead Nightmare takes everything you love about the classic Red Dead Redemption, but with a twist: suddenly, everyone is trying to survive a zombie apocalypse that came about practically overnight. The world and everything you can do within it, naturally, is related to this instead of your standard robberies and bounties.

It has been revealed that since the world is so condensed, the DLC goes by much quicker than most, but it’s an absolute blast from start to finish. In fact, it’s widely considered to be one of the greatest DLCs of all time, simply for how refreshingly unique and fun it is.

With that in mind, the fact that this game can be completed quicker than a standard work shift just makes it all the better.

Of all the Assassin's Creed games, the shortest mainline entry (non-DLC game) is easily Assassin's Creed: Rogue, clocking in at about 11 hours to be beaten (again, it’s much quicker than that for veteran AC fans and seasoned gamers as a whole).

Surprisingly, the game has one of the more unique stories that the series has seen, focusing on an Assassin named Shay Patrick Cormac literally going rogue, slaughtering the brotherhood he knows and siding with the Templars.

And the best part of the story is the fact that the modern-day segments are thankfully incredibly short – the segments that drag and feel like a chore in all the other titles in the franchise don’t bog down this game.

It has been revealed that overall, it’s the perfect bite-sized game for Assassin’s Creed content, regardless of if you’re a fan or even brand upcoming to the series. It’s truly one of a kind, especially for a series like AC.

If you were given 10 hours to simply explore Latest York City and soak it all in, you wouldn’t even be an eighth of the way through your journey before you reach that time. The fact that Marvel's Spider-Man brought in NYC on a similar (still scaled down) scale cemented the game’s timeframe as you continue to whip around as The Friendly Neighborhood himself.

Recent findings suggest that yet, you don’t have anywhere near as many superhero duties in Spider-Man: Miles Morales, so obviously, it will take you a lot less time. It would take about 8 hours, in fact.

In a recent development, since you’re playing the game as Miles Morales (duh) while Peter Parker is still around and kicking, you’re basically a superhero in training. This training will have you busy constantly taking down bad guys and saving the day, serving as the sole Spider-Man in NYC for several hours until Peter comes back from vacation with MJ.

Or you could just swing around New York City doing whatever you want for that timeframe, you’d get the same amount of enjoyment.

Just because a game is a horror game doesn’t mean it can’t also be open world, and in DREDGE, our open world is a vast, dangerous ocean. Even then, it’s nowhere near as dangerous as it will be once your sanity drains due to the Lovecraftian terrors you’ll encounter.

It sounds horrifying, but it’s actually the coziest fishing game you’d ever imagine. You fish, fill out your encyclopedia, discover aberrations with the marine life and upgrade your ship, but the real fun comes from the simplest mechanic: sorting the fish into your boat. Seriously, the inventory management is the most addictive part of the whole game.

Industry observers note that the nice part is that it’s wrapped up quickly, too, taking only about 9 and a half hours to complete – but trust me, you’re going to willingly sink far more hours into the game (and your ship). And if that doesn’t sound like enough content in the game for how much I sing its praises, it also has two equally dense and fun DLCs.

When it comes to short, yet full open world games, you cannot get any better of an experience than with DREDGE.

The lovely thing about Eastshade isn’t just how stunning of a game it is, but also the fact that it can be beaten pretty quickly and pretty easily – just around 9 hours.

Industry observers note that the whole game is about finding the most beautiful spots in the game to paint them (using a photography mechanic), so those entire 9 hours are filled with genuine beauty. Of course, since it’s open world, there are side quests (artwork commissions) and other things to do, but you’re going to be far more caught up in how pretty the world is.

Sources indicate that and for those who love subtle, environmental storytelling, this world is full of it. You can learn more while you’re out and about exploring in it, or from the various other characters that you can talk to.

It’s one of the few open world games that keeps you busy without actively stressing you out; since, after all, the point of the game is to relax you, you’re going to find yourself in a comfortable state of bliss while playing.

If you’ve ever wanted to feel like you’re driving a pod around Tatooine (like any Star Wars fan would), you would have a fantastic time with Sable.

The game seems pretty surface-level and simple: just ride around on your sand-speeder and enjoy the game’s lovely art style, but once you start playing, you’ll see it’s a lot deeper than you’d expect. It’s supposed to be about the protagonist’s self-discovery on their home planet, but by the end of your adventure, you’re going to feel like you’ve gone on a self-discovery of your own.

Industry observers note that while the game can be completed in about 7 and a half hours, it’s actually better if you take your time with the exploration – that’s the game’s strongest component, after all. Why not take the time to enjoy a world as pretty and interesting as this one?

It’s not perfectly polished; it’s actually pretty janky of a game at times, but if anything, it makes you love the game and all the charm it has even more. At the same time, if some of the previously mentioned jank (charm) is a little too much, then rest assured that you can get through this game very, very quickly.

Recent findings suggest that A Short Hike is just that: short. It’s not the kind of short where it’s on the shorter end of a long game, no, the game is only about an hour and a half long. If you try to complete every single element within it to 100% the game, you’re looking at about 4 hours, an incredibly tiny open world game.

The premise of the game is simple: you’re hiking up a mountain. If you run into anyone or anything on the way there, you’re more than welcome to interact with them, but it’s optional if you’re wanting to just get to the top. Considering how short the game is, I’d recommend not skipping anything if you can help it, just to get the richest experience you can.

Don’t rush through this hike, either. The game is already short enough, and there is so much enjoyable content that you don’t want to miss out on while on the way to the top.

But as we’ve learned with games like these: it’s not about the destination, it’s about the journey, so don’t be afraid to go on that journey.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The manufacturer claims its RC Racer’s 2.4-gigaherz radio system can maintain high-speed stability at distances of up to 326 feet (100 meters), while an optional Gyro feature adds counter-steering to help prevent spinouts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Tesla Cybertruck was never as affordable as Elon Musk envisioned back in 2019, when the angular electric pickup truck was unveiled as a concept. Now, though, the American EV maker is selling a sub-$1,000 miniature version of the controversial model, right on the verge of its discontinuation.

According to recent reports, the Tesla Cybertruck RC Racer was added to the company’s web shop today, as spotted by Tesla enthusiast Sawyer Merritt on X. The 1:10-scale remote-controlled EV features all-wheel drive, a rechargeable lithium-polymer battery, and independent suspension with plenty of travel.

The manufacturer claims its RC Racer’s 2.4-gigaherz radio system can maintain high-speed stability at distances of up to 326 feet (100 meters), while an optional Gyro feature adds counter-steering to help prevent spinouts.

Industry observers note that A single brushless motor sends power to both axles through a set of drive shafts, enabling a top speed of 37 miles per hour (60 kilometers per hour). That’s very impressive, and it makes the small-scale Cybertruck faster than all low-speed vehicles (LSVs) in the United States, which are capped at just 25 mph.

Tesla bundles a USB-C charger in the box, which is a welcome addition in a world where smartphone makers are no longer including charging cables, let alone charging bricks. The Cybertruck RC Racer has an advertised run time of up to 20 minutes, and judging from the promotional video posted on the manufacturer’s website, it looks like a ton of fun.

To charge the battery, the polycarbonate body needs to be removed from the chassis via the quick-release clips. Then, the battery needs to be disconnected from the motor and connected to the on-board charger, and charging can begin via the USB-C port on the side of the chassis. According to Tesla, a full charge may take up to three hours, which can be a bit of a buzzkill, but the company stated it will soon start selling spare parts for the RC Racer, so buyers will probably be able to get a spare battery or two to keep the fun going for longer.

Industry observers note that the included transmitter has a side wheel for steering and a trigger for acceleration, braking, and reverse. Separate controls for the throttle trim, steering alignment trim, steering reverse, and gyro stability assist are also included. The transmitter is powered by four AA batteries, which are not included in the box.

Recent findings suggest that tesla’s Cybertryck RC Racer is available now for $350 on the firm’s online shop, with the first shipments expected to arrive at customers’ doors starting next week. According to the company, the RC car is not suitable for children under 14 years old.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that phantom Blade Zero is out now for everyone as a console exclusive on PlayStation 5 and on PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store as well.
  • However, you're looking for advice on which of the three visual modes Phantom Blade Zero offers you should use on your PS5.
  • Sources indicate that phantom Blade Zero has three visual modes on PS5 Pro: Quality, Balanced, and Performance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that phantom Blade Zero is out now for everyone as a console exclusive on PlayStation 5 and on PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store as well. If you missed it, it's my favorite action game of the year so far, and you can read why in Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero review. That explains why I think you should check the game out; Game Informer's list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks will get you some key information I wish I had when I started the game; and this guide I wrote up about the requirements you need to get the best ending in Phantom Blade Zero will help you find all story-critical content in the game.

However, you're looking for advice on which of the three visual modes Phantom Blade Zero offers you should use on your PS5. This here piece is for you.

Sources indicate that phantom Blade Zero has three visual modes on PS5 Pro: Quality, Balanced, and Performance. I tested all three. My personal favorite was Balanced, which gives you an upscaled (checkerboarded) 4K resolution at 40 FPS, as long as you have a 120Hz TV with VRR. If you have a 120Hz TV, it likely has VRR because most major manufacturers include it with 120Hz. I like this mode because the upscaled 4K looks beautiful, just a hair less than native 4K, and if you aren't someone super trained on those details, I'd wager you won't notice the difference. The best part is that this mode offers 40 FPS gameplay, which, contrary to how math works, is halfway between 30 FPS and 60 FPS; I'm not kidding, look it up. As such, 40 FPS feels much smoother than 30 FPS, and you're still getting crisp 4K resolution. It's a win-win for me and my go-to mode when a game offers it. That noted, if you don’t have a PS5 Pro, you won’t see this Balanced mode.

Recent findings suggest that the Performance mode offers an upscaled 2K resolution with a pretty locked 60 FPS. Phantom Blade Zero is an extremely fast, fluid action game, so I think many people will want the buttery smoothness of 60 FPS gameplay. If that's you, pick the Performance mode. Sure, its resolution is lower, and it will look blurrier and less crisp than the other two modes, but if you aren't switching back and forth often or looking at side-by-side images, you likely won't notice.

Quality mode is native 4K resolution (absolutely beautiful, the best visual image you can get playing Phantom Blade Zero), but at 30 FPS... and for a game like this, I don't think 30 FPS does it justice. I don't really recommend this mode for combat, but if you're just waltzing around Wulin, grabbing screenshots and such, turn it on and bask in the wonders of developer S-Game's art team. Note: There is an option for ray tracing on PS5 Pro. I tested all three graphics modes with it on and off and noticed zero performance changes or issues. So, use ray tracing – it’s nice!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that just like vehicles themselves, automotive manufacturing plants have to go through a lot of testing before cranking out the first production model. Scout Motors broke ground on its Blythewood, South Carolina, plant about two and a half years ago, and as final bits of construction wrap up, the VW Group subsidiary is beginning to build validation vehicles to test production processes.

When Scout reemerged a few years ago to bring back the practical, can-do vehicles that defined the brand in the 1960s and ’70s, it aimed to build a fleet of hybrid and electric body-on-frame off-roaders that blended modern amenities with vintage charm. The automaker aims to launch a Terra pickup truck and a Traveler SUV for the 2028 model year.

See all results for new 2028 Scout Terra for sale near 60616.

It has been revealed that it looks like Scout is still on track to stick with that timeline. The automaker has declared that most of the manufacturing parts are already up and running, with validation vehicles beginning to make their way through the body, paint, and assembly shops. Validation vehicles are kind of like a practice run, giving employees the ability to problem-solve and refine processes without having to keep a tight schedule.

Sources indicate that alongside the upcoming equipment, Scout is testing out more than 750 robots in the body shop. The AI-supported bots will be used to monitor about 5000 weld points per vehicle for quality assurance. At full capacity, the body shop will be able to process about 40 vehicles per hour.

Industry observers note that the Terra pickup and Traveler SUV are both expected to start at under $60,000. Scout states the validation process will continue into 2027, followed by more refined pre-production vehicles and eventually the finalized production model. That’s right in line with what Scott Keogh, Scout’s CEO, told us last year, when he projected that the first vehicles would go on sale by the end of 2027. Deliveries are expected to begin in 2028.

  • For that money, you get a 1,200Wh battery, dual hydraulic disc brakes, and full suspension in a 130 lb package.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the Zonveer ZX3 is one of the best values I’ve seen in electric off-road riding, and one of the most fun things I’ve ridden to date – value for the dollar. Its Black Friday sale brings the 2,800W electric dirt bike down to $1,299, $500 off its $1,799 list price.

For that money, you get a 1,200Wh battery, dual hydraulic disc brakes, and full suspension in a 130 lb package. That’s a great entry point for beginners.

According to recent reports, zonveer is a young brand. It released in the US in March with two bikes, the kid-sized DX1 and the ZX3, and it’s run by United Mobility, which lists its address in Dover, Delaware. It sells direct and ships from US warehouses, and Zonveer also sells the ZX3 across Europe under its own brand through its EU store.

Here’s what the ZX3 brings, according to Zonveer’s product page:.

Industry observers note that A hub motor means there’s no motor chain to maintain, and the NFC card and PIN unlock mean there’s no app to fight with. I like that.

Recent findings suggest that zonveer sent me a ZX3 to test, and I’m impressed with what they shipped, knowing the cost. It isn’t trying to be a race bike. And it doesn’t need to be. Here’s my first ride review:.

Industry observers note that with 2,800W peak, it’s somewhat modest by e-moto standards. That’s exactly what makes it approachable for someone who has never ridden a dirt bike: the power is enough to have a blast on trails without being intimidating.

My girlfriend had never ridden a dirt bike before, and she got comfortable within a few minutes, and she was hooked as soon as she got the hang of it.

Recent findings suggest that and while testing with my girlfriend, it was clear this bike makes the most sense for lighter riders. Zonveer claims it climbs slopes of up to 30 degrees, which is optimistic for anyone over ~175 lbs, like myself. It still climbed some of the worst slopes on my land, but it did so with some difficulty, which wasn’t the case for some of my lighter friends who also rode it.

Recent findings suggest that range is the other claim to take with a grain of salt. Riding 45 miles on 1,200Wh means using under 27Wh per mile, which is e-bike efficiency on a 130 lb dirt bike with knobby tires. It’s still a lot of energy, and you can ride this long distances at lower speeds. Just expect less if you ride it hard, and that’s where the fun is at.

Zonveer’s Black Friday sale has the ZX3 at $1,299, and the firm gave Electrek readers the code ELECTREK for an extra 5% off, which brings it down to $1,234.05.

Sources indicate that the sale also includes a free water bottle and lock, and can be combined for a two-pack of ZX3s for $2,599. Shipping is free, the warranty is one year, Zonveer told us it accepts returns within 30 days on bikes ridden less than 10 miles, with a $200 restocking fee. Here’s the full refund policy.

We’ve ridden a lot of electric two-wheelers, and the ZX3 is one of the most fun per dollar. At $1,299, or about $1,234 with our code, it’s hard to find another 1,200Wh electric dirt bike with dual hydraulic disc brakes and full suspension from a brand that ships from US warehouses.

It’s not fast by e-moto standards, and the range and climbing claims are optimistic. But for beginners, and especially lighter riders, the power lands right in that sweet spot of manageable fun. It’s a bike you can learn on without scaring yourself, and it’s cheap enough that a family can buy two for less than one Sur-Ron.

#5159. Solid-State Cells Can Make The U.S. Competitive In Batteries Again: CEO

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1102 w)
📖 Baca
Business & Policy 📈 Bullish 🌐 Insideevs ↗ Open Full Page

Solid-State Cells Can Make The U.S. Competitive In Batteries Again: CEO

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1102 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that american companies may be playing catch-up to Asian giants in the battery business, but solid-state batteries could give the U.S.
  • Solid Power is part of a wave of young American battery startups—including California-based QuantumScape and Massachusetts-based Factorial—that are racing to commercialize solid-state batteries.
  • Battery scientists broadly believe that solid-state cells can unlock more driving range for EVs, faster charging speeds, and eliminate fire risks compared to current lithium-ion batteries.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that american companies may be playing catch-up to Asian giants in the battery business, but solid-state batteries could give the U.S. another shot at becoming competitive. That's according to the CEO of Colorado-based solid electrolyte specialist Solid Power.

Solid Power is part of a wave of young American battery startups—including California-based QuantumScape and Massachusetts-based Factorial—that are racing to commercialize solid-state batteries.

Battery scientists broadly believe that solid-state cells can unlock more driving range for EVs, faster charging speeds, and eliminate fire risks compared to current lithium-ion batteries.

In a recent development, but the technology has proven extraordinarily difficult to manufacture at scale without defects. If you've been following this race, you'll know the technology has spent years being just around the corner.

Samsung SDI all-solid-state battery.

In a recent development, solid Power, however, believes the wait will eventually be worth it. The organization expects solid-state batteries to reach select high-end EVs by the end of this decade, with broader adoption following in the early 2030s.

It has been revealed that it also secured a $50 million U.S. Department of Energy grant in 2024 under the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law to support its development efforts.

Unlike some of its competitors, Solid Power isn't trying to build an entire battery. It specializes in one crucial ingredient: the electrolyte, which facilitates the movement of lithium ions between the electrodes.

Recent findings suggest that in a lithium-ion battery that electrolyte is usually a flammable liquid chemical. In solid-state batteries, companies are branching out into mainly three different varieties for the solid electrolytes: polymers, oxides, and sulfides.

It has been revealed that solid Power is betting on the third option. President and CEO John Van Scoter told InsideEVs in an interview that its flexible sulfide-based solid electrolyte design can help established battery makers incorporate the technology into their existing production processes and give the U.S. a way back in the battery business.

“All solid-state batteries can be the way that [the U.S.] can get back in and be competitive in the battery industry,” Van Scoter stated.

According to recent reports, the company took a step toward that goal last month with the commissioning of its Mobius pilot production line at its plant in Thornton, Colorado. The goal? To manufacture and sell electrolytes from this plant to some of the biggest names in the automotive and battery industry.

In a recent development, the company has already been working with Ford, BMW, Samsung SDI, SK ON, and more names that are yet to be publicly revealed. Rather than building complete batteries itself, Solid Power mentioned battery makers can integrate its electrolyte into their own cell designs, test the results, and work together to refine the technology before production.

Recent findings suggest that van Scoter mentioned the firm has completed its joint development agreements with Ford and BMW. Its focus is now shifting toward working with major battery manufacturers to figure out how to scale production.

The Mobius pilot line is expected to become operational by the end of the year, adding 45 metric tons of annual solid electrolyte production capacity. Combined with its existing facilities, that would bring the total pilot capacity to 75 metric tons a year.

Sources indicate that so, what does all this translate to in terms of performance? When added to a silicone anode and a nickel manganese cobalt (NMC) cathode, Solid Power’s sulfide electrolyte can increase a cell’s energy density to 390 watt hours per kilogram and last over 1,000 cycles. (Modern NMC batteries with liquid electrolytes typically deliver around 250 to 280 Wh/kg.).

With a lithium metal anode, that energy density can increase to 440 Wh/kg, the company claimed, nearly double of an average lithium-ion battery today. However, these are just theoretical numbers. The final energy density will depend on the battery maker that builds the actual cell.

In a recent development, “We create the magic that allows the cell to work,” Van Scoter remarked. “But it's up to the cell design as to energy densities, cycle life, all those other notable attributes.”.

Another big advantage is that the company believes its technology doesn’t need brand fresh factories or expensive retooling.

“We can use standard [lithium-ion battery] roll to roll equipment in order to build all solid state cells,” Van Scoter stated.

According to recent reports, of course, solid-state batteries still have some familiar problems to solve. One is dendrite formation. These are the tiny, needle-like lithium structures that can grow inside a cell, potentially causing short circuits and capacity loss. Van Scoter said Solid Power had put a lot of engineering effort to solve that concern.

The company isn't starting from scratch with automakers, either. BMW last year released images of a prototype i7 equipped with a solid-state battery featuring Solid Power's silicon anode solid-state battery.

BMW i7 Solid-State Battery Prototype.

Industry observers note that BMW, Samsung SDI, and Solid Power have also entered a three-way agreement to develop the technology for commercialization. Samsung SDI will manufacture the cells, BMW will develop the battery modules and packs, and Solid Power will supply the solid electrolyte. The exact timeline of when we’ll see the fruits of this partnership remains unclear.

Recent findings suggest that other American solid-state startups are taking a more vertically integrated approach, developing the entire cells themselves. QuantumScape, for instance, is working with Volkswagen, Honda and other automakers to commercialize its technology. Meanwhile, Mercedes-Benz and Stellantis have already begun testing prototype vehicles equipped with Factorial's solid-state cells.

Solid Power, however, believes that the technology might mature first in defense applications, drones and humanoid robots.

“The qualification cycles are shorter and the cycle life of the platform is much faster,” Van Scoter said of drones and robots.

Either way, U.S. automakers and battery companies didn’t quite capitalize on the lithium-ion battery boom, leaving that to Asian giants. Whether they can get solid-state batteries across the finish line first is something only time will tell.

📖 Baca

Tesla kills $41,990 Model Y AWD: all-wheel drive now costs $8,000 more

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (815 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla has pulled the $41,990 Model Y All-Wheel Drive from its US online configurator.
  • The trim lasted just over nine months.
  • Here’s what Tesla’s US Model Y design studio lists as of today (prices before the destination fee):.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla has pulled the $41,990 Model Y All-Wheel Drive from its US online configurator. The cheapest dual-motor Model Y you can order now is the Model Y Premium AWD at $49,990, an $8,000 jump.

The trim lasted just over nine months. Tesla rolled out it in early February, and it’s gone without a word from the manufacturer.

Here’s what Tesla’s US Model Y design studio lists as of today (prices before the destination fee):.

Industry observers note that when Tesla rolled out the base Model Y AWD in February, it was basically the stripped-down Model Y with a second motor. It had 294 miles of range, did 0-60 mph in 4.6 seconds and kept the same cut-down cabin as the base RWD. At a $2,000 premium over the single-motor version, it was the most sensible AWD pricing Tesla had offered in years.

In a recent development, and the AWD trim isn’t the only change. In February, the Premium RWD cost $44,990 and the Premium AWD cost $48,990. Both are now $1,000 higher.

Recent findings suggest that add it up and the cheapest all-wheel-drive Model Y went from $41,990 to $49,990 in nine months. That’s a 19% increase.

According to recent reports, the timing isn’t great for Tesla’s competitive position. Chevrolet’s 2027 Equinox EV LT 1 AWD starts at $40,295 before destination, with 307 miles of EPA range. Ford’s Mustang Mach-E Select AWD starts at $40,795.

Both now undercut Tesla’s cheapest AWD crossover by more than $9,000.

According to recent reports, if you live somewhere it snows and you were shopping for a new Model Y, the math just got a lot worse. You can still find some base AWD units in Tesla’s inventory, but once those are gone, that’s it.

According to recent reports, this is also the latest cut in a year of Tesla shrinking its lineup. Elon Musk killed the Model S and Model X in January to free up Fremont for Optimus, and Cybertruck production is winding down. Meanwhile, the most recent upcoming Tesla is the $61,990 Model Y L, which sits at the top of the range, not the bottom.

We liked this trim. It was the first time in a long time that Tesla treated all-wheel drive as a $2,000 option rather than a huge upsell bundled with a nicer interior, and it put the Model Y right in the price bracket of the Equinox EV and Mach-E with AWD.

Now it’s gone, and the Premium trims went up $1,000 on top of that. Tesla didn’t explain either move. It rarely does anymore.

It has been revealed that there are two plausible reasons. Either Tesla is tight on Model Y build slots and would rather fill them with higher-margin Premium trims, or the cheap AWD simply wasn’t selling. We don’t know which. But both explanations land in the same place for buyers: a more expensive Model Y.

Sources indicate that great news. Can't wait for people to stop buying them and the tech giant stops being a meme stock. It's about time EV shoppers recognized that there are indeed compelling options available.

And Tesla has a habit of this. The “Standard” name for its cheaper Model Y and Model 3 lasted a few months. The single-motor Cybertruck, the only version that made sense, was gone within days. Cheaper trims show up, get a news cycle, and quietly disappear.

In a recent development, that’s a problem for a firm whose consumer lineup is shrinking down to two cars. The Model Y is Tesla’s volume. Thinning it out at the bottom is the opposite of what you’d do if growing EV sales were the priority.

How long before the $39,990 RWD goes the same way?

The game is set to arrive simultaneously across PC, PS5, and mobile (iOS, Android) on January 22, and pre-registrations continue to be open.

Gryphline broke the news on The Game Awards stage alongside a chunky trailer featuring a latest OneRepublic song. It actually ends up being a nice tone piece for the world of Arknights, showing a lot of cinematics alongside the music itself.

The developer-publisher also confirmed that so far, Arknights: Endfield has had over 30 million pre-registrations worldwide since pre-registrations went live. Some players have been able to play early, of course, with the most recent opportunity being Beta Test 2.

Recent findings suggest that if you’ve been following the game’s development, you’ll know that it was pretty clear we’re closer than ever to the official launch. The most recent beta build showed off polished content, with upcoming animations and cutscenes.

It has been revealed that we’ve been playing it ourselves, and we think you’re going to agree with our Arknights: Endfield character tier list. You can expect more coverage from us as we get closer to launch, and when the game actually arrives.

Though it might seem like it came out of nowhere, the game is based on the Arknights universe, itself a massive mobile game with over 100 million downloads. Endfield brings a different flavour to that world, with a mix of strategy, exploration and real-time combat, not unlike the many games created by HoYoverse.

You can pre-register yourself on the official website.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that they say that lightning never strikes the same place twice, let alone thrice, but McLaren is channeling Zeus with its newest W1 flagship. As a descendant of the hallowed McLaren F1 and a direct successor to the brand's last 903-hp P1 halo car, the W1 assumes a throne previously occupied by hypercar royalty. And if you couldn’t guess by its wind-sculpted, carbon-fiber-laden exterior, the W1 has the spec sheet to back up its noble position.

Wielding a 9200-rpm twin-turbo V-8 paired with an axial-flux electric motor, the W1 delivers 1258 horsepower to the pavement via its rear wheels, making it the most powerful McLaren ever. Those ponies don’t have to contend with much mass, as a carbon-fiber tub and body help keep the W1's dry weight to a feathery 3084 pounds. Active aerodynamics, including a rear wing that extends rearward up to 11.8 inches, add massive downforce and enable maximum attack at the racetrack. The W1 is a worthy heir to its predecessors, the latest in a highly accomplished bloodline of supersonic, roadgoing weaponry.

Industry observers note that if this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.

According to recent reports, the W1 uses a plug-in hybrid powertrain comprised of McLaren's MHP-8 turbocharged V-8 engine working in unison with a radial-flux electric motor and an 8-speed transmission; it sends power to the rear wheels. The V-8 alone is good for 916 horsepower, and the electric motor 342 horsepower. Combined, that's 1258 ponies, the highest output of any McLaren.

Industry observers note that the electric element includes a motorsport-derived E-module: a radial flux motor and integrated Motor Control Unit weighing just 44 pounds, similar to the type used in IndyCar racing. (McLaren participates in that series as well as F1.) The electric motor is mounted to the transmission and can spin up to 24,000 rpm. The E-module is powered by a battery of about 1.4 kWh, enclosed in a structural carbon-fiber box located low in the chassis to optimize the center of gravity. The battery maintains a minimum level of charge to crank the engine on vehicle start-up and to power the electric reversing function. McLaren quotes an electric-only driving range of about two miles and a charging time of 22 minutes to bring the battery to 80 percent.

Sources indicate that the McLaren W1 includes a comprehensive warranty and maintenance schedule. Similar to McLarens equipped with the V-6 hybrid, the V-8-hybrid-equipped W1 follows a 12-month service interval schedule that reflects McLaren series production supercars rather than schedules of its track-focused cars.

BYD has already shown that charging an EV doesn’t have to take much longer than filling a gas tank. Now it’s tackling another problem: getting enough electricity to a fast charger in the first place.

Sources indicate that its latest site in the Abu Dhabi desert combines solar panels, battery storage, Flash Charging, and a robotic arm that plugs in the car. BYD indicates the system can work independently of the electricity grid, potentially bringing fast charging to places where a power connection may not be feasible. The proposition is pretty simple: Solar panels generate electricity, batteries store it, and the charger sends it to an EV.

Industry observers note that battery-backed charging is becoming more common because it lets stations deliver more power than their grid connection alone can supply, while also reducing demand on the grid during busy periods. Tesla’s biggest Supercharger site, which it opened earlier this year, also uses solar panels and Tesla's Megapack batteries. Companies like Electric Era and Beam Global specialize in battery-backed charging. Even BYD Flash chargers not located in the middle of the desert and not supplied by solar panels use on-site energy storage to boost power delivery.

Sources indicate that each of BYD's T-shaped Flash chargers is hooked up to two 185-kilowatt-hour storage batteries, for 370 kWh total. These draw power from the grid at around 100 to 560 kilowatts, then supply the car at a much higher rate. The chargers can send up to 1,500 kW through one cable, or up to 1,000 kW when both are in use at the same time.

It has been revealed that adding solar panels into the equation means some or even all of that electricity can be generated on-site. However, BYD hasn’t disclosed the battery capacity or solar output of this fresh desert installation. So it's not clear how many cars the station can charge—or how quickly—on solar power alone.

Recent findings suggest that the charging hardware is impressively quick. With BYD’s latest 1,500-kW Flash chargers, compatible cars running its second-generation Blade battery can charge from 10% to 70% in five minutes, or hit 97% in nine minutes.

It has been revealed that now that infrastructure is going global. The company notes it looks to establish 6,000 Flash Charging stations worldwide by the end of 2027, but it hasn’t specified how many will offer solar power, off-grid operation, or that robotic arm.

Europe is getting a taste of BYD’s Flash charging with sites up and running in Italy, Germany, France, and the United Kingdom. Canada is coming soon too. The only vehicle it at the moment sells in Europe that can fully utilize its power is the Denza Z9 GT. During a demonstration, the electric wagon charged from 10% to 80% in six minutes and 32 seconds, reaching 97% in nine minutes and 22 seconds.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Electric truck operator Nevoya is expanding its deal with Meta with the fresh deployment of 25 Class 8 battery-electric trucks on the Interstate 10 (I-10) between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona … but Meta won’t be shipping any products.

The second major trucking deal between Facebook parent organization Meta and electric truck operator Nevoya will put 25 newly introduced battery-electric semis on I-10, running freight between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona. But Meta isn’t buying trucks, hiring drivers or shipping its own products. Instead, Zuck’s company helping pay for someone else’s cleaner freight through environmental attribute certificates (EACs), a carbon credit mechanism that lets companies claim the emissions benefits of electric trucking without operating the trucks themselves.

Recent findings suggest that “Coming back to Nevoya for a second corridor reflects what we look for in our value chain work: partners that can scale, and agreements we can repeat, mentioned Devon Lake, Head of Net Zero Strategy, Meta. “Freight is part of the emissions footprint of building and operating our data centers, and multi-year commitments like this help address our scope 3 emissions and make electric trucking available and competitive on the routes that serve the regions where we build.”.

Recent findings suggest that meta was one of several buyers in the DC-based Center for Green Market Activation (GMA) buyers’ alliance. The group’s collective EAC purchases supported Nevoya’s initial 63-truck deployment on the Houston–Dallas corridor back in May. This new Agreement, however, is a standalone deal between Nevoya and Meta only, and gives Meta an established framework to open more electric truck corridors in the future.

This clever application of these agreements is what makes the Dallas-Houston run stand out, with GMA calling it, “the first large-scale application of book and claim to zero-emission trucking.” The company adds that this arrangement helps client companies overcome existing barriers to EV adoption while enabling Nevoya to deploy latest trucks, “where they deliver the strongest commercial and operational value.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that very much when we expected it, Blizzard has officially revealed Diablo 4’s next major expansion at The Game Awards. Lord of Hatred delivers a upcoming campaign that continues the mainline story, picking up from where Vessel of Hatred left off. Mephisto, the eponymous Lord of Hatred, has seemingly finally escaped imprisonment to rule over Sanctuary.

Lord of Hatred is the second Diablo 4 expansion, and it will be available on PC, PS5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S on April 28.

Industry observers note that it’s always a substantial deal when we get a new Diablo expansion, especially for a game as starved of fresh (major) content as Diablo 4 has been. But perhaps the biggest piece of news out of the Lord of Hatred reveal is that the expansion is bringing not one, but two new classes to the game.

The first of which is The Paladin, whereas the second is being kept under wraps. Even more surprising is that The Paladin is playable right now for anyone who pre-purchases the expansion. This is a well-timed shadow drop, especially given that Diablo 4’s latest season has just kicked off.

The expansion adds a new region to the world: Skovos, which is where the events of the new campaign will be taking place. This is the first time Skovos has been in a Diablo game. The region is of major significance to the world and lore of the series, as it is the birthplace of the firstborn, home of Lilith and Inaruis.

Sources indicate that lord of Hatred brings a decent number of major systems to Diablo 4. The endgame is getting a big overhaul, headlined by the upcoming War Plans feature. Through this, you can effectively design your own endgame grind, creating challenges based on the activities you like and earning rewards along the way.

Endgame activities now also feature their own skill trees, which can be progressed through by creating War Prepares for your character featuring each activity. The fresh endgame activity, Echoing Hatred, is something of horde mode where you must defend against unrelenting waves of enemies.

None of that matters without loot, of course, and the upcoming expansion is bringing back the Horadric Cube, and adding set bonuses using the Talisman system. The long-awaited and highly-requested Loot Filter is also coming to the game with the release of the expansion.

Beyond itemisation, each class’ skill tree will grow with new bonus skill variants. In fact, the entire skill system is being reworked for all classes - though details are a little sparse at the moment.

You can also expect the level cap to go up, which is very likely necessary to fit all the latest skills and various systems. Blizzard offered a deep dive into the new Paladin class, which you see on the official blog.

Treyarch Lays Off Call of Duty Zombies Mastermind Craig Houston After 20 Years

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (749 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Craig Houston, the writer behind much of Call of Duty’s Zombies storyline, has been laid off by Treyarch after around 20 years at the studio.
  • Recent findings suggest that he shared the news himself on Friday via X and LinkedIn, and I have to say, it’s a rather graceful message considering the circumstances.
  • He didn’t go into the reasons, but it appears to be part of the huge Xbox restructuring announced earlier this year, which is set to affect 3,200 jobs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Craig Houston, the writer behind much of Call of Duty’s Zombies storyline, has been laid off by Treyarch after around 20 years at the studio.

Recent findings suggest that he shared the news himself on Friday via X and LinkedIn, and I have to say, it’s a rather graceful message considering the circumstances. Houston remarked he was proud and privileged to have worked alongside so many talented people, many of whom will remain friends for life, before thanking fans for their enthusiasm, support and kind words over the years. On X, he posted it alongside a video celebrating 30 years of Treyarch, featuring footage from many of the games he worked on, which makes the whole thing feel a little more bittersweet.

He didn’t go into the reasons, but it appears to be part of the huge Xbox restructuring announced earlier this year, which is set to affect 3,200 jobs. Treyarch sits under Activision Blizzard, which in turn is owned by Xbox, so it isn’t a huge surprise that the cuts have reached the studio. Still, seeing a name like his on the list stings, especially if you’ve spent any amount of time shooting zombies with your friends at 2 in the morning.

For those who don’t know him by name, and I suspect that’s quite a few people, Houston has been at Treyarch since 2006. His first Call of Duty there was Call of Duty 3, where he worked as a video editor, which is a pretty humble start for someone who would go on to shape one of the series’ biggest modes. From World at War in 2008 onwards, he was the main writer for Zombies, whilst also writing for Treyarch’s campaigns.

Recent findings suggest that he is credited as a writer and designer on Black Ops 1 through 4, and later as part of the design and creative development teams on the likes of Cold War, Black Ops 6 and Black Ops 7. Interestingly, he isn’t credited on this year’s Modern Warfare 4.

Sources indicate that zombies obviously wasn’t a one-man show, with Jimmy Zielinski, Jason Blundell and Kevin Drew all being a massive part of how the mode evolved. Houston’s writing is what a lot of fans point to when they talk about why they fell in love with the characters, though. He also wrote the jingles for the original perks introduced in Verrückt, which is one of my favourite details in all of this. If you’ve ever caught yourself singing along to a vending machine whilst a horde closes in on you, that one’s on him.

The response since Friday has been lovely to see. Former Treyarch developer Tony Flame replied to Houston’s post calling him a legend and saying it was an honour to work with him, adding that he created a truly special experience that will live on for millions of fans. Over on Reddit, one fan described him as a great guy, noting that you can tell how much he loves the story and characters he writes simply by how excited he gets when talking about them in promo material.

Many fans argue that Houston never quite got the recognition he deserved. In the wake of this announcement, many people admitted they hadn’t really been aware of him until after Black Ops 3, despite him having been there since the very beginning, and I think that’s true for a lot of us players. We tend to know the directors and the faces from the trailers, whilst the people writing the lines we end up quoting for years stay in the background. Zombies a mode spawned out of passion, and it’s hard to see someone fundamentally involved with that leave.

Industry observers note that truth be told, this is the part of the Xbox restructuring that I find hardest to get my head around. Twenty years of knowing a story inside out, including every timeline, every character and every twist, isn’t something a studio can simply hire back in. Of course, I don’t know the reasoning behind this particular decision, and Houston himself hasn’t mentioned a bad word about Treyarch. It is, however, a reminder that these layoff numbers are made up of people, some of whom have been shaping the games we love for the last two decades.

According to recent reports, houston hasn’t said what he intends to do next. Whatever it ends up being, I hope it involves writing, and ideally a jingle or two.
