  • We knew it was coming soon after the fresh model appeared in a regulatory filing in China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) last month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, BYD opened pre-orders for the third-generation Tang starting at about $34,000 in China. This five-seat flagship SUV packs more than you’d expect for the money, with two massive 30-inch-plus screens inside and up to 850 km (528 miles) of CLTC range.

The third-generation Tang joins the Great Tang, or Da Tang, as it’s called in China in BYD’s expanding flagship SUV lineup.

We knew it was coming soon after the fresh model appeared in a regulatory filing in China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) last month.

BYD announced on Friday that pre-orders for the third-gen Tang are officially open, starting at 225,000 yuan, which is around $34,000.

The “large five-seat flagship SUV,” as BYD calls it, is available in three variants, priced from 225,000 yuan ($34,000), 240,000 yuan ($36,000), and 260,000 yuan ($39,000) with rear- and all-wheel-drive variants.

The two lower-priced variants are both RWD, offering a CLTC range of up to 850 km (528 miles), while the top-spec dual-motor AWD version has up to 770 km (478 miles).

All versions use BYD’s second-generation Blade Batteries and Flash Charging tech, enabling the battery to be charged from 10% to 80% in five minutes, or nine minutes to go from 10% to 97%.

Industry observers note that inside, the five-seat SUV packs a surprising amount of tech and premium extras for the price. The setup features two massive screens: a 35.4″ integrated display and another 30″ panoramic theater screen.

Unlike its predessor, which offered five and six-seat configurations, the third-gen Tang will only be offered as a five-seater.

The five-seat setup opens up interior space for passengers and the third-gen Tang has the largest front trunk (frunk) in its class at 205L, BYD said.

Like many of its new flagship vehicles, the third-gen Tang is equipped with BYD’s latest tech, including its God’s Eye B driver-assistance system and Disus-A dual-chamber intelligent air suspension body control system.

Other added features include a 22-speaker Dynaudio sound system, intelligent electric all‑wheel drive, a high-speed tire blowout stability system, and its iTAC intelligent torque control system.

Lu Tian, the general manager of BYD’s Dynasty division stated third-gen Tang vehicles have arrived at dealerships nationwide.

Why mention "two enormous screens" like they are some markers of a more premium vehicle or represent some value? We don't measure the utility of cars by screen real estate per dollar. It's the other part of the utility that matter: range, driving dynamics, road trip convenience, fit/finish/materials/insulation. Personally, I don't think "enormous screens" are going to age well as an automotive trend.

The Great Tang received over 150,000 preorders by the time it rolled out in mid-June, a record for a single BYD model.

Since its official launch, the larger Great Tang (Da Tang) has sold more than 10,000 units for four straight months now.

The Great Tang is on sale in China in pure electric (EV) and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) powertrains. The cheapest EV variant starts at 239,900 yuan ($35,500) a CLTC driving range of 800 km (497 miles). Starting at just 269,900 yuan ($40,000), the Flagship EV version uses a bigger (130.15 kWh) battery, offering a CLTC range of up to 590 miles (950 km).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EA Sports has revealed 3 new Heroes coming to FC 26 Ultimate Team as part of Team 1 of the Winter Wildcards promo: Ivan Zamorano, Claudio Pizarro and Jill Scott.

The Bayern and Werder Bremen legend Claudio Pizarro is famously the Bundesliga’s oldest ever player, after turning out well past 40 years of age - up front no less. But he’s making an appearance in FC 26 because he won the Hero Vote Poll a few months ago, with the Peruvian edging out notable nutter Steffan Effenberg and the prolific Brazilian striker, Elber.

The love for South American Heroes continues with Ivan Zamorano presented in his Real Madrid guise rather than part of the unbelievably stacked Inter squad which featured legends and Icons ranging from current Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone to Javier Zanetti and Ronaldo Nazario.

And probably most interestingly, Queen of the Jungle and centurion Lioness, Jill Scott, is also coming to shore up the midfield with a card which fits the “Gullit Gang” pre-requisite of all face stats over 80 - including a dominant 91 physical befitting her role as one of the most recognisable enforcers in women’s football.

Whether her in-game body type will actually let her put that strength out on the pitch (she will surely also have Bruiser) remains to be seen, but she could easily have the gangly aura of Patrick Vieira if the rest of her PlayStyles are right.

New Ultimate Team Heroes have been added mid-season before, including the likes of Enzo Francescoli in FC 24, but 3 at once looks to indicate that EA is leaning on Heroes to add fan-favourite players to the game with a lower threshold than Icons.

Plus they can be given away for free without upsetting the power curve as much as Icons, as shown by the free Classic XI Heroes handed out recently (I got Mario Gomez, F).

The rest of the Winter Wildcards team features a host of equally famous, and now infamous, players with some featuring 99 stats and alternative positions.

Highlights include striker and CAM versions of Balon D’or holder Ousmane Dembele, but also everyone’s love-to-hate Low Driven Shot master, Claudia Pina.

There are also incredibly strong-looking Gabriel and Fede Valverde cards, as well as downgraded, and therefore hopefully cheaper, versions of Icons like Johan Cruyff.

  • May Mobility declared on Thursday that it plans to integrate its autonomous driving systems into the Buzz to give it a job wherever driverless taxis are welcome.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the Volkswagen ID. Buzz hasn't exactly been a smash hit in the U.S. But that hasn't stopped commercial customers from eyeing up the nostalgic electric van for something it's particularly good at: moving people.

May Mobility declared on Thursday that it plans to integrate its autonomous driving systems into the Buzz to give it a job wherever driverless taxis are welcome.

May wants to use its existing tech stack to equip up to the ID. Buzzes with hardware and software that can see "up to 10 seconds into the future.".

In a recent development, well, kind of—May's tech uses onboard predictive modeling to anticipate how the world around it will move, similar how a human assess other drivers around them. It creates multiple scenarios in its digital brain and uses the model's reasoning to determine which one is most suited for its environment.

The tech would also make the cars capable of integrating with any of the "global robotaxi platforms," which is one of the ways that May is approaching its partnership-first business model. Presumably, that means its existing fleet partners like Lyft, Uber, and other ride hailing services around the world.

May's approach is also a silent win for folks who want to make sure that Buzz doesn't fizzle out.

One of the biggest blockers to Buzz adoption on the consumer side has been the price. While that could change in the coming months, the van's initially high price tag and just so-so range made it a fairly lukewarm offering to EV buyers looking to park the Buzz in their own driveway. That's why Robotaxis might be the best use of the Buzz yet.

It has been revealed that it's roomy enough to comfortably haul plenty of passengers (and whatever cargo they bring along), plus it has the easy ingress and egress of a minivan. Other companies seem to agree, even VW's own MOIA arm that recently began testing an autonomous version of the Buzz in Los Angeles.

So far, May has completed about 600,000 commercial driverless rides in the U.S. and Japan. And while it hasn't said how many cars it operates, May is pretty open about its long-term goal for the Buzz.

It looks to put 10,000 of these autonomous ID. Buzzes on the road by 2031. That all starts with road testing early next year, followed by delivering the first fleet vehicles to customers by 2028.

  • According to recent reports, the newly introduced entry-level EV is “the last piece of the puzzle,” Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer noted last March after unveiling the ID.
  • Volkswagen remarked the production version will launch in 2027 with a starting price of around €20,000 ($22,000).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, volkswagen is getting ready to launch a fresh electric car starting at about €20,000 ($22,000) in 2027, and it looks like the entry-level EV may no longer be nameless. A newly filed trademark could have just given away what VW looks to call it.

According to recent reports, the newly introduced entry-level EV is “the last piece of the puzzle,” Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer noted last March after unveiling the ID. EVERY1 concept car.

Volkswagen remarked the production version will launch in 2027 with a starting price of around €20,000 ($22,000).

In a recent development, the latest model will sit below the ID. Polo in Volkswagen’s Electric Urban Car Family, a lineup of compact, affordable electric cars.

It has been revealed that volkswagen’s current entry-level EV lineup includes the ID. Polo, ID. Cross, the Cupra Raval, and Skoda Epiq, all based on its fresh MEB+ platform.

Sources indicate that after launching the lower-priced standard versions of the ID. Polo and ID. Cross recently, starting at €24,995 and €27,995, respectively, Volkswagen is preparing to launch an even smaller, more affordable EV next year.

A recent trademark filing with the European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO) and the German DPMA may have just revealed the name of VW’s upcoming €20,000 EV.

Volkswagen filed a trademark application for the name ID. UP on October 22, 2026, with the EUIPO and DPMA, suggesting this will be the name of the upcoming electric car in 2027.

It has been revealed that the trademark follows previous reports that VW planned to revive the former Up! name as part of its shift away from its previous numerical naming scheme (ID.3, ID.4, ID.5, etc.).

Volkswagen has kept most details a secret thus far. Like the ID. Polo, the first to go on sale with an established VW nameplate, the ID. UP is expected to use the same 37 kWh LFP battery to reduce costs.

Sources indicate that the VW ID. Polo with the 37 kWh battery offers a WLTP range of up to 334 km (207 miles), so the smaller ID. UP will likely provide around the same, if not slightly more.

Volkswagen noted it will offer at least 250 km (155 miles) of range. It will also use a new 70 kW (94 hp) electric motor, enabling a top speed of 130 km/h (80 mph).

The production version of the ID. EVERY1, expected to arrive as the ID. UP, will be one of nine new models VW plans to launch by 2027.

Volkswagen previously remarked the entry-level EV will be 3,880 mm long, which would position it between the former Up! (3,600 mm) and the ID. Polo (4,053 mm). Despite its compact size, VW said the electric city car will seat four passengers and offer a luggage compartment volume of 305 liters.

The VW Group’s latest Electric Urban Car Family is off to a strong start, securing nearly 150,000 orders after series production began in June.

All models within the family are built on the MEB+ platform with a FWD powertrain, and share more than 80% of the components and tech.

Volkswagen remarked the production version of the ID. EVERY1 will be among the first vehicles based on its zonal, software-defined vehicle (SDV) architecture, which it is developing through its joint venture with Rivian.

Ah, finally a car in the upper range of being meaningful and sensible.

It has been revealed that if someone needs more, then those are obviously special needs people. Being like can't enter and exit such a sensible car. Or like having to move the 15 horses of their 5 daughters. Or being a fieldworker driving a gazillion miles every day. Or requiring a lot of attention from lesser beings.

In March, the Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies (RV Tech) joint venture tested the new SDV architecture on the ID. EVERY1, alongside Audi and Scout reference vehicles, validating over-the-air (OTA) capabilities.

The newly introduced architecture will enable “highly automated driving features” and “advanced infotainment solutions,” with continuous OTA updates.

While VW noted it will deploy the SDV architecture in “electric vehicles across markets in the Western Hemisphere,” the entry-level EV is not expected to reach the States.

Sources indicate that volkswagen is, however, preparing to launch the ID. Tiguan, which will launch in 2027 as the successor to the ID.4 (and ID.5 in Europe).

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rinnai has launched a latest lineup of electric heat pump water heaters that adds wifi controls and more installation options to an appliance that can cut the energy needed for hot showers.
  • According to recent reports, the REHPW series comes in 50-, 65-, and 80-gallon sizes.
  • Heat pump water heaters pull heat from the surrounding air and transfer it into the tank.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rinnai has launched a latest lineup of electric heat pump water heaters that adds wifi controls and more installation options to an appliance that can cut the energy needed for hot showers.

According to recent reports, the REHPW series comes in 50-, 65-, and 80-gallon sizes. It builds on Rinnai’s existing REHP lineup, with changes designed to make the units easier to install, monitor, and maintain.

Heat pump water heaters pull heat from the surrounding air and transfer it into the tank. Moving that heat requires less electricity than producing it with conventional electric resistance elements. There’s no fuel combustion at the appliance, although emissions from its electricity supply depend on the grid.

In a recent development, rinnai lists a Uniform Energy Factor, or UEF, of 3.75 for the 50-gallon model and 4.0 for the two larger versions. Higher numbers mean greater efficiency under standardized testing; actual bills depend on electricity rates, hot water use, and installation conditions.

The lineup delivers up to 91 gallons of hot water in the first hour, depending on tank size. That rating includes both stored hot water and what the unit can heat during that hour – useful context when several people take consecutive showers.

There are five operating modes, 4.5 kW backup heating elements, and a variable-speed fan designed to keep noise down. The heat pump can operate with ambient air as low as 37°F.

Installation is where some of the more practical upgrades show up.

Sources indicate that the upcoming Rinnai heat pump water heater units have water connections on both the top and side, giving installers more options for connecting existing plumbing. Both the air intake and exhaust are on top, allowing zero side clearance where Rinnai’s installation requirements permit.

In a recent development, an optional ducting kit adds flexibility for tighter spaces. Carrying handles help with moving the tank into place, and the air filter slides out horizontally from the side for cleaning.

Rinnai has also added a third tank temperature sensor to the 50- and 80-gallon models to help manage hot water delivery.

Wifi adds remote monitoring and control. Rinnai’s updated Central app supports the REHPW series, including scheduling and tools to use time-of-use electricity rates to manage energy use.

The units also carry CTA-2045 AC Level 2 certification for demand response. That gives compatible utility programs a way to communicate with the water heater and adjust its electricity use. Rinnai claims the certification can help qualify homeowners for local and state utility demand-response rebates; availability depends on the program.

The series is Energy Star certified, meets NEEA Tier 4 requirements, and complies with California’s Title 24 requirements, including JA13, according to Rinnai. Warranty coverage includes 10 years for the tank and other parts, plus one year for labor.

Sources indicate that I’m very happy with my hybrid heat pump water heater. I run it in heat pump only mode in summer and it helps cool the house for free. For anyone on the fence, especially your utility offers a rebate, it’s definitely worth looking at.

Rinnai directs buyers to an installer for pricing, so the upfront cost – and how much a local rebate might offset it – will require a quote. However, the REHP series price on Amazon hovers around the $2,000 mark.

Industry observers note that we’ve spent a lot of time playing the game’s recent tests, and we’ve put together some early guides on how to get Roaming Oak Timber, how to unlock and upgrade hobbies and more. We also have a few cooking recipes to share with you.

Tesla Opens Self-Driving Cybercab Orders To 'Select Customers' At $29,990

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (858 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla will soon start selling its steering wheel-free Cybercab for personal use, the company announced on Friday.
  • According to recent reports, the Cybercab will cost $29,990, undercutting the Model 3 by $7,000 and making the golden two-seater Tesla's cheapest vehicle ever.
  • The Cybercab won't operate anywhere in the country, Tesla claims, but rather in "supported service areas." It will also require a $299-per-month autonomous driving subscription to operate, with the first month included for no charge.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla will soon start selling its steering wheel-free Cybercab for personal use, the company announced on Friday.

According to recent reports, the Cybercab will cost $29,990, undercutting the Model 3 by $7,000 and making the golden two-seater Tesla's cheapest vehicle ever. According to a screenshot of the order page shared by Tesla, deliveries will begin as soon as next month.

There are a few catches. The Cybercab won't operate anywhere in the country, Tesla claims, but rather in "supported service areas." It will also require a $299-per-month autonomous driving subscription to operate, with the first month included for no charge. That totals to some $3,600 per year just to use the vehicle, before insurance or maintenance costs.

It has been revealed that and the model will be sold to hand-picked buyers, at least to start. "Select customers are now being invited to purchase Cybercab for personal use," the manufacturer stated in a tweet on its Robotaxi X account. Tesla said initial availability is limited.

Industry observers note that it's not clear when or if sales will expand to the general public. But the sale of a car one can actually own that is capable of driving itself without supervision would be a massive milestone for both the automotive world and for Tesla in particular.

Sources indicate that putting autonomous cars in the hands of regular people has been one of Elon Musk's central promises for about a decade, and he's missed his self-imposed deadlines year after year. Meanwhile, today's driverless cars are owned and operated by companies running ride-hailing services, like Waymo, Zoox, and Tesla—not by individuals. The Cybercabs in operation today are part of Tesla's Robotaxi service, which opened for business last year and now shuttles riders around in a handful of U.S. cities, including Austin and Miami.

Recent findings suggest that tesla's biggest boosters online cheered the news. But it's also sure to tick off some of the many Tesla owners who have paid for Full Self-Driving over the years and have been waiting patiently for their Model 3s and Model Ys to become autonomous. Most recently, Musk remarked that will happen in the second quarter of next year in areas where the Robotaxi service operates.

The Tesla Cybercab has two seats and no steering wheel or pedals.

According to recent reports, tesla is far from the only company looking to sell autonomous cars to the public someday. Rivian aims to introduce lidar and a new in-house chip to the R2 in the hopes of giving it self-driving capability someday. General Motors plans to introduce an eyes-off version of Super Cruise to the Cadillac Escalade IQ in 2028. It'll operate on highways first before expanding to other road types, GM notes.

According to recent reports, tesla advertises the personally-owned Cybercab as "fully autonomous" and says owners will be able to monitor their vehicles and manage rides via the Tesla app. But overall, the announcement raises almost as many questions as it answers.

For example, there was no mention of whether customers would be able to add their cabs to the Robotaxi fleet and earn passive income, another longtime Musk promise. It's also not clear where the Cybercab will be able to operate, nor whether Tesla will expand that territory swiftly enough to make buying one worthwhile beyond a handful of cities.

Another cloud of uncertainty looming over the Cybercab's rollout is regulatory in nature. The Cybercab's unconventional design has caught the attention of the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, which questions how exactly Tesla determined that the vehicle complies with motor vehicle safety standards. The Tesla lacks a steering wheel, pedals, and side-view mirrors, all things that are typically required for a car to be street-legal.

The federal government lets companies apply to roll out noncompliant vehicles, but those deployments are capped at 2,500 vehicles per year. (Zoox, for its part, was recently granted an exemption to commercially deploy 5,000 of its autonomous pods over two years.) NHTSA has noted it's working to streamline autonomous-vehicle rules, which could work in Tesla's favor here.

In a recent development, if Tesla can pull this off, it'll be one for the history books. Of course, the company has made numerous ambitious promises around self-driving cars—like 1 million robotaxis by 2020, and unsupervised self-driving pretty much every year since—and it has generally fallen short. Whether the Cybercab rollout breaks that streak is still to be determined.

#5114. 10 Games That Made Me Weirdly Passionate About Jobs I'd Never Want

📅 15 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2179 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

10 Games That Made Me Weirdly Passionate About Jobs I'd Never Want

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2179 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, some of my favourite games are, when you really think about it, just jobs.
  • It has been revealed that the funny thing is that I wouldn't actually want any of these jobs.
  • Industry observers note that I had sunk many hours into both PowerWash Simulator games long before I ever held an actual pressure washer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, some of my favourite games are, when you really think about it, just jobs. I have pressure-washed patios, stamped passports, hauled cargo across half of Europe and sold second-hand books out of a trailer, all of it voluntarily and in my free time. And boy, did I take every single one of them seriously!

It has been revealed that the funny thing is that I wouldn't actually want any of these jobs. Some of them look like far too much hard work, others require a kind of patience I most definitely do not possess, and with one or two, I'm fairly certain I'd end up in prison. That is probably exactly what makes them so enjoyable from the safety of my sofa, so let's take a look at the ten games that made me weirdly passionate about jobs I'd never want.

Industry observers note that I had sunk many hours into both PowerWash Simulator games long before I ever held an actual pressure washer. That finally changed earlier this year, and I'm pleased to report that watching grime disappear is just as satisfying in real life as it is on screen. On a warm summer's day, it's even quite fun.

Sources indicate that still, there's a lot to be said for staying warm, dry and cozied up on the sofa whilst doing it. The game has an almost meditative quality that I couldn't quite find with a real hose in my hands, and that's no accident. Lead designer Nick McCarthy has said that the team left out certain real-world inconveniences on purpose, and I'm grateful for every single one of them.

According to recent reports, futurLab released the sequel on 23 October 2025, bringing 38 latest jobs to Muckingham, online co-op for up to four players and new tools like an abseiling rig and a cherry picker. There are also two kittens named Bubbles and Squeak, which was frankly all the convincing I needed. As an actual career, though, it looks like an awful lot of work, so I'll stick to the version without the wet socks.

Papers, Please's premise is incredibly dark and difficult: you are manning a booth at the border of the fictional Eastern Bloc country of Arstotzka. It's 1982, and as a border inspector, it is your responsibility to check passports, permits and anything else that gets slid across your desk. Make a mistake and you get a wage deduction. Your family, meanwhile, desperately needs that money. The game is, however, also tense and brilliant, and it also taught me that I would be entirely unsuited for the job.

In a recent development, quite frankly, I'm just not enough of a bootlicker for it. I'm far too nice, and my first instinct is to wave everybody through, which is not something Papers, Please looks kindly upon. Being generous with your stamp sooner or later gets you killed by your own government, and it's hard to build a career on that.

Note: Lucas Pope worked on the Uncharted series at Naughty Dog before making a game that's almost entirely about paperwork.

By its tenth anniversary in 2023, the game had sold over five million copies, so there are clearly plenty of people out there who are much better at saying no than I am. I have a lot of respect for them. I'd just rather not meet them at passport control.

Running a late-night coffee shop in an alternative version of Seattle sounds like a dream. Even more so when you consider that your visitors will consist of elves, orcs and mermaids that are living alongside humans. Coffee is the great connector here, since the need for a warm drink and someone to talk to is universal across every race. Toge Productions chose Seattle because Starbucks first opened there, and also because the rain sets the mood so well. It's easily one of the coziest games I own.

Parts of this job would actually suit me extremely well: I enjoy good banter, I'm perfectly happy with small talk, and I seem to have the kind of approachable face that makes strangers trauma dump on me far more often than you'd expect. If being a barista was only about listening, I'd be employee of the month.

According to recent reports, unfortunately, you also have to make the coffee, and Coffee Talk is the game that revealed me just how hilariously bad I am at latte art. Nothing I produce looks like it was made on purpose. So as much as I love the idea, I could never run a coffee shop of my own.

Note: Creator Mohammad Fahmi sadly passed away in March 2022. He pitched the game as holding a warm cup of coffee by a window whilst it rains outside and lo-fi music plays in the background, which is exactly how it feels.

Recent findings suggest that stardew Valley is meant to be about running a cute little farm with cute little animals on it. The way I play it, with spreadsheets at the ready and more wiki tabs open than I'd like to admit, has very little to do with that. My approach is a lot closer to a general planning a war than a farmer enjoying the countryside.

The forensic intensity I bring to this game does scare me a little. Every day is planned, every crop has to earn its place, and my poor character hasn't had a quiet afternoon in years. If I ran a real farm like that, I'd work myself into a burnout before the first harvest.

Note: Eric Barone, better known as ConcernedApe, made Stardew Valley on his own over roughly four years.

The game turned ten on 26 February 2026 and has sold around 50 million copies. I'd love to know how many of those players are peacefully watering their parsnips and enjoying the sunset, and how many are like me. I have my suspicions.

Something happens to me whenever I open Euro Truck Simulator 2. Within minutes, I turn into a 60-year-old trucker who has been doing this for decades, completely locked in, with nothing on my mind except my cargo and the motorway ahead. I can't explain it, but it awakens something in me.

According to recent reports, there are two wolves inside of me: One is a sweet softie, and the other one is a fourth-generation trucker that graduated from the school of hard knocks, living and breathing 18-wheelers. Sadly for the second wolf, I'm really, really bad at parking, and truth be told, I'm no better at it in the game. That feels like a bit of a dealbreaker for a job that ends with reversing a trailer into a loading bay.

According to recent reports, SCS Software first released the game at retail in autumn 2012, before it arrived on Steam on 16 January 2013. By its tenth birthday, it had sold over 13 million copies, and players had bought DLC more than 80 million times. Clearly, I'm not the only one with a trucker wolf, so at least I'm in good manufacturer.

Exterminauts is an upcoming co-op shooter from Behaviour Interactive, the studio behind Dead by Daylight, and it hands you several jobs at once. As part of a crew of three, you clock in, take on MegaCorp contracts, repair what's broken and exterminate alien pests along the way. It was revealed at gamescom Opening Night Live in August 2026 and is planned for 2027.

Anyone who has watched me deal with a woodlouse or a spider knows that pest control isn't my calling. I'm quite a caring person, so I had a lot of fun with the healing side of things. I've also discovered that I'm alarmingly quick to shoot my own teammates, sometimes because they were being annoying, and sometimes entirely by accident.

Note: Friendly fire is on in Exterminauts, and swinging one of the bigger weapons around carelessly is enough to take a teammate down.

According to recent reports, A colleague who keeps taking out the rest of the crew isn't much use to anyone, no matter how good her healing is. I can't imagine it going down well in a performance review, either. It's better for everyone if I stay off the payroll.

Sources indicate that subnautica is one of my favourite games of all time, which means I approach the deep ocean with a healthy dose of suspicion. Dave the Diver has done nothing but confirm that this is the correct attitude. You spend your days diving into the Blue Hole to catch fish, and the further down you go, the more things would like to eat you instead.

In a recent development, once the sun sets, the second job begins, and you help chef Bancho run the sushi restaurant, serving customers and keeping the drinks coming. All of that after a full day of nearly being eaten by sharks! I’d be a horrible sushi tester on the basis of not liking fish, and I could also never be the waiter on the basis of lacking a good sense of balance.

It has been revealed that note: The restaurant is the idea of Dave's friend Cobra, a former arms dealer who now handles the business side of things. Naturally.

According to recent reports, by September 2026, Dave the Diver had sold more than 10 million copies across all platforms, and I completely understand why. It's a wonderful game. It's also the best argument I've ever seen for staying on dry land and ordering takeaway.

Kerbal Space Program puts you in charge of a space program run by the Kerbals, little green aliens who are far braver than they have any right to be. You build rockets, launch them and watch most of them explode. I was oddly passionate about all of it, right up until the moment I finally made it into orbit.

I'm very aware that the game doesn't end there. It had taken me so long to reach that one milestone, though, that my passion fizzled out on the spot, and I decided that my work here was done. That's quite unusual for me, as I'm normally someone who needs to tick off every last goal.

Industry observers note that A real head of a space program with that attitude wouldn't bode well for anyone. NASA worked with developer Squad on an asteroid mission upgrade in 2014, and ESA followed with missions of its own in 2020, so the people who do this for a living are clearly made of sterner stuff than I am. I have a lot of respect for them, and I'm more than happy to watch from the ground.

According to recent reports, barbie Rewind was developed by Digital Eclipse, published by Atari and released on 12 November 2026. It is unfathomably fun. You get to decorate the DreamHouse with over 250 pieces of furniture and decor inspired by real Barbie playsets, from a classic pink vanity to a '90s inflatable chair. There are also 16 classic Barbie games from 1991 to 2007 included, one of which, Barbie: Vacation Adventure, had never been released before.

Truth be told, I think I'd make a good interior designer, and I think I'd enjoy it, too. In Barbie Rewind, you get to design to your heart's content, and nobody questions your choices. Ken, Teresa and Christie do pop in to ask for help, but none of them will ever tell you that your sofa is ugly.

Recent findings suggest that real clients are a different story. Even when something looks questionable at best, you have to go with the flow and keep them happy, and whilst you'd hope they trust your design decisions, there's absolutely no guarantee that they will. I don't think I have the temperament for that, and I'm fairly sure someone would end up wounded.

Recent findings suggest that in Tiny Bookshop, you leave everything behind to sell second-hand books out of a little trailer in the seaside town of Bookstonbury-by-the-Sea. Each morning, you pick a spot, stock your shelves and wait for the locals to wander in. Many of the books are real ones, which I love.

I've worked in retail before, I'm quite a good salesperson, and I enjoy helping people find what they're looking for. The customers in Tiny Bookshop put that to the test, because a fair few of them behave as if it's their very first day on Earth. Not all of them, mind you, but enough of them describe the book they want so vaguely that it borders on nonsensical.

On top of that, everyone in town seems to need a favour. Community is vital, of course, but I'm trying to run a bookshop here, and I'd quite like to be left alone to do it! Over half a million players have fallen in love with Tiny Bookshop, and it won three German Developer Awards in 2025, so this one might just be a me problem. I'd still end up scaring all of my customers away.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla is now inviting “select customers” to buy a Cybercab for personal use at $29,990, but the car won’t move unless you also pay $299 a month for an “Autonomy Subscription.”.
  • And it only works inside Tesla’s Robotaxi service areas in Texas and Florida, the same geofences that have turned out to be significantly smaller than what Tesla advertises.
  • Tesla’s official Robotaxi account revealed the invites on X on Friday with screenshots of the order page and the invitation email.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla is now inviting “select customers” to buy a Cybercab for personal use at $29,990, but the car won’t move unless you also pay $299 a month for an “Autonomy Subscription.”.

And it only works inside Tesla’s Robotaxi service areas in Texas and Florida, the same geofences that have turned out to be significantly smaller than what Tesla advertises.

Tesla’s official Robotaxi account revealed the invites on X on Friday with screenshots of the order page and the invitation email.

Sources indicate that the order page lists the Cybercab at $29,990 before taxes, with an estimated delivery of December 2026 in Austin, Texas. You need to put down a $1,000 non-refundable deposit to order.

Sources indicate that the subscription isn’t optional. It’s pre-checked on the order page at $299 per month, with one month included, and the fine print states “Subscription and regular vehicle maintenance required to operate.”.

The email is even more direct. Its asterisk reads: “Only available in supported service areas. Subscription required for operation.”.

The rest is what we already knew. Two seats, a 21-inch center touchscreen, 20.1 cubic feet of cargo space, and no steering wheel or pedals. Tesla calls it “fully autonomous” and states you’ll “manage your ride in the app.”.

Musk had promised a Cybercab “below $30,000” when he unveiled it in 2024. He technically hit it. He just didn’t mention the $3,588 a year it takes to use it. Over five years, that’s about $47,600 for a two-seater, before insurance, maintenance, taxes, and charging.

Recent findings suggest that tesla runs its Robotaxi service in eight cities: Austin, Dallas, Houston, Fort Worth, and San Antonio in Texas, and Miami, Orlando, and Tampa in Florida. That’s where a Cybercab can operate. Everywhere else, it’s a $30,000 sculpture in your driveway.

According to recent reports, and those service areas aren’t what Tesla says they are. Independent tracker Koby Pierce tested thousands of addresses in the Robotaxi app and found that the areas where Tesla actually accepts pickups and drop-offs are only 59% to 78% of the advertised geofences in the six cities he checked. In Austin, the very city where Tesla is delivering these cars, it’s about 59%.

It has been revealed that railroad crossings are a massive reason why. In Houston, the creator of Robotaxi Tracker found the app quoting about 40 minutes to go two blocks downtown because the vehicle appeared to route around rail crossings. Tesla also lists San Antonio’s airport inside its polygon but doesn’t serve it.

Then there’s the regulatory cloud. NHTSA has ordered Tesla to prove under oath that a car with no brake pedal meets federal safety standards that require one. Tesla answered on October 30 and asked that the entire response be kept confidential. NHTSA hasn’t ruled. Tesla is now selling the car to consumers anyway.

I think this is going to be a total mess. It looks like Tesla is only doing this by invitation and delivering it in Austin to prove they can deliver an “unsupervised” vehicle in 2026.

Tesla is going to sell these to fans who are excited about owning a self-driving car, and many of them will find out the limitations aren’t worth $299 a month on top of a $30,000 car.

According to recent reports, sure, if your monthly Uber bill is well over $300 and you live and work deep inside the geofence, maybe the math works on paper. Until you realize you have to park it somewhere once you get to your destination. Or that it can’t take you to a friend’s place two neighborhoods over. Or that a 15-minute drive turns into an hour because the car won’t cross a train track. With an Uber or a Waymo, that’s someone else’s problem. With a Cybercab, you’re paying for the privilege.

No point trying to calculate what it will cost over X years. Tesla can change that monthly fee at will anyway (and shall be expected to, considering their overall pricing history).

And here’s the part that makes no sense to me. The Cybercab runs on the same AI4 computer as the current Model Y. Tesla already runs unsupervised Model Y Robotaxis in these same geofences. So why can’t the Model Y owners who already paid for “Full Self-Driving” get unsupervised operation in those same zones? Wouldn’t be even easier to turn that on these vehicles which have accumulated much more data? Tesla keeps pushing that to “next year,” at the moment around Q2 2027, while asking people to buy a new two-seater that can do nothing else.

Sources indicate that if the tech works unsupervised in Austin, turn it on for the Model Y owners in Austin. If it doesn’t, why should anyone pay $47,000 over five years for a car that only works where Tesla notes it does?

Like with every other Tesla product lately, the delivered version is going to be a lot more disappointing than the one that was sold on stage.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, vince Zampella, known for co-creating the Call of Duty series, among many other roles, has died.
  • In a recent development, according to NBC, Zampella’s Ferrari hit a concrete barrier after leaving a tunnel in the San Gabriel Mountains, north of Los Angeles.
  • Vince Zampella is one of the industry’s most prolific creators.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, vince Zampella, known for co-creating the Call of Duty series, among many other roles, has died. Zampella, 55, died in a car crash in Los Angeles on Sunday. The fatal crash killed him, along with the occupant of his car.

In a recent development, according to NBC, Zampella’s Ferrari hit a concrete barrier after leaving a tunnel in the San Gabriel Mountains, north of Los Angeles. Zampella was unfortunately trapped in an ensuing car fire, and the passenger was ejected.

Vince Zampella is one of the industry’s most prolific creators. His storied career is long, and is responsible for some of the biggest shooter franchises in history. It started with Medal of Honor in the 90s, a game that changed WW2 shooters forever.

Industry observers note that zampella later co-founded the legendary Infinity Ward in 2002, the team that would go on to redefine multiplayer shooters forever. Infinity Ward is the studio responsible for the Call of Duty series, which remains one of the biggest games for publisher Activision, and the entire industry.

It has been revealed that zampella then left the studio he founded in 2010 following a major fallout with Activision. He, along with longtime collaborator, Jason West, went to rival publisher EA to form Respawn Entertainment.

In a recent development, respawn went on to create the Titanfall series, and later Apex Legends. The studio is responsible for non-shooters, of course, like the third-person action game series Star Wars Jedi. Zampella was instrumental in making the game possible, having hired God of War 3 director Stig Asmussen to helm a team within Respawn out of a desire to diversify the studio’s output and prove he can do more than make shooters.

Industry observers note that zampella had only recently met with journalists and peers at The Game Awards, where Battlefield 6 was nominated for multiple awards. Battlefield 6 is the most successful game in series history, in part as a result of Zampella’s leadership. The legendary leader was given the reigns of the struggling multiplayer shooter franchise in 2021, with a goal of finding a viable future.

Zampella’s sudden death has shaken the industry, and many mourn his loss as the news started spreading.

“We are heartbroken by the loss of Vince Zampella, a creative leader whose work shaped generations of players and helped define what modern shooters and action games could be,” EA said in a statement.

Industry observers note that “While his impact reached far beyond any one game or studio, we will remember Vince for how he indicated up every day, trusting his teams, encouraging bold ideas, and believing in Battlefield and the people building it. We are deeply grateful for his leadership, his generosity, and the care he brought to everything he touched, and we will carry that forward with us.”.

#5111. Diesel Prices Are Surging. This Electric Trucking Firm Is Seeing More Interest

📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (732 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Insideevs ↗ Open Full Page

Diesel Prices Are Surging. This Electric Trucking Firm Is Seeing More Interest

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (732 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that high gas prices have helped drive more interest in electric cars this year.
  • Eye-watering diesel costs are pushing more shippers to consider a switch to electric trucks, Roozbeh Charli, CEO of electric and autonomous freight firm Einride, told me in an interview.
  • “You’re definitely seeing an upswing in both customer conversations and just general narrative” around electrification, he stated.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that high gas prices have helped drive more interest in electric cars this year. But it’s not just everyday drivers who are looking to ditch fossil fuels.

Eye-watering diesel costs are pushing more shippers to consider a switch to electric trucks, Roozbeh Charli, CEO of electric and autonomous freight firm Einride, told me in an interview.

“You’re definitely seeing an upswing in both customer conversations and just general narrative” around electrification, he stated.

Diesel prices have risen far more severely than prices for regular gasoline, putting extra pressure on commercial operators. The average cost of diesel in the U.S. has shot up by more than 60% since the war with Iran began, to over $6 per gallon. Shippers are facing far higher fuel costs in Europe too. It all means customers who told Einride they’d revisit the idea of electric freight sometime down the line are deciding to get the ball rolling.

“A lot of those customers are coming back now, saying ‘let’s get started, rather sooner than later,’” Charli stated.

Sources indicate that there’s some evidence that those conversations are generating actual business. Einride, which was founded in 2016 and sells electric freight services and software, states its sales pipeline tripled year over year during the first half of 2026. Its conversion rate doubled over the same period.

And it isn’t the only one noticing an uptick in demand. In September, a coalition of shippers like PepsiCo placed an order for 2,500 electric trucks in a deal that’s set to double the U.S. fleet of electric Class 8 trucks. Catalyst Mobility, one of the nonprofits running the program, has stated it’s noticed more interest in EV trucks from companies that weren’t involved in the deal due to diesel prices.

Charli chalks the increased interest up to a couple of things. The pricing pain today is part of it. It means there’s a broader range of customer use cases where electric trucks are price-competitive with, or cheaper than, using traditional substantial-rigs. Those are typically what he calls “middle-mile” applications of, say, 100-200 miles back and forth, with high utilization. That last part is key, since battery-powered trucks still tend to cost more than diesel ones.

The situation is also making some companies realize just how exposed they are to drastic swings in the price of diesel, Charli said.

Our weekly newsletter breaks down the biggest mobility news every Friday.

The trend is encouraging for reasons beyond economics. Heavy-duty trucks make up a relatively small portion of the U.S. fleet, but they account for a disproportionate share of fuel consumption and harmful air pollution.

“Any exposure to diesel exhaust is going to be harmful to your health,” indicates Ray Minjares, heavy-duty vehicles program director at the International Council on Clean Transportation. “And so since there's really no safe level, the obvious solution, particularly in a world where commercial zero-emission vehicles are already available, is to switch to that technology.”.

The Tesla Semi represents a "step-change" for electric trucking hardware in the U.S., Einride CEO Roozbeh Charli said.

Sources indicate that high diesel prices aren’t the only tailwind helping to drive trucking electrification this year, Charli said. The long-awaited launch of the Tesla Semi not only helped bring more attention to electric trucking, but it also introduced a genuinely groundbreaking offering to the U.S. market, he said.

“The Tesla Semi, in a U.S. context, is definitely a step-change in the capabilities of the hardware” in terms of range, performance, and price, he mentioned.

In August, Einride unveiled aims to deploy 500 Semis to service Amazon and other North American customers, tripling its fleet. Tesla’s truck is several years late to full-scale production. But given the diesel situation these days, maybe it’s right on time.

“They timed it well,” Charli noted.

#5110. I finally got a USB-C charging e-bike, and it costs 75% less than Rivian’s bike

📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1024 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

I finally got a USB-C charging e-bike, and it costs 75% less than Rivian’s bike

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1024 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I’ve been waiting years for electric bikes to finally embrace USB-C charging.
  • Meet the ENGWE Zip, a quirky little folding electric bike that costs just €999 and has quickly become one of my favorite examples of how a small feature can make a big difference.
  • When it debuted earlier this year, it became only the third production e-bike I’ve seen that could charge via USB-C, allowing it to use the same charger that is likely already shared by your phone and laptop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’ve been waiting years for electric bikes to finally embrace USB-C charging. We’ve already standardized much of our lives around the convenient little connector, from phones and laptops to tablets and countless other gadgets. But for some reason, electric bikes have largely missed the memo. Now, though, I’m finally riding an e-bike that charges with USB-C, and the best part is that it doesn’t cost an arm and a leg.

Meet the ENGWE Zip, a quirky little folding electric bike that costs just €999 and has quickly become one of my favorite examples of how a small feature can make a big difference.

When it debuted earlier this year, it became only the third production e-bike I’ve seen that could charge via USB-C, allowing it to use the same charger that is likely already shared by your phone and laptop.

USB-C charging on electric bikes isn’t entirely latest, but it’s surprisingly rare. Ampler was one of the first companies to introduce it barely a year ago, though its bikes are sadly no longer in production after the firm’s bankruptcy. More recently, Rivian’s ALSO electric bike arrived with USB-C charging, but that bike costs around $4,500 – at least if you want the model that’s slowly starting to ship.

In a recent development, the ENGWE Zip, on the other hand, costs roughly a quarter as much as its only USB-charging competition. At €999, it’s priced at a relatively affordable US$1,100. That’s a quarter of the cost of the only other USB-C charging e-bike on the market.

In a recent development, of course, it’s not nearly as technologically advanced as Rivian’s ALSO e-bike. But hey, it’s at least shipping.

And while the Zip is a fun little 16″ wheel folding electric bike in its own right, with a compact design that makes it easy to store and transport, it’s the charging setup that has me particularly excited.

Instead of keeping track of yet another proprietary charging brick, I can simply grab the USB-C charger from my laptop and plug it into the bike. There’s one in my living room by the couch. There’s one by my bed. There’s one in all of my friends’ places. There’s a USB-C charger everywhere.

If I’m traveling around, that means one less charger to pack. If I’m visiting someone, there’s a decent chance they already have a compatible charger sitting around.

Industry observers note that heck, I can even use a basic USB-C phone charger in a pinch. Sure, charging a relatively large e-bike battery at 20W isn’t going to be particularly quick, but the fact that I can do it at all is incredibly convenient.

In a recent development, plus, the bike has one more trick. The battery also outputs USB-C, so I can charge my laptop or other devices from it as well. I can even charge two devices simultaneously, thanks to the dual USB-C ports.

Sources indicate that the battery is housed in a roll-top bag that is locked into the headset of the bike but can be rapidly unlocked for charging off the bike. And since it’s a keyed lock, no one can steal the battery even when the bag is left on the bike.

I typically charge the battery still mounted on the bike, though occasionally when I want to use a friend’s USB-C charger, I’ll just pop the bag off and bring it right up to wherever the closest USB-C charger is located.

Industry observers note that it may not be the fastest charge, but it’s pretty darn convenient. And with a 360Wh battery, a powerful 100W laptop charger will still get it pretty much full in 4 hours, or for a more typical 50% recharge, roughly two hours.

And that’s really the beauty of USB-C charging. It’s not necessarily about charging faster. It’s about having options. It’s about not being stuck if the very specific charger that only works on your e-bike doesn’t happen to be around exactly where you are.

Industry observers note that of course, there’s a technical reason we haven’t seen USB-C charging spread across the e-bike industry quite as quickly as it has with smaller electronics. Most e-bike batteries operate at 36V or 48V nominal, meaning their charging voltages are higher than the 20V typically supplied by common USB-C laptop chargers. That requires additional voltage conversion and charging circuitry inside the bike or battery.

But clearly, it can be done. And if ENGWE can offer it on a €999 electric bike, there’s a pretty compelling argument that more manufacturers should be taking a serious look at the technology. In this case, it’s all housed inside the battery, meaning it could be directly incorporated into any e-bike whose manufacturer is brave enough to spec it.

According to recent reports, I’m not suggesting that every e-bike needs to abandon its dedicated charger tomorrow. For larger batteries, high-powered chargers still make plenty of sense, especially when you want to get back on the road swiftly.

But having USB-C as an additional charging option? That’s something I’d love to see become standard.

For years, we’ve seen how electric bikes are becoming more convenient, more practical, and better integrated into our everyday lives. Yet when it comes to charging, we’re still carrying around a collection of more or less proprietary chargers.

It has been revealed that now I’m riding a barely $1k electric bike that can charge from the same power brick as my laptop. And frankly, I think it’s about time the rest of the e-bike industry caught up!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, tesla drivers can now seamlessly charge their electric cars at Ioona Rechargeries using a feature called Autocharge, as reported by State of Charge. With Autocharge, EVs can simply be plugged in, and the session will start automatically, without the driver having to do anything. Billing is also handled automatically, but a one-time setup needs to be completed to enable the functionality to work in the background.

In Tesla and Ionna’s case, a third-party smartphone application is needed to get started, as the charging network doesn’t have its own app. Drivers need to download and set up the Presto Charging app, which bundles over 190,000 chargers across the United States.

Sources indicate that the setup involves creating an account with Presto Charging, scanning the car’s VIN for validation, and manually starting the first charging session in the app. While the initial charging session is active, an “Enable Autocharge” option will appear on the screen, which needs to be confirmed by the driver.

After this initial learning session, charging at Ionna locations will start automatically, and the driver’s payment method will be used to pay for the dispensed energy automatically.

According to recent reports, to be clear, Presto Charging’s Autocharge function is not the same as Plug & Charge, even though it works in a similar way. With Plug & Charge, the EV communicates directly with the charger using a digital certificate, while Autocharge uses the car’s charging port network address to identify the vehicle and authorize it with a specific charger. In this case, the Presto Charging app takes the car’s information, checks it, and passes it to the charger, which starts the charging session.

Ionna Rechargeries feature CCS and NACS connectors.

Recent findings suggest that plug & Charge is generally regarded as being a more secure option, but Presto Charging claims it constantly monitors sessions to prevent any problems. For instance, if the same vehicle appears as charging in a different location than the charger, the platform can flag it and fix it. Presto Charging handles all of the charging history and user data, which could be useful, considering Ionna doesn’t offer a way of keeping track of charging stops at its stations.

To make the feature more appealing to Tesla owners, the first session using Autocharge at Ionna is free. After that, pricing will be similar to Ionna’s regular offering, though it’s crucial to note that Presto Charging will get a small share to keep the lights on and squash any potential bugs. Other automakers have enabled Plug & Charge at Ionna, and drivers can use the card terminals at all stations to pay for charging.

It’s an important step for Ionna, which is still small compared to Tesla’s own Supercharger network, but has made significant progress when it comes to the quality of charging sessions. According to J.D. Power’s latest driver satisfaction survey, Ionna ranked first, and it’s hardly surprising, given how we’ve always had great experiences with the organization’s chargers. They always work, they’re fast, and there are clean amenities nearby.

Recent findings suggest that last month, Ionna opened its 200th station, marking a huge milestone for the up-and-coming firm. In total, the network now has over 1,600 ports across the country—double compared to seven months ago—and it’s not slowing down. No fewer than 80 fresh locations are under construction, and more are planned.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • And Tesla wants consumers to sign it while still refusing to give unsupervised self-driving to the Model Y owners it has been selling “Full Self-Driving” to for nearly a decade.
  • The “Cybercab Autonomy Subscription Agreement” (version 20261112) went up on Tesla’s configurator late Friday, hours after the tech giant started inviting select customers to order the Cybercab for personal use at $29,990 plus a mandatory $299 per month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that tesla has posted the agreement that comes with its $29,990 Cybercab, and it’s even worse than the order page suggested. The two-seater can’t move without a $299 monthly “Autonomy Subscription” that Tesla can reprice with a month’s notice, suspend for a week, or cut off entirely.

And Tesla wants consumers to sign it while still refusing to give unsupervised self-driving to the Model Y owners it has been selling “Full Self-Driving” to for nearly a decade.

The “Cybercab Autonomy Subscription Agreement” (version 20261112) went up on Tesla’s configurator late Friday, hours after the tech giant started inviting select customers to order the Cybercab for personal use at $29,990 plus a mandatory $299 per month.

The key line is short: “Your Cybercab will not operate without an active Autonomy Subscription.” There’s no steering wheel and no pedals, so that isn’t a figure of speech. Stop paying and you have a $30,000 object in your garage.

That personal-use clause kills the whole pitch. For years, Musk told people they’d buy a Tesla, add it to the fleet, and make money while they sleep. The first Tesla sold to consumers for unsupervised operation is contractually barred from doing exactly that.

Then there’s the geofence. Tesla’s Robotaxi service areas are already smaller in practice than advertised: when we tested them, real coverage was between 59% and 78% of the advertised maps, and parts of the Houston map have been called “fake” by the person tracking it. Now Tesla reserves the right to shrink that area after you’ve paid for the car.

Mark Valorian, who went through the terms on X, summed it up as “an endless variable-rate lease with a ridiculous down payment.” That’s about right.

Over five years, the car plus 59 paid months of subscription comes to $47,631 before insurance, registration, charging, and taxes, all of which are on the owner.

This is the part that should make every Tesla owner angry.

Tesla has spent the last year telling everyone that its Model Y is just as much a robotaxi as the Cybercab. Ahead of the Robotaxi launch in Austin, Musk stated the cars were “the Model Ys we make currently, there’s no change to it.” On Tesla’s Q3 2026 earnings call last month, AI chief Ashok Elluswamy said Cybercabs and Model Y robotaxis already run the same software, and that customer cars might join the network around Q2 2027. The Cybercab debuts on the same AI4 computer found in the current Model Y.

So the hardware is the same, the software is the same, and unsupervised Model Ys are already operating in the exact geofences where Cybercab owners will be allowed to ride.

Yet the people who paid for it get nothing. Tesla started selling “Full Self-Driving Capability” in 2016 on the promise that every car it built had the hardware for it. Owners paid up to $15,000 for the package. In February, Tesla stopped selling it outright and moved to a $99 per month subscription, which still requires you to supervise the car at all times.

Tesla’s answer to all those owners is a new car. One with two seats, no controls, a geofence it can move whenever it wants, and a subscription that costs three times as much as FSD.

I’ll say it plainly: this car is for suckers who want to give their money to Elon Musk.

Recent findings suggest that you don’t own a Cybercab in any meaningful sense. You pay $30,000 for the right to keep paying Tesla $299 a month, at a price Tesla can raise, in an area Tesla can shrink, under rules Tesla enforces, with a camera pointed at you the whole time.

There are three possible reasons Tesla isn't allowing model Y owners to use FSD in the allowed zones:.

1: the robotaxis are in fact different from the model Ys being sold.

2: Tesla doesn't have enough "remote operators" to cover all of those supposedly self-driving cars if users join the network.

3: Tesla isn't willing to accept liability when FSD kills someone.

In a recent development, and the Model Y part is what gives the game away. If Tesla truly believed its unsupervised system was ready for customers, the obvious move would be to turn it on for the Model Y owners in Austin who already paid for it. It’s the same computer and the same software in the same geofence. But that would mean honoring a promise made in 2016, on cars already sold, with no new revenue attached.

A new vehicle wipes that slate clean. No legacy FSD buyers, no HW3 baggage, just a fresh customer locked into a $299 monthly fee from day one. What Tesla built is a subscription with a $30,000 entry fee attached to it.

So what happens the first time Tesla emails Cybercab owners a month’s notice that the price is going to $399?

For one, this is the first time all five of them are brought together. The patch is also adding some important latest features, alongside anniversary events, and more.

Throne of Eros also doubles as the fresh Wish Pool, which is the one that has all of the game’s love interests in a single banner. This is a limited-time affair, of course, but it’s not the only thing you should look forward to here.

The even bigger news is that you can target your Wishes through the Xspace Echo, which lets you select five Memories to create your own pool from. You can use this to get any Memories you might not have, of course.

On the topic of Memories, you’ll also be able to unlock new second anniversary KV Memories, as part of a Yearly Highlights Event that will let you look back on your own journey with the game over the past year.

It has been revealed that on the story and narrative side, Throne of Eros adds two upcoming main stories, with new branches for Xavier, and Rafayel. There’s even a narrative-specific event that will run throughout the anniversary period, through which you can earn two daily outfits for each of the five love interests.

The celebrations also extend to new anniversary content like mail, and video calls. You can purchase a Yearly Pass, and check out some new arrivals at the Lunar Shop.

Beyond the anniversary content, version 5.0 also adds a newly introduced feature to the game: Home, which essentially offers a hub to get you directly to interacting with love interests that doesn’t have to do with combat or story.

You can also expect various other quality of life updates that touch on the Journal, Phone Moments Search, Resources Quick Cleanup, and latest Tete-a-Tete that should make interacting with all of them more streamlined.

Sources indicate that have you recently started playing Elemental Powers Tycoon and are unsure which powers are the best? Well, you’re in luck because our Elemental Powers Tycoon tier list will assist you in figuring this out. We have rated all powers from S to D, with S being the highest and D the lowest. This tier list lets you focus on mastering powerful characters and avoid struggling with the lower-tier options. We've added a description for each character to help you understand the reasoning behind their ranking.

Industry observers note that elemental Powers Tycoon is an enjoyable Roblox game that draws inspiration from various anime, merging the typical tycoon format with powers acquired using money. The developers made the skins of their characters resemble famous figures from many anime series and movies, including Naruto, One Piece, and HxH.

Sources indicate that additionally, I’ll be incorporating numerous anime references. If I’ve overlooked any anime or characters, please let me know in the comments.

Now, let’s jump straight to the tier list.

Thunder Thunder is among the super-broken characters in EPT and sports a Killua-like appearance. It’s understandable why it’s OP; it has an exciting and all-around kit with damage and a long-duration stun. Even though you can fly around on Nimbus like Goku, there’s no Kamehameha. Instead, you have a flashy and strong thunder attack that can one-shot almost everyone, which is sufficient to rank the character at the top of our Elemental Powers Tycoon tier list. Time This character can stop time and slow down enemies, holding an exciting kit of skills and well-balanced damage. He is among the most OP champs, although the S-tier rank is for the excellent invisibility skill. You can go unnoticed by your adversary for a short time, making for a comeback moment in every fight if used strategically. If you are into time manipulation and want to become the invisible man, here’s your chance. Nature Hashirama is the master of nature manipulation, an influential figure from the Naruto series. In the game, he is famous for his wood and tree attacks. One of his skills is the ability to pull any enemy in a specific direction, which you can use to drag them into your deadly attack range. I also consider the damage high, which makes him easily qualified for the S tier. Technology Now we have my favourite character, and you will understand why once you try technology. He has the best skill kit with high damage output. The sword he holds can throw projectiles every third strike with no cooldown, and he can summon two large hexagon-shaped cells that fire towards the cursor’s position. But these are not the only perks! You can summon a turret that knocks enemies around, levitates, and becomes invulnerable to damage while being able to cast skills. And finally, create a tesseract that sucks in anyone approaching it to deal 63 damage over nine pulses. This character is your best pick if you want to dominate EPT easily. Bones Bones is another OP champ, well-known for having almost average skill damage, but that one “jealousy” skill that can one-shot everyone sets the bar high to be in the S tier. I would recommend it for those who want to abuse one skill and get the most out of their kills.

Industry observers note that darkness2024-03-05 Darkness is powerful right now. If you’re a Madara Uchiha wannabe, you will enjoy this pick. The kit resembles purple shadows and the special Giant Hand move that pulls opponents underneath. Catching someone in it is an inevitable knockout. There’s also the ability to teleport forward for a surprising attack or to dodge enemy overkill skills. Overall, darkness is considered strong, but it is not the best choice. The downside is that it’s hard to hit your main skill, which makes winning a gamble. Light Light is Admiral Kisaru from One Piece. All fans of the series will recognise them instantly. The character has a fantastic set of skills and abilities. You can run fast, teleport, and damage your enemies significantly. Remember that high mobility is necessary in this game, and people who can master this character will also be hard to kill. Space Space, represented by an astronaut’s skin, is an above-average character with a mix of solid and weak weapons. However, it made it easy to reach the A tier thanks to the UFO skill and the significant damage some of his guns inflict. Another downside is his melee weapon, which is not the best to swing around. Devil Denji represents the devil from the Chainsaw Man series. Boasting above-average skills made it easy to get into the A-tier list. The damage and the mobility skills are well-balanced. The character mainly focuses on wielding a devil sword that deals hellfire damage over three cycles, teleporting in the cursor's direction, inflicting damage upon landing, and throwing puddles of black fluid as projectiles. Devil is very entertaining and strong at the same time. However, why not in the S tier? The answer is simple: I’m considering how tough it is the land some skills. Venom Venom is a toxic character, as the name implies. He uses poison, which deals continuous damage and empowers attacks. He holds a stun ability, self-buff (health and speed) and bubbling venom, which covers a wide area. The character is a good choice, with many players already invested in mastering him. The melee damage could be better, and is the only downside of this character.

Ice Ice, a character as cold as Esdeath, has the most exciting skill in their stun, which limits the enemy's mobility and jump power. It is super-efficient against high-mobility tycoons. However, it does come without a downside. The skill set doesn’t hit hard for overkill, and she lacks burst damage, making her a laid-back character requiring patience. She is undoubtedly the best pick if you’re into that play style, however. Gravity Admiral Issho represents gravity from One Piece, but this time, the character is in the okay-ish category. It has some good stuff and skills, but remains in the B tier if we talk about the best powers, as other Tycoons could easily overpower it. The other downside is his firepower hitbox, which is hard to land and needs to be more dominant on the battlefield. Crystal We place Crystal in the B category, the epitome of average characters, because her kill options aren’t as deadly as they should be, making it a bit hard to deal with enemies. The more you play her, the more you discover how challenging she is to use. Supersonic Supersonic is all about speed and hitting from a distance. His moves include Sonic Blaster for ranged damage, Sonic Barrage for a quick burst of projectiles, and Sonic Twister to zip around the map. He’s a great pick if you like fast, agile play rather than relying on raw power or heavy crowd control.

In a recent development, fire Fire is somewhat useless, as sadly represented by Naruto, but it has one of the best skins in the game. The number of combos you must do to defeat someone is tremendously annoying. I wouldn't recommend this character if you are seriously trying to beat some enemies. It's only a good choice if you're entirely into aesthetics.

In a recent development, earth Earth is low because you have to be lucky to hit your skills. It’s hard to use since the hitboxes are small and your range is short, so you must get close to your opponent. Even if you miraculously land some hits, they won’t be deadly enough to eliminate your adversary, which is annoying. It's not my cup of tea, but feel free to try him out.

According to recent reports, that’s all for our Elemental Powers Tycoon tier list. I hope it is helpful for all the newbies and veterans alike. I'll patch it accordingly as the meta changes, which it surely will. Until then, have fun and keep an eye on similar content like our Anime Dimensions tier list, Blade Ball ability tier list and Ultimate Tower Defense tier list.

Genshin Impact’s latest Special Program has spilled all the beans on the game’s next major patch, Luna 4. The update, which arrives on January 14, kicks off 2026 with several bits of latest content, including some previously-teased characters.

Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.

Recent findings suggest that the first latest arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden. Columbina is a 5-Star Hydro Catalyst wielder. Her kit revolves around supporting the squad via Lunar Reactions. She can trigger coordinated Lunar Reaction DMG, even when she’s off the field.

Recent findings suggest that the Moon Maiden’s special ability, Lunar Domain, further boosts all Lunar Reactions by applying a DMG bonus, including summoning more thundercloud strikes for Lunar-Charged reactions. Columbina is also capable of converting Electro-Charged, Bloom, and Hydro Crystallize reactions into Lunar Reactions, as well as revive fallen squad members.

Speaking of elemental reactions, new in this version is Lunar-Crystallize, a new reaction that’s triggered when Geo meets Hydro (under certain conditions). When triggered, Lunar-Crystallize summons three Moondrifts near enemies. When triggered three times, Moondrift Harmony gets activated, dealing Geo DMG to enemies caught in its radius.

It has been revealed that then there’s Zibai, an Adeptus from Liyue. Zibai is another 5-Star character, a Geo Sword wielder. Zibai can, through entering a special state where they can build up energy, unleash an Elemental Skill that deals Lunar-Crystallize DMG.

The longer the fight goes on, the more Lunar-Crystallize reactions are triggered, the higher (and more often) the damage of Zibai’s Elemental Skill becomes.

Sources indicate that luna 4 continues the Nod-Krai story arc, with a big confrontation with Il Dottore. This is the focus of the newly introduced Archon Quest, completing which will earn you a new outfit. There’s a gameplay element to that new chapter, too, with the reveal of Piramida, a new area north of the region. Piramida is the headquarters of the Lightkeepers.

The first phase of Luna 4’s Event Wishes will, unsurprisingly, feature Columbina. It’ll also include reruns of Ineffa. The second phase is when Zibai becomes available, alongside another newcomer: Illuga, a 4-Star, polearm-wielding Geo Lightkeeper. The second phase’s rerun will be Neuvillette, who’s also going to have a upcoming outfit in the shop at a discount.

It has been revealed that version Luna 4 brings back the annual Lantern Rite event, taking place in the mainland of Liyue. The event features its own set of minigames with unique rewards, alongside new stories of the Adepti.

In a recent development, all around Liyue Harbor, you’ll be able to place Xiao Lanterns and inscribe them with messages for others to read. You’ll also earn some Fortune Coins from Auspicious Treasure Trees, which you can later exchange for gifts.

Finally, you can look forward to the newly introduced Classic Mode in Miliastra Wonderland, which lets you invite select Teyvat characters to join you.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • With the standard 18-inch wheels, the crossover gets an 8% bump in range, but with the optional 19-inch wheels, the base-spec Model Y can now cover up to 335 miles, a 10% increase.
  • It’s unclear what Tesla did to improve the range of the most affordable Model Y, but one thing is certain: the price.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla has increased the estimated range for its most affordable Model Y trim. The 2027 Tesla Model Y Rear-Wheel Drive is now listed on the American company’s website as being capable of driving up to 348 miles on a full charge, up from 321 miles before.

With the standard 18-inch wheels, the crossover gets an 8% bump in range, but with the optional 19-inch wheels, the base-spec Model Y can now cover up to 335 miles, a 10% increase.

It’s unclear what Tesla did to improve the range of the most affordable Model Y, but one thing is certain: the price. Just like before, the entry-level crossover starts at $41,630. The range change is not yet reflected on the EPA’s website, which still lists the old 321-mile rating, but that will likely change in the future, as the company submits newly introduced paperwork.

Industry observers note that the longer range brings the most affordable Model Y just seven miles shy of the more expensive Premium trim’s estimated driving distance. The Model Y Premium costs $6,000 more and offers faster acceleration, slightly more range, a revised exterior design, and a more upmarket interior.

Features like an FM radio, heated rear seats, a rear passenger display, adaptive high beams, and frequency-dependent shock absorbers can only be had on the Premium or higher trims. The entry-level Model Y also comes with a glass roof that’s covered by a one-piece headliner.

Sources indicate that this is just the latest reshuffle of Tesla’s lineup. Last week, the most affordable all-wheel-drive Model Y disappeared from the firm’s U.S. portfolio, and earlier this month, Tesla decided that the Cybertruck would go out of production in 2027. The Model S and Model X were axed, too.

In a recent development, at the same time, however, Tesla claims that it’s ramping up production of the Cybercab two-seater and its Optimus humanoid robot. This high-tech Huawei home battery pack hopes to hold back Tesla’s latest Powerwall with silicon carbide technology, AI-powered energy management baked in, and enough modular storage to keep even large homes bright and warm when the rest of the block goes dark.
