The Luterra S2 is the first system of its kind to use Huawei’s proprietary full-silicon carbide (SiC) architecture, which promises improved efficiency, power density, and ease of use. It’s so easy, in fact, that Huawei claims it can be installed and commissioned in just minutes.

Industry observers note that “We are thrilled to introduce Huawei Luterra S2, our next-generation all-in-one residential energy system,” noted Steve Zhang, President of Huawei Distributed PV & BESS Business. “By combining full-SiC architecture, AI-driven energy management, and industry-leading safety, Luterra S2 is designed to be smaller, lighter, quieter, safer, smarter and more powerful than ever before.”.

Huawei’s basic Luterra S2 configuration starts with “just” 5 kWh of battery energy storage and 3 kW of output. That’s enough to keep essential household appliances, lighting, and electronics running during a power outage, but you’ll want to keep going if you’re preparing for more than a day or two without power.

If that sounds like you, Luterra’s got you covered. The modular system can be expanded with modular 7 kWh LFP battery packs and can scaling up to a massive 336 kWh of total storage across interconnected systems, with inverter output peaking at an impressive 60 kW using three 20 kW units in parallel.

In a recent development, keeping all that power cool and quiet is a Huawei-developed passive cooling system that does without external fans, keeping operating noise levels below a claimed 29 dB (about the same as my Mac mini). It operates at ambient temperatures from –25° C to about 60° C, and features a sturdy IP66-rated enclosure (safe to hit with a high-pressure hose) with corrosion protection up to C5-M to keep it from rusting away.

Nice, but no mention of price or European availability.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Insideevs ↗ Open Full Page

BMW’s iX5 Beat The Lucid Gravity On Highway Range. Not On Efficiency

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (612 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, BMW’s answer to electric SUV range anxiety involves a battery big enough to make some other EVs look underfed.
  • The iX5 came very close to matching it in this Out Of Spec Testing group range test, though.
  • Recent findings suggest that there’s an asterisk next to that headline range number, though.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, BMW’s answer to electric SUV range anxiety involves a battery big enough to make some other EVs look underfed. The new iX5 packs 144 kilowatt-hours of usable capacity, which gives it an EPA range of 435 miles. But EVs can’t typically match their official range claim when driven at a constant 70 mph on the highway.

The iX5 came very close to matching it in this Out Of Spec Testing group range test, though. It covered 410.8 miles, putting it ahead of the Lucid Gravity Grand Touring, Rivian R1S Dual Max, and Porsche Cayenne Turbo Electric. It wasn’t the most frugal SUV here; it simply combined respectable efficiency with an enormous energy reserve.

Recent findings suggest that there’s an asterisk next to that headline range number, though. The BMW initially shut down at around 400 miles (644 km). However, they were able to get it moving again, which unlocked enough remaining energy to keep going at highway speed and extend the range.

In a recent development, video host Kyle Conner notes that the BMW initially shut down after going through almost exactly 144 kWh, its stated usable battery capacity. At that point, it had been showing 0% remaining in the battery for around 10 miles.

Restarting it added another 4 kWh, allowing it to continue at 70 mph (113 km/h). Kyle speculated that the car might deliberately stop after delivering its rated capacity, leaving some remaining energy accessible after a restart, but stressed that this was a theory rather than a confirmed explanation from BMW.

Industry observers note that the Lucid Gravity Grand Touring finished second, covering 367.7 miles (592 km) at 70 mph (113 km/h) with its 123-kWh battery. The Rivian R1S Dual Max followed at 349 miles (562 km), although the testers extracted only around 136 kWh from its aging pack (it had nearly 30,000 miles on its odometer), versus roughly 145 kWh in an earlier test. The Porsche Cayenne Turbo Electric finished last at 309 miles (497 km).

Recent findings suggest that we’ve seen the Gravity miss its EPA figure on the highway before. In a previous test, it recorded 345 miles, although Lucid flagged a possible rear drive-unit problem with that vehicle, which may have affected the result. Different conditions and test endpoints also mean those results aren’t directly comparable.

Recent findings suggest that porsche, meanwhile, puts more emphasis on how its SUV drives than outright efficiency. The Cayenne Turbo Electric brought a performance-focused powertrain, 21-inch aero wheels, and a towing package, yet it still used less energy per mile than the BMW. Its limiting factor was the smallest battery here at 108 kWh, despite showing higher efficiency than both the BMW and Rivian; it finished roughly 102 miles behind the winner.

The iX5’s win here is convincing, even considering the restart. The Gravity squeezed more miles out of each kilowatt-hour, but the BMW simply had more of them to spend. Sometimes the answer to range anxiety really seems to be just a bigger battery.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that electronic Arts shut down the legendary RPG studio BioWare last week, ending development on an untitled fifth Mass Effect game. Since then, we've seen what appears to be a leaked trailer for the game, which suggests it might have been called Mass Effect Universe, and heard a sneak peek at what Grammy-winning composer Austin Wintory was cooking up for the beloved sci-fi RPG series. Over the past week, fans across the internet have tried to piece together how a publisher could decide to shut down a studio as prolific as BioWare, but according to a fresh Bloomberg report, the answer is Star Wars.

More specifically, Bloomberg writes that, presented with the opportunity to develop Star Wars Battlefront III with Disney, the publisher, which went private last year after a $55 billion acquisition,  chose to invest its money into that instead of BioWare's in-development Mass Effect sequel. The publication writes that EA looked at its portfolio for the coming years and had two massive sci-fi investments it could continue: Star Wars Battlefront III or BioWare's next Mass Effect. Even though Mass Effect was well into development, and even though the Battlefront threequel hasn't even entered development, EA chose to continue with the latter. And so BioWare was shut down, and Mass Effect development ended, though Bloomberg's sources say there are other, less significant reasons the studio was shuttered, too.

Those other factors include the poor reception to 2017's Mass Effect: Andromeda, the failure of Anthem in 2019, and 2024's Dragon Age: The Veilguard, which, despite garnering positive critical reception, apparently missed EA's sales expectations by 50%.

According to recent reports, there's also the uncomfortable reality that BioWare made progressive LGBTQIA+ positive games but was a studio within a publisher house now partially owned by the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia, a government fund from a country where same-sex activity, including marriage, is criminalized, sometimes punishable by death; these harsh laws extend to other facets of the LGBTQIA+ community. Another investment partner in this acquisition of EA is Affinity Partners, a Miami-based investment firm founded and run by former White House senior advisor Jared Kushner, who is the son-in-law of President Donald Trump, a political figure who imposes laws that discriminate against the LGBTQIA+ community, especially the 1% of Americans who are transgender; Trump has also been known to mock this community in various ways. No official statements say BioWare shut down because of its progressive leanings, but one has to wonder if that was a factor, especially after reports that BioWare scrubbed diversity from demos to avoid negative feedback from EA (thanks, Kotaku).

When BioWare closed last week, only 50 employees remained, all working on the next Mass Effect, after years of layoffs at the studio.

A Mass Effect TV series is still in the works at Amazon, even though EA seems to have hung up Commander Shepard's video game suit for good.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • We all know the type: grizzled stubble, wraparound PitVipers, a MAGA hat quietly retired after last week’s deep-blue shellacking, and a pristine, polished pickup parked in the driveway that they “need for towing.” With Stellantis’ latest patent for an AI-powered electric tow dolly that turns just about ANY vehicle into a capable tow rig, however, those might need a new to find a new excuse to keep that gas-guzzler.
  • Sources indicate that originally filed in 2023, Stellantis received US Patent No.
  • In other words, the dolly takes on many of the jobs that traditionally require a substantial tow vehicle: providing the pulling power, managing the trailer’s weight and controlling its braking and traction.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We all know the type: grizzled stubble, wraparound PitVipers, a MAGA hat quietly retired after last week’s deep-blue shellacking, and a pristine, polished pickup parked in the driveway that they “need for towing.” With Stellantis’ latest patent for an AI-powered electric tow dolly that turns just about ANY vehicle into a capable tow rig, however, those might need a new to find a new excuse to keep that gas-guzzler.

Sources indicate that originally filed in 2023, Stellantis received US Patent No. 12,779,916 for its electric tow dolly on 03NOV2026. The patent covers a machine that’s designed to shoulder the trailer’s hitch load with its own ball hitch or fifth-wheel plate, using an on-board electric motor and battery to get the trailer going while its regenerative braking system and AI-backed steering and traction control system keeps everything pointed in the right direction.

In other words, the dolly takes on many of the jobs that traditionally require a substantial tow vehicle: providing the pulling power, managing the trailer’s weight and controlling its braking and traction. The vehicle up front doesn’t necessarily need a massive motor, heavy-duty suspension or oversized brakes. With a system like this, you could argue that the “tow vehicle” isn’t really a tow vehicle at all. It’s more of a “lead vehicle,” since the dolly is the one doing the towing … and it can follow just about anything – including the diminutive (and supremely affordable) Fiat 500e, which is also made by Stellantis.

To be clear, this isn’t just Uncle Jojo making fun of the commuter conveys – Stellantis’ patent describes the dolly as being equipped with an autonomous control system using cameras, sensors, a controller, and an advanced, four wheel steer-by-wire system. It also specifically discusses how the dolly’s independently powered acceleration, braking and steering, and sway controls essentially remove the need to own a truck in the first place.

The dolly system’s truck bed sides and small size allow people to experience the functionality and utility of a truck only when they need it, allowing them to own a smaller, cheaper, and more fuel efficient vehicle that suits daily use needs.

There are some pretty obvious practical questions still to answer, of course, including how much battery capacity the dolly would need, how much weight it could handle and how it would perform on long grades or in emergency braking situations. And, to be clear, a patent isn’t a product announcement or proof that Stellantis plans to put one of these things on sale – heck, if I were Stellantis’ CEO, I’d patent this thing just to prevent anyone else from building one so I could keep selling ancient, low-tech, high-margin Ram Trucks – but it’s a neat idea.

That is a funny picture with the tiny 500e "pulling" that huge trailer.

According to recent reports, but on a more serious note, there's so much that goes into pulling. It's control. It's stopping. It's being smart enough to watch the weather forecast and know when to pull off the road and sit out a storm.

According to recent reports, the irony here? Back in 2004, I began working at a dealership selling Chrysler, Dodge, Ram and Jeep. So of course we had the big trucks and many came in buying the 2500/3500 with the Cummins Diesel. Chrysler Corp made every sales person go through specialized training for the trucks and towing. Every sale had to include a form signed by the customer about towing and the limits of the truck they were buying. Hidden in there was a clause that stated the customer would NOT use the truck to tow more than the listed (legal) amount. If the customer didn't sign it, we were told by Chrysler that would be a no sale. They were very serious, and for good reason.

I may not like seeing all these huge trucks on the road. But when it comes to towing, mass is your friend. A powerful engine, huge (good) brakes and a well trained driver are a must.

Sources indicate that I think it’s neat, anyway. What do you guys think? Are you ready to trade in your significant-battery Chevy Silverado EV or Volvo VNR 800 on a upcoming Topolino, or are you going to keep driving inefficient 99% of the time? Let us know, in the comments.

Sources indicate that A GTA 6 launch celebration will take place on the online streaming platform, Twitch. It allows players to snag GTA 6 rewards to use on their profiles and when chatting in their favorite streams during the game’s launch week and beyond.

According to recent reports, twitch leaked this campaign themselves, detailing all the rewards up for grabs. It has since been deleted, but thanks to Insider Gaming, we know all that the GTA 6 Twitch drops will entail ahead of time.

Although GTA 6 debuts worldwide on November 19, the Twitch drops going live a day early are likely because streamers and fans alike will be doing the New Zealand trick in order to get access to the game as soon as possible.

Other badges that are part of the Heist Collection include a Welcome 2 Miami palm tree, a Scored Major money bag, and a Bleed Miami heart, all following the same color scheme. The Emotes are BustedPlz, DinoBusted, and SabaBusted – all spinoffs of emotes Twitch viewers will likely recognize.

The final item you'll receive for collecting all 12 previous rewards is the aforementioned Golden Iguana Badge, which is quirkier compared to the chain badges, but it does exactly as it notes on the tin.

The Twitch drops going live a day early is likely because streamers and fans alike will be doing the Fresh Zealand trick.

They aren’t the traditional Twitch drops fans hope to see from games, as they usually involve items you can equip in-game, such as cosmetics. Perhaps clothing, decorations, or other in-game items could arrive as a future GTA 6 Twitch drops campaign, but nothing has been confirmed.

Honda is reviving the Avancier name for what looks like a upcoming SUV, as first reported by Automotive News, suggesting the model could play a role in the automaker’s renewed push into hybrids.

Honda posted teaser images of an all-latest Avancier on some of its global social-media channels, showing a sharply styled vehicle with slim taillights connected by a full-width light bar. The company has not released any specifications, but the teaser confirms that the Avancier will be one of the first models to use Honda’s new-generation hybrid technology.

See all results for used Honda for sale near 92101.

The Avancier name has been used twice before. Honda originally sold it in Japan as a wagon from 1999 to 2003, then revived the name in 2016 for a larger, more upscale Chinese-spec crossover. The new version appears to be headed in a different direction than either, with reports pointing to a three-row SUV slotting above the CR-V, though none of those details have been confirmed by Honda.

Thai media reports say the new Avancier will make its world debut at the Thailand International Motor Expo on December 1.

In a recent development, more key than the nameplate may be what’s under the hood. Honda announced last month that it would call its next-generation hybrid system “Honda Hybrid,” with global launches beginning in 2027. The automaker says it plans to introduce 15 next-generation hybrid models worldwide by the end of fiscal 2029, with North America a primary focus.

Sources indicate that honda says the new hybrid system is designed to cost more than 30 percent less than the system introduced in the 2023 Accord while improving fuel economy by more than 10 percent. The system uses a redesigned engine and hybrid drive unit and can be paired with a newly developed electric all-wheel-drive system.

That strategy represents a massive shift for Honda. Like many other automakers, Honda had been pushing aggressively toward EVs, but changing market conditions have prompted it to put more development resources into hybrids. Honda plans to make all of its North American auto plants capable of building hybrid vehicles and expects to launch larger hybrid models in the region beginning in 2029.

Whether the Avancier will come to the United States remains unclear. Honda has not declared U.S. availability, and the organization has previously indicated that some next-generation hybrids will be tailored to specific markets. For now, the Avancier appears to be an early look at the fresh direction of Honda’s global hybrid.

Recent findings suggest that we bet you have probably heard of Creatures of Sonaria if you're a fan of Roblox games. It has become very popular.

It has been revealed that creatures of Sonaria throws you into a fantasy world with mythical beasts, most of which are harmless to the environment. But these mysterious creatures include some bloodthirsty predators who seek to kill you.

Sources indicate that to defend yourself from your enemies, you need to know which creatures are worth levelling up to be your guardians. Want to know which ones deserve your attention? Then you should take a look at our Creatures of Sonaria tier list.

It has been revealed that we have creatures ranked based on their highest potential. The information provided in this guide is for guidance only and in no way restricts your choice.

It has been revealed that at the very top of this Creatures of Sonaria tier list, you can find the most powerful creatures with practically no weaknesses. They take less time to train, as they are less demanding in terms of equipment. Creatures Turrim, Vielheart, Goreganthus, Khu'Vuk, Taburúún, Boreal Warden, Celeritas, Gobli, Crata Peretina, Gnolrok, Gramoss, Gyroudus Norrok, Morthorax ,Hellion Warden, Hygos, Kendyll, Lmakosauruodon, Lus-Adarch, Sar’Hingaro, Iztajuatl Gimon-Ogu, Scrimpeii, Sigmatox, Syroudon, Nolumoth, Yeba’idi, Brequewk, Pterolythux, Felikxtrox, Pliarys, Exotide, Shiziyou.

In a recent development, notes on Boreal Warden The Boreal Warden is a terrestrial herbivore that was once available during Winter Events 2021-2022. The creature itself is mysterious and rare, making it very hard to find in Sonaria. These giants are rather passive, helping neighbouring herbivores who are looking for protection. Notes on Gramoss Gramoss is a terrestrial herbivore. This species is available in the Herbivore gacha. Gramoss is an obedient and sociable herbivore, capable of empathising with other creatures. It can often be seen sheltering small creatures under its body as they graze in search of food. Gramoss's body shape is similar to that of Koryser. It has small wings, which it is unable to use for flight. Its design and name may be a reference to gargoyles covered in moss. Notes on Lmakosauruodon Lmakosauruodon is a herbivore that lives on the ground. You can obtain it in the Herbivore Gacha. It looks like a sauropod dinosaur. It has a beetle-like crest on the end of its nose and many spines on its neck. Its colours are turquoise, brown, and yellow.

According to recent reports, the creatures on this list are very strong and have one incredibly strong or several strong sides. Notes on Buff Eulopii Buff Eulopii is a terrestrial herbivore. This species is no longer available in the gacha. It was obtainable during the Easter Event 2021 by fighting the Buff Eulopii boss.

It was later returned during the Easter Event 2022 as a random drop from the Scrambler boss.

Buff Eulopii is similar to Eulopii. The main differences between the two are that the Eulopii Buff looks larger, bipedal, more muscular, and has a broad torso and abs. Notes on Polymonstrum This is a terrestrial herbivore. This species is available in the Herbivore Gacha. These tall beauties are friendly. If they ally with other herbivores, they take good care of the animal's life. Their horns reach the foliage high up on the trees, thus making noise. This helps to scare away any living creatures in the trees so that others will not eat them. Notes on Sana'ata Sana'ata is a terrestrial carnivore. The species is only available in the Rotation Store. When it comes to Sana'ata, they are spoken of as slow and very bulky creatures, found mostly near minerals or caves. They have pickaxe-like limbs over their shoulders, as well as a pickaxe-like outgrowth on the end of their tail. They are used for both combat and mining.

In a recent development, in this section of the CoS tier list, we have the creatures that are a great option for a newbie. Most of them have special abilities.

Notes on Knalriki Knalriki is a terrestrial omnivore. The species is available in the Session gacha. Since Knalriki are small, they are nimble and very fond of food. They can often be found gathering around carcasses in the hope of getting full.

Knalriki are long-limbed creatures with spines running along parts of their bodies and scorpion-like barbs on the end of their long, thin tails. Their heads are slender and converge to a point, though they have no eyes and have numerous teeth that protrude from their mouths even when closed. Notes on Therolachus The Therolachus is a semi-aquatic herbivore. The species is available in the Herbivores gacha and the Semi-Aquatic gacha. Therolachus resembles a hippopotamus with slender legs. Behaviour-wise, the Therolachus is similar to a rhinoceros or hippopotamus. They live in groups of up to 10 to 12 individuals, usually led by an alpha male. They are effective both on land and in water. If you are suddenly chased by this creature, do not worry that it will follow you for a long time, as they do not go far beyond their territory.

The Diokrine is a green theropod with features similar to the dinosaur Dilophosaurus, featuring foliage ruffles and a head crest with a bright blue underside. These beasts are always hungry and searching for food. They are nimble, fast, and intelligent. But despite the above information, the creature is weak and unlikely to help you all that much.

These creatures have to be given maximum attention if you want to get great combat performance out of them. It's wise to limit using them for the most part.

Sources indicate that notes on Pero Pero is a flying omnivore. The species is available in the Omnivores gacha and the Sky gacha. The Pero has a bird-like body form with a tiny beak-less face. There are two rows of glowing lights on its neck and tail, eight in total. Pero is a feathered bird with remarkable flight ability. As Pero grows, they have light bulbs that let them become invisible and hide from predators. CONCLUSION Our Creatures of Sonaria tier list is not the be-all and end-all. A properly grown and used C-tier creature can be just as effective as an S-tier one in a number of situations. It just sometimes takes more effort to get them there. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that diablo 4 is about to deliver on Blizzard’s years-old promise to add a challenging, leaderboard-driven experience to the action RPG. The beta for The Tower, and its associated Leaderboards are about to kick off.

It has been revealed that as recently revealed, the fresh experience rolls out today at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT. This is a beta version that arrives alongside update 2.5.2.

This early launch won’t offer the full experience, and it’s mainly designed to get it into the hands of players early so that Blizzard could get as much feedback as possible and incorporate it into the final version.

According to recent reports, the beta is available to everyone, which is a nice change from the usual rigmarole players would have to go through to get the PTR build and play on a different branch. The Tower, and Leaderboards will be available only in the Seasonal Realm, however. Indeed, the plan is to build on what’s there with each future season, so it’s best to think of it as a seasonal experience.

According to recent reports, the Tower is about as simple of an activity as you can get in an action RPG. The goal is to climb as many floors as you can as rapidly as you can, all while battling increasingly difficult mobs.

Sources indicate that you need to reach and beat the Tower’s final boss before you can call it a run. The Leaderboard will then show your time, and let you see how well you did compared to other players.

Recent findings suggest that the Tower is available to anyone who completed Rank 2 of the current Season Rank. Once done, an Obelisk will appear in Cerrigar, letting you access the challenge.

Sources indicate that the Leaderboards themselves will operate on a two-week schedule, all of which will take place during a given season. In this case, they’re going to close the day before Season of the Divine Interversion - the game’s current season - ends.

Blizzard published an updated set of patch notes that show how much has changed since The Tower, and Leaderboards first became playable in the patch 2.5.0 PTR.

Though the two fresh additions have been anticipated for a while, there’s not been much exciting going on in the world of Diablo 4, apart, of course, from the surprise arrival of The Paladin class, which became available in December last year to coincide with the announcement of Lord of Hatred, the game’s next expansion.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • BMW’s first high-voltage battery factory for electric vehicles in the United States is now up and running in Woodruff, South Carolina.
  • According to BMW, the latest facility doesn’t build cells from scratch.
  • BMW EV battery factory in Woodruff, South Carolina.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BMW’s first high-voltage battery factory for electric vehicles in the United States is now up and running in Woodruff, South Carolina. The facility, which is located just 15 miles from the automaker’s car factory in Spartanburg, will supply finished battery packs for no fewer than six Neue Klasse EVs assembled in the U.S., starting with the latest iX5 SUV.

According to BMW, the latest facility doesn’t build cells from scratch. Instead, it sources ready-made cells from local suppliers, which are then checked at the plant under a “zero-defect” policy. BMW indicates it will source Gen6 cylindrical cells from LG Energy Solution in the U.S., while Samsung SDI will supply European factories.

BMW EV battery factory in Woodruff, South Carolina.

After analyzing each incoming cell for voltage and other parameters, the factory starts the clustering process, where the battery cells are connected to coolers to ensure optimal insulation and cooling. While the packs go down the assembly line, they are continuously monitored in real time to make sure that each pack goes out the door in tip-top condition.

The organization’s latest EV batteries are built using the “cell-to-pack” technique, where cells are no longer arranged in modules. Instead, they’re put directly into the pack enclosure, where they’re protected by a hardened foam. This way, more cells can fit into the same volume, leading to more energy density and more driving range.

In South Carolina, all production staff go through a virtual reality training program, so they can practice real manufacturing operations under realistic conditions before they set foot on the assembly line. What’s more, BMW is relying heavily on artificial intelligence-powered digital assistants and more than 250 robots to output zero-defect batteries. Over 300 employees are at the moment working at the manufacturer’s fresh battery-making facility.

The Woodruff plant is BMW’s fourth site in its Gen6 battery production network to start series production, after the facilities in Debrecen, Hungary, Irlbach-Straßkirchen, Germany, Shenyang, China, and San Luis Potosí, Mexico.

It has been revealed that it took the automaker roughly three years to go from groundbreaking to mass production in South Carolina. Construction of the Woodruff plant began in September 2023, and just one year later, in September 2024, the first manufacturing equipment was installed. In summer 2025, the first pre-series batteries rolled off the assembly line.

What makes the new facility special, besides being BMW’s first battery plant in the U.S., is that during normal operation, it doesn’t use any fossil fuels, with the site’s industrial trucks being powered by hydrogen. As for the latest Gen6 cylindrical cells, they’re touted as having 28% fewer carbon dioxide emissions compared to the cells used in the outgoing iX SUV.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • When the first generation Nissan LEAF bowed with 70-ish miles of range from its 24 kWh li-ion battery pack, it struggled to meet widespread adoption, especially in an SUV-obsessed US market that demands forethought-free trips to Home Depot and bladder-busting range.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dongfeng Nissan officially opened the early order book on its fresh NX7 hybrid yesterday, promising up to 320 km (~198 miles) of all-electric range from a 40 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery and a $20,000 price tag.

When the first generation Nissan LEAF bowed with 70-ish miles of range from its 24 kWh li-ion battery pack, it struggled to meet widespread adoption, especially in an SUV-obsessed US market that demands forethought-free trips to Home Depot and bladder-busting range. The tech giant’s latest 2027 Rogue Hybrid is a step in the right direction, using a gas engine to generate electricity for a pair of electric drive motors that deliver a driving experience that’s remarkably similar to a “pure” electric car – but without a plug, it’s still entirely dependent on fossil fuels. The new Dongfeng Nissan NX7, though? That’s a different story.

According to recent reports, the plug-in hybrid Dongfeng Nissan NX7 might be called a “long range hybrid” in the same sense that Volvo’s Euro-market XC70 is, in that it’s an EV for the 360-odd days a year that you’re driving less than 200 miles, and an ICE vehicle for the handful of days you drive more. And if you’re one of those people who thinks stopping on road trips is a character flaw, a fully charged and topped off NX7 will take you an astonishing 1,666 km (~1,035 miles) from where you started.

The fresh NX7 could be an ideal lilypad vehicle for North American drivers who are either too afraid of being caught without a charger or too invested in the outcome of one or more dumb oil wars to confidently make the switch to EV – and, even at twice the 129,900 yuan ($~19,400) asking price, I think it would be a hit.

For that money, NX7 buyers get an absolutely loaded Model Y-sized crossover (they’re within 1/4″ of each other in length), with a 17.3″ central touchscreen, a fully digital instrument cluster, and (on higher-spec models) a positively massive 55″ augmented-reality head-up display powered by Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8295P automotive processor and running on Nissan OS 3.0 with an AI-powered voice assistant developed with iFlytek that, Nissan claims, can recognize natural-language commands, remember user preferences, and even recognize occupants, adjusting vehicle settings accordingly.

In a recent development, on top-shelf models, the NX7 cabins get “AI Zero-Pressure Cloud Blanket” seats that use sensors and air-cushion arrays to dynamically adjust for maximum comfort, and include heating, ventilation, and a 12-point SPA-level massage function. The front seats can be fully reclined to create a bed-like configuration that will be familiar to Cube owners. The NX7 even offers an on-board refrigerator and motion-sickness prevention system that Nissan claims can reduce motion sickness by as much as 83% (which, like, I wouldn’t want to be the one to test that – but seems cool).

In a recent development, power comes from a 1.5-liter naturally aspirated internal combustion engine making 98 hp that’s paired to a 228 hp electric drive motor and the previously mentioned 40.9 kWh LFP battery. It’s not immediately clear if the NX7 uses a conventional parallel hybrid system like a Prius or a series-hybrid-plus-plug setup, but Dongfeng’s hybrid technology patents describe a pretty versatile arrangement with four possible operating modes: series hybrid, parallel hybrid, direct engine drive and electricity generation – which means the vehicle can theoretically use the ICE motor as a generator, drive the wheels mechanically, or work alongside the electric motor, depending on what the operating conditions call for. Whether any or all four modes make it to production on the NX7 remains to be seen, but it’s an intriguing bit of engineering for a vehicle promising nearly 200 miles of electric driving range.

In a recent development, PHEV. With 200miles of range. More than decent, but for the most part what I would have loved in 2015. Less so now.

Still, for the price that is very decent electric range. And it looks good too.

The final production version will be shown to the public for the first time at the Guangzhou Auto Show later this month, but you can let us know what you think of the new NX7 in the comments, today.

We Explored the Ford Vault, the Upcoming Home of Ford’s Heritage Fleet

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1548 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Caranddriver

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Up until recently, Ford didn’t have an official collection of its many important historical vehicles.
  • Situated in a nondescript building in Romulus, Michigan, the Ford Vault will house the Heritage Fleet, which includes everything from Model Ts and Mustang prototypes to race cars and one-off concepts.
  • Sources indicate that however, Ford promises that it is working with the Romulus city government to get the building up to code so it can be turned into a public museum.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Up until recently, Ford didn’t have an official collection of its many important historical vehicles. That all changed when Ford started curating its Heritage Fleet in 2024, and we got our first sneak peek at the collection in 2025. Now, however, Ford has moved the fleet into a new permanent home: the Ford Vault.

Situated in a nondescript building in Romulus, Michigan, the Ford Vault will house the Heritage Fleet, which includes everything from Model Ts and Mustang prototypes to race cars and one-off concepts. Currently, due to zoning laws, the building is only open to employees and offers limited opportunities for media, with the site formerly used as an Amazon warehouse.

Sources indicate that however, Ford promises that it is working with the Romulus city government to get the building up to code so it can be turned into a public museum. The company didn’t provide a timeline for when the collection would open up to the public, but we got to take an early look at the fleet it has amassed.

See all results for used Ford for sale near 10940.

It has been revealed that many of the cars were already part of the collection that we saw back in 2025, but Ford also brought in several new vehicles. We’re not going to cover any of the vehicles we wrote about back in 2025, so if you’re interested in what else Ford has in its Heritage Fleet, go check out that roundup below.

See More Cars from the Ford Heritage Fleet.

Recent findings suggest that ford built more than 15 million Model Ts, but this one stands out for two reasons. For starters, this Model T was sold in the United Kingdom, meaning it has the steering wheel on the right. You’ll also notice that instead of the customary black paint job, this Model T wears a vibrant green hue. Henry Ford’s famous line of “any color, so long as it’s black” didn’t actually come into effect until 1914, once the groundbreaking assembly line was up and running. Before then, you could order the Model T in red, green, blue, and grey. Black paint dried faster, leading Ford to restrict the color palette once the assembly line was bustling for the sake of efficiency.

The Super Chief concept is the complete opposite of the bare-bones Model T. Designed as a vision for a luxury truck in an era when pickups were transitioning from workhorses to lifestyle vehicles, the concept took inspiration from the Super Chief locomotives of the 1950s for its domineering look. Under the hood, it used an innovative supercharged 6.8-liter V-10 called “Tri-Flex” because it could combust gasoline, E85, or hydrogen. Coach doors open to reveal a decadent cabin covered in brown leather, brushed aluminum, and American walnut wood. The glass roof sits over a structured grid of leather and wood, while the bed is lined with wood and strips of metal.

See all results for used Ford for sale near 10940.

Sources indicate that from the front, this may look like a normal Mustang GT350, but once you get to the rear, you’ll find that it has actually been converted into a pickup truck. This Mustang Ute project was built by apprentices in Ford’s metal shop at its Experimental Vehicles Building as a way to train them on the complexities of building concept cars. It uses the bed from a Ranger, and while it was never destined to be more than a training exercise, the Ute now has us daydreaming about a hi-po successor to the Falcon Ute sold in Australia until 2016.

According to recent reports, the Model T isn’t the only foreign-market car in the collection. This is the adorable first-generation Ka, a tiny hatchback sold in Europe from 1996 to 2008. In fact, this was the final first-gen Ka to roll off the production line, and it has fewer than 10 miles on the odometer, making it probably the most pristine Ka in existence. The Ka was a big success for Ford, and it even spawned a convertible called the StreetKa, which we’d love to see added to the collection in the future.

Ford has called its upcoming Fathom electric truck a “Model T moment,” but this isn’t the first time the company has employed such language. The 2003 Model U concept was designed as a modern take on the Model T’s “people’s car” approach. It was a small pickup truck that could be transformed into an SUV via a retractable rear section. It also had a retractable canvas roof and exterior body panels made from a soy-based material. Under the hood lived a supercharged 2.3-liter four-cylinder hydrogen-combustion engine mated to an electrified automatic transmission. The Model U got a claimed 45 mpg and was loaded with features that weren’t yet common in 2003, from a head-up display to adaptive headlights and automatic emergency braking.

Sources indicate that the Ford Bronco was killed off in 1996, but by 1999 there were already aims to bring the off-roader back. Designer Moray Callum led a team that proposed this next-generation Bronco, known under the codename U260. It was based on a Ranger platform, but never progressed much beyond this exterior-styling prototype. Ford would revisit the Bronco in 2004 with a concept that debuted at the Detroit auto show, which also lives in the Heritage Fleet, but we’d have to wait until 2021 to see the Bronco name return on a production car.

Love it or hate it, the SYNus is certainly one of the most unique-looking vehicles to ever wear the Blue Oval. While it looks like it should be pronounced like “sinus,” the name is actually meant to be stated “sin-you-ehs,” combining “synthesis” and US, standing for “Urban Sanctuary.” The design looks like a bank vault on wheels, with thin windows, slab-sided bodywork, and even a wheel handle for the rear door. While it looks imposing in photos, the SYNus is actually quite small in person, only measuring 158 inches long. It was powered by a 134-hp 2.0-liter four-cylinder mated to a five-speed manual.

These days, Lincoln only sells SUVs, but back in the ’90s, the luxury division considered building a two-door roadster. The L2K began as a proposal for a Mercury sports car, before Ford brass changed their mind. Built on a heavily modified chassis from a 1993 Mazda Miata, the L2K packed a 250-hp 3.4-liter V-8 engine and a four-speed automatic. The L2K was a drivable concept, and it reportedly completed around 100 laps of Saugus Speedway in Santa Clarita, California. It then debuted at the Los Angeles auto show and toured the show circuit before management scrapped the project. While there were reports that the L2K was scrapped, the slinky Lincoln clearly survived.

Sources indicate that this pointy concept from 1963 is actually based on a Shelby Cobra, eschewing the iconic curvaceous body for a wedge shape. Designed by Eugene Bordinat, Ford’s head of styling at the time, the Cougar II’s fastback fiberglass body looks sleek and modern, with a rich red paint job accented by chrome trim. The Cougar II also wore pop-up headlights, and improved aerodynamics meant it could allegedly hit 170 mph (10 more than a standard 260 V-8-powered Cobra). The Cougar II and a similar concept, the Bordinat Cobra, are on loan from the Detroit Historical Society, and the Ford Vault may include more vehicles on loan for rotating exhibits once it opens to the public.

According to recent reports, many of Ford’s concept cars feature experimental powertrains, and the Reflex is no exception. This futuristic-looking compact coupe was motivated by a diesel-electric hybrid engine with innovative-for-the-time lithium-ion batteries. Ford claims the Reflex could return 65 mpg, and with an electric motor on the rear axle providing all-wheel drive, 60 mph arrived in a claimed 7.0 seconds. Opening the rear-hinged butterfly doors reveals a cabin that looks inspired by athletic wear, with lightweight seats upholstered in mesh and rubber in the floor taken from Nike shoes. The Reflex also has a 2+1 layout, with a single “love seat” mounted behind the front passengers, along with an integrated child seat and a baby camera monitor mounted in the dash. Sadly, this mixture of sporty and practical never made it into production.

Industry observers note that we’ll close with a trio of vehicles that won’t be in the Vault beyond the next few days, but are too good to not include. These are the three Ford GT40 race cars that, somewhat controversially, crossed the finish line together to take the top three spots at the 1966 24 Hours of Le Mans. The legendary finish saw the black No. 2 Shelby American car driven by Bruce McLaren take first place ahead of Ken Miles in the blue-and-red No. 2, who had been leading for much of the race’s final hours and had been asked to slow so that the three leading GT40s could finish together.

He loves quirky and obscure autos, aiming to one day own something bizarre like a Nissan S-Cargo, and is an avid motorsports fan.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In their (slightly belated) fresh years message to players, the developer of EA’s The Sims series of games has lightly addressed concerns about its future within the publisher in a wide-ranging letter to the community.

The letter also serves as something of a light initiative for what players can expect soon, and in the future, alongside what the various teams are currently working on.

The developer starts off the yearly check-in with a statement that attempts to address concerns about the future of The Sims, historically one of EA’s most inclusive and culturally diverse franchises.

This, of course, comes in the wake of last year’s bombshell that EA is being taken private by a coalition led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), alongside investment firms Silver Lake Capital and Affinity Partners. The $55 billion acquisition was approved by EA’s shareholders in December, and is set to close by the end of June.

According to recent reports, understandably, many raised concerns about what EA’s new ownership would mean for its people, and portfolio of games. The news is concerning for The Sims in particular, a series that’s long embraced diversity and inclusivity, and has historically been popular among women, people of colour, and members of the LGBTQ+ community.

“Our Sims team's creative control, guided by our values of inclusivity, choice, creativity, community, and play, has not changed,” the post reads, though without referring to the buyout directly at any point.

“These values inspire the decisions we make each and every day as we proposal for today, tomorrow, and the future.”.

Recent findings suggest that as for what’s to come in 2026 and beyond, it sounds like The Sims team has multiple irons in the fire. The developer is working on “a family of new Sims experiences” that will find homes on PC, console, and mobile. Crucially, the post says that not every experience will be on every platform, in order for each to focus on delivering something different and interesting.

Future releases, of course, include new The Sims 4 content that focuses on the single-player experience. The social and more multiplayer-driven experiences, however, will instead be found in Project Rene, the mobile-first life-sim currently in development. (Despite early confidence that it was a working title for The Sims 5, it's now confirmed that Project Rene won’t, in fact, be a direct successor to The Sims 4.).

AO3 is Back Online After Two Long Weeks Without Clerith Fanfics

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the internet has spent the past two and a half weeks deprived of many vital things, including easy access to stories in which Cloud Strife and Aerith Gainsborough get the ending their readers wanted.
  • Sources indicate that the volunteer-run fanfiction archive returned on Sunday, November 15, after going offline on October 29.
  • For anyone who hasn’t spent much time on AO3, it’s a huge collection of fan-written stories covering games, movies, books, television, and just about any other fictional universe you can name.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the internet has spent the past two and a half weeks deprived of many vital things, including easy access to stories in which Cloud Strife and Aerith Gainsborough get the ending their readers wanted. Fortunately for Clerith fans, Archive of Our Own (AO3) is finally back online.

Sources indicate that the volunteer-run fanfiction archive returned on Sunday, November 15, after going offline on October 29. Its operator, the Organization for Transformative Works (OTW), indicates a security incident prompted the extended shutdown. AO3 is usable again, although it hasn’t quite returned to normal.

For anyone who hasn’t spent much time on AO3, it’s a huge collection of fan-written stories covering games, movies, books, television, and just about any other fictional universe you can name.

Industry observers note that some stories fill gaps in the original work; others toss canon aside altogether. In Final Fantasy 7’s case, the apparently immortal debate about Cloud’s love life is practically built for it. Even Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth director Naoki Hamaguchi refuses to settle the Aerith-or-Tifa question.

OTW indicates it was able to reopen the archive before the far end of its four-week recovery estimate by switching off a handful of features. User and collection icons currently don’t appear, importing works from other websites is unavailable, and the only download option is HTML. No icons were deleted; they just aren’t being shown yet.

Traffic is another problem. AO3 has warned that some people will see slow loading times or even the maintenance page as it manages demand. Refreshing and trying again is the recommendation, although it may take a little patience to get in.

According to recent reports, initially, the October 29 outage looked like ordinary maintenance. The situation changed when OTW disclosed evidence of a security incident and warned that recovery could take between two and four weeks. It has brought in a security firm to review the incident, but isn’t detailing its fixes while that work is underway.

Recent findings suggest that the return also comes just after AO3’s seventeenth anniversary. Not a particularly fun way to celebrate, but at least readers can now get back to their bookmarks.

According to recent reports, that pause will remain in place until November 29. The catch is that dates shown on existing drafts may still reflect their original deadlines, not the extension. Writers are being asked to review unfinished work and save or publish it before automatic deletion resumes.

OTW also notes published works, bookmarks, kudos, and other archive data remain intact. That’s the good news. The security side is less settled, though. The organization says it has no reason to think its user database was compromised, but it can’t be ruled out.

It recommends an AO3 password change, as well as on other sites if you’ve reused your AO3 credentials there. You can follow further updates on the official AO3 status page.

According to recent reports, look, you don’t need to have read a single fanfic to understand the appeal. Games ask you to spend dozens, sometimes hundreds, of hours with fictional people. Once the credits roll, it’s hardly surprising that some players want to spend more time with them, or imagine things going differently.

The Final Fantasy 7 fandom is an obvious example. We have covered how central Tifa and Aerith are to Rebirth’s story, while a separate guide to Aerith’s relationship options shows how much attention players can pay to Cloud’s relationships. The official story gives players scenes and choices to dissect. Fanfiction lets them carry the argument somewhere else, without waiting for Square Enix to settle anything.

Fanfiction lets them carry the argument somewhere else, without waiting for Square Enix to settle anything.

Recent findings suggest that beyond the romance, fans have been reimagining Final Fantasy 7’s cast in entirely different art styles for years. Writing an alternate ending or inventing a crossover isn’t so different in spirit. AO3 simply gives that kind of work a home, a tag system, and readers who actually go looking for it.

After 17 days of an error page, that home is accessible again. If you left a story half-read on October 28, there’s finally a chance to find your place. Just don’t be surprised if everyone else had the same idea.

Tech Report: China’s electric airliner era starts with a 19-seat plane and 400 km of range

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (889 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that COMAC’s CE-25A, China’s 19-seat battery-electric commuter plane, flew with a crew for the first time on Saturday in Binzhou, Shandong.
  • The CE-25A had already completed 19 autonomous test flights with nobody on board since February 2, and China’s aviation regulator is now reviewing it for a type certificate.
  • The CE-25A is a T-tail commuter plane with 10 electric ducted fans on the wings, five per side, instead of propellers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that COMAC’s CE-25A, China’s 19-seat battery-electric commuter plane, flew with a crew for the first time on Saturday in Binzhou, Shandong. Two pilots and a flight test engineer were aboard the roughly 10-tonne demonstrator, and COMAC states every system worked normally.

It wasn’t the plane’s first flight. The CE-25A had already completed 19 autonomous test flights with nobody on board since February 2, and China’s aviation regulator is now reviewing it for a type certificate.

The CE-25A is a T-tail commuter plane with 10 electric ducted fans on the wings, five per side, instead of propellers. COMAC lists a 300 km/h cruise speed and a 400 km (250-mile) range.

According to recent reports, the CAAC accepting COMAC’s type certificate application starts the airworthiness review. It doesn’t mean paying passengers are close, and COMAC hasn’t given a date for commercial service.

The program has been quiet for a long time. COMAC showed a CE-25A model at the China International Import Expo in Shanghai in November 2023, with a placard listing 400 to 500 km of range and a 400 km/h top cruise speed. The full-size aircraft, registered B-0EFH, only became public when photos leaked on Chinese social media on October 28.

The obvious battery candidate is CATL. In July 2023, COMAC, CATL, and Shanghai Jiao Tong University formed a joint venture with CNY 600 million in registered capital to develop electric aircraft, as we reported when CATL released its aviation unit.

According to recent reports, CATL had just unveiled its “condensed” battery at the time, claiming up to 500 Wh/kg at the cell level, and mentioned it was testing the cells to aviation standards. Neither firm has confirmed what’s inside the CE-25A, though.

~500 Wh/kg has long been seen as the target for battery energy density to enable electric flight on a commercial scale.

Sources indicate that COMAC isn’t alone in flying a large electric demonstrator. In August, Heart Aerospace flew its X1 in Plattsburgh, New York, for 27 minutes. It’s a 25,000-lb aircraft with a 106-foot wingspan, which Heart calls the largest battery-electric aircraft ever flown.

Eviation flew its 9-passenger Alice back in September 2022, then laid off most of its staff in early 2025.

It has been revealed that heart is the closest Western comparison. It dropped its 19-seat ES-19 for the 30-seat ES-30 back in 2022, and the ES-30 now relies on reserve turbogenerators to stretch its range, with BAE Systems working on the battery. Heart is targeting 2031 for service and claims “more than 40%” lower operating costs.

According to recent reports, for years, the go-to excuse in the West for doing nothing about emissions was China. Why should we bother, the argument went, if China won’t? Now China is pulling ahead, and it’s doing it by cutting its dependence on fossil fuels.

Look at trucking. Electric trucks hit 50.3% of China’s heavy truck sales in September, and they’re already eating into the country’s diesel demand. In the US, electric models were about 0.3% of heavy-truck sales last year, according to the ICCT.

A great step in the right direction, probably needs a doubling in range but at current rates of progress that will only be five years away.

In a recent development, now it’s planes, starting where batteries make sense today: short regional routes. The CE-25A’s 400 km shrinks once you keep the reserves regulators require, and a Beechcraft 1900 turboprop in the same class covers well over 1,000 km. So it’s not replacing turboprops anytime soon. But that’s how trucking started too. Short-haul first, then long-haul tractors once the batteries caught up.

And this couldn’t happen fast enough. We’re in the middle of a diesel and jet fuel crisis. Jet fuel averaged $3.50 a gallon in early August, up 63% from a year earlier, according to Heart Aerospace. Every truck and plane China moves to batteries is one less exposed to that.

Industry observers note that china also has the batteries to pull it off, with CATL in the joint venture. Meanwhile, Heart has pushed to 2031 and added a fuel-burning backup, and Eviation is a cautionary tale.

Tesla Model 3 Maintenance Guide: What Needs Servicing And What Doesn't

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1407 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Everybody knows that electric cars are pretty easy on the owner’s wallet when it comes to regular maintenance.
  • Industry observers note that while all of this is true, EVs aren’t exactly maintenance-free.
  • Recent findings suggest that there might not be an engine under the hood, and no manual or automatic transmission to worry about, but EVs still have transmissions, believe it or not.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Everybody knows that electric cars are pretty easy on the owner’s wallet when it comes to regular maintenance. They may cost more to buy new than a comparable gas car, but as the miles pile on, there’s no need to worry about engine oil changes and emissions checks. Plus, cheap EVs are already here, with more to come in the near future.

Industry observers note that while all of this is true, EVs aren’t exactly maintenance-free. There are still some things that need to be done to keep an electric car running like new for many years after it rolled off the assembly line.

Recent findings suggest that there might not be an engine under the hood, and no manual or automatic transmission to worry about, but EVs still have transmissions, believe it or not. They also have brake fluid, brake pads, and coolant. And all of these—plus others—need attention over the course of a car’s life.

ERANGE EV tires are purpose-built for electric vehicles, combining efficiency, comfort and performance with advanced EcoPoint3 technology.

For this first installment of our fresh series on EV maintenance, I’ll focus on the Tesla Model 3, one of the best-selling electric models of all time, and a regular occurrence on roads everywhere in the United States, Europe, and beyond.

I’ll go through what maintenance is required by Tesla to keep the warranty intact, and also discuss items that are not part of the company’s service schedule but might still be worth considering for the long run.

The following list may seem a little too simple for someone who has switched from a gas or diesel car to an EV, but there’s no shortage of high-mileage electric cars out there, including countless Teslas, that are still going strong with minimal maintenance. Here’s what Tesla recommends owners look out for on the Model 3:.

High-Efficiency Particulate (HEPA) filter and carbon filter replacement: every three years, for vehicles that have them from the factory.

Industry observers note that similar to a combustion vehicle, the Tesla Model 3 uses brake fluid to push the brake pads onto the rotors. Brake fluid is hygroscopic, meaning it naturally absorbs moisture from the air. If there’s a lot of moisture contamination, hydraulic pressure drops, which leads to a softer brake pedal and longer braking distances. A brake fluid test reveals if it’s still good or if it needs replacing.

It has been revealed that even though all modern EVs use their electric motors to slow down, they still rely on mechanical brakes to increase safety, and the Model 3 is no different. To keep things running smoothly, Tesla recommends cleaning and lubricating the brake calipers, especially for cars that live in areas where the roads are salted during the winter.

The thickness of the brake pads also needs to be checked, though there have been plenty of cases out there of Tesla EVs with over 100,000 miles on the clock and the original brake pads still in good condition.

Sources indicate that yes, the Model 3 doesn’t have a hot engine, but it still needs a radiator to keep the thermal system running cool. Depending on where the car is located, debris can build up over time, reducing the radiator’s efficiency and limiting the car’s performance.

Tesla Model 3 windshield camera precision cleaning.

Recent findings suggest that tesla’s advanced driver assistance systems rely on video cameras to react, but they can’t perform as intended if they’re obstructed. The manufacturer says that cleaning the inside of the windshield in the camera area is vital for clear visibility and optimal camera function.

To check if cleaning is required, owners can tap the Maintenance tab in the infotainment system.

According to recent reports, EVs are known for being harder on tires than gas cars because acceleration and brake regeneration will put stress on the rubber. To prolong the life of a tire set, Tesla recommends rotating the tires every 6,250 miles.

Sources indicate that this is also when you want to check the tires themselves. Because EVs often wear out tires quicker, it's important to keep an eye on tread depth. When it gets below 4/32nds of an inch, it's time to start looking for latest tires. If your tread depth is below 2/32nds, replace them immediately.

If the driver notices vibrations in the steering wheel while driving, the wheels may need balancing. With unbalanced tires, handling, tire life, and steering components are affected.

If the vehicle pulls to one side when the steering wheel is straight, or if there’s uneven wear on the tires, a wheel alignment may be needed. The procedure is also recommended after installing new tires.

All of the vehicle’s maintenance needs can be viewed in the Maintenance Summary on the central touchscreen, which provides a record of when common actions were last performed and recommends when to perform them next.

Sources indicate that tesla says that all of these items need to be performed at an authorized service center. This includes servicing the low-voltage and high-voltage batteries. However, there are some maintenance actions that should be considered by owners who want to treat their EVs as their forever cars.

We’ve all heard of “lifetime fluids,” but ask any well-versed mechanic out there, and they’ll say that they don’t exist. Instead, car manufacturers refer to them when it’s their job to maintain the car under warranty. After the warranty expires, the owner is on the hook for all repairs, including those that could have been avoided.

The following recommendations are nowhere to be found in Tesla’s maintenance initiative, but some technicians still recommend them. Even though they’re not required actions, Tesla has service procedures for all of them, and its service centers can perform them if the owner asks.

Tesla used to recommend changing the transmission fluid in its drive units every 100,000 miles, but that went the way of the dodo. Now, the company’s transmissions, which transfer power from the electric motor to the wheels, have built-in filters, but plenty of mechanics out there believe that it’s good practice to renew the fluid every 100,000 miles at the latest.

In a recent development, the Model 3 uses coolant to keep the high-voltage battery at an optimal temperature. Just like on a combustion car, the coolant needs to be checked and replaced if it becomes contaminated.

Over time, rubber bushes will lose their elasticity or even crack. If this happens, knocks or rattles will make their presence felt, requiring a visit to a service center. Even though Tesla implemented many manufacturing novelties over time, it still hasn’t figured out how to replace the age-old rubber bushes found in all cars.

Industry observers note that under warranty, Tesla's authorized service centers should handle all maintenance items. However, after the warranty expires, many of the maintenance actions found on this list can be easily done at home by the owner. Air filter changes and radiator cleaning are DIY jobs that shouldn't take hours to complete, even for people who haven't done any mechanical work before.

Best of all, though, Tesla has published all of its service manuals online, and anyone can follow the service procedures to do maintenance jobs. What's more, in recent years, plenty of independent EV shops have popped up, and they can usually handle repairs and maintenance at lower costs than Tesla. That noted, Tesla's own shops will happily inspect and repair older models, too.

According to recent reports, keeping an EV on the road should be much cheaper than a gas car, but it still requires some maintenance. Over a five-year period, the main maintenance items should include at least one set of latest tires, multiple tire rotations, two brake fluid tests and maybe one flush, two cabin air filter replacements, several brake checks, and at least one set of wiper blades.

#5085. The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – October 30, 2026

📅 30 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1690 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gameinformer ↗ Open Full Page

The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – October 30, 2026

📅 30 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1690 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Welcome to Devil's Night, the night before Halloween, where video games are best served scary.
  • Phantom Blade Zero is one of the best action games I’ve ever played, and it’s certainly one of the most impressive to watch.
  • If you have any fond memories of IllFonic’s ill-fated Friday the 13th: The Game as I do, you simply must play the studio’s latest, Halloween: The Game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Welcome to Devil's Night, the night before Halloween, where video games are best served scary. After tomorrow night – Halloween proper – no more scary video games allowed. At least not until mid-September, 2027. I'm sorry, I don't make the rules. Below you will find our weekend gaming recommendations (which is actually surprisingly light on scary games – apologies), but before that, here are some of the biggest stories of the week.

Phantom Blade Zero is one of the best action games I’ve ever played, and it’s certainly one of the most impressive to watch. Beijing-based developer S-Game uses China’s Wuxia brand of action (which was actually banned for some time during the 20th Century by the country’s government) to create a stylish, fluid, and hyper-engaging combat system. It will constantly leave you in awe that action combat can look this good. But looks aren’t everything. Fortunately, Phantom Blade Zero delivers on all fronts, with weapon mechanics so detailed that picking up a new blade can feel like unlocking a new character in a fighting game. The story won’t blow your socks off, but it’s certainly engaging and enticing enough to bring you through Phantom Blade Zero’s 40 or so hours of content. If you’re not interested in the “perfect ending,” which is the only satisfactory one in my opinion, you can complete the game in less than 30 hours. S-Game mixes high-octane combat with sprawling and rewarding exploration to create a must-play during this already busy season of games. You can read more of my thoughts in the Game Informer Phantom Blade Zero review, and if you are hopping in this weekend, be sure to check out my list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks I wish I knew before starting it.

If you have any fond memories of IllFonic’s ill-fated Friday the 13th: The Game as I do, you simply must play the studio’s latest, Halloween: The Game. It is essentially Friday the 13th with Michael Myers instead of Jason, but with a decade of lessons learned from the team’s teeth carving in other horror properties and games. You’re either Michael or a citizen; the former wants to kill you and all the NPCs in various suburban maps, while the latter must rescue as many NPCs as possible while staying alive themselves. It’s that classic cat-and-mouse formula IllFonic is the master of, but with all the style, substance, and synths of John Carpenter’s Halloween masterpiece. Plus, Halloween: The Game features IllFonic’s first crack at a single-player campaign, and while it’s largely a tutorial for playing as Michael, if you’re a Halloween mega-fan like me, it’s worth checking out if only to take part in some of the film’s most iconic kills. You can read more of my thoughts in the Game Informer Halloween: The Game review here, and if you’re hopping in this weekend, there’s a upcoming map, additional Halloween-themed cosmetics to unlock, and more waiting for you.

In a recent development, overwatch is in the midst of its Halloween event, which have always historically been pretty interesting. This year it's Mystery Madness: Graveyard Games. In it, you begin by picking one of three characters in a random role. And then, as the game progresses, you choose perks that upgrade, alter, or completely change what your character can do. It can get really chaotic where by round three characters like Orisa might be three times her normal size or Torbjorn might have placed a giant turret on Mercy's making her a flying death machine. There are also Halloween skins, as well.

It has been revealed that tom the Postgirl is an odd little adventure that I'd recommend to fans of Untitled Goose Game. You play as Tom, a creepy girl who's tasked with delivering packages to the people of her wacky town, which is depicted with storybook-style illustrations and a color palette limited to black, white, and red. On the surface, you're delivering packages, but the game's real story is based on Tom's tendency to peep where she shouldn't, peering into townsfolks' windows to watch their odd lives. On house is full of kids who live like dogs; another has a couple with a bizarre obsession with tickling. You never know what each window might reveal, and I quickly sympathized with (and enabled) Tom's compulsion. You also have the capacity to cause quite a bit of trouble by stomping on flowers, haphazardly snipping strings and cords, or even stealing packages and using them for your own mischievous purposes. It's a pretty short experience, completable in just a few hours, making it a nice palate cleanser between the massive releases at the end of the year.

This Devolver Digital-published game has a simple but head-turning premise. You’re a profoundly angry woman who returns to her small hometown armed with nothing but a sledgehammer, which she uses to smash everything in sight. The town is also inhabited by robots possessing human consciousnesses. Swinging the hammer can either punch holes through walls or, with enough force, reduce entire buildings to rubble. But why is she doing this? Why is she so mad? A substantial part of Virtue and a Sledgehammer’s allure is its fascinating and well-written tale about the protagonist’s strained relationships with her sister and mother. Learning more about their lives requires you to keep smashing, but the more you learn, the more you begin to question whether smashing everything is actually a good idea.

Industry observers note that this bizarre indie blends fun match-3 puzzle-solving with tower defense gameplay wrapped around a funny but surreal story. The match-3 gameplay involves sliding tiles to match geographic elements like castles, trees, and rivers to collect resources that feed into the tower defense portion. Depending on how the board looks when the puzzle portion ends, you send troops (sustained by the resources you collected) to attack/defend against rival castles and gather more items; board positioning determines how well this can go. The two mechanics feed into each other to create a fun loop that grows in complexity as latest mechanics are introduced. Did I mention the game is also very weird? The silly tale centers on a medieval court designating you the chosen savior to rescue their lost queen (and many other tasks), and the dumb tone adds personality to a sometimes dry genre. Titanium Court charmed and impressed us when it debuted on PC earlier this year, and now console and mobile players get their chance to hold court.

Sword of the Sea is a beautiful, 2025 game about surfing through the sand atop a floating sword. It recalls Journey, the emotional 2012 PlayStation game, which makes sense as it comes from the artists and developers that worked on that game, developer Giant Squid. Giant Squid also made 2016's Abzû and 2020's The Pathless. It's a talented team and Sword of the Sea maintains that reputation. And now you can play it on Switch 2. You can read my full review of the game (though this review pertains to the PlayStation 5 version) right here.

Cities: Skylines arrived on PC more than a decade ago, but is still revered as one of the greatest modern city-builders. Even now, three years after the sequel's release, Paradox continues supporting and porting the original game. A couple years after its initial release, Cities: Skylines received a strong console port, which did an admirable job of adapting the controls to gamepads, but the Switch version was always the weakest of the bunch. As of this week, Switch 2 owners can play a less compromised version, expanding the Switch's 9-tile limit to a much larger 25-tile limit, as well as better performance and textures, better control panels, and a ton of DLC and added content. And on top of that, if you own the Switch 1 version, you get a deep discount on the Switch 2 version.

While not specifically about this new Switch 2 version, you can read our original reviews of the base PC version here, and the base console version here.

Minecraft has held its dominant spot in pop culture for so long that it's easy to forget a simple fact about it: the game is awesome. This week, it's coming to Switch 2, giving potential miners another platform to explore procedurally-generated caves in. You've certainly heard of it, and you've probably played it, but I still feel it often doesn't get the flowers it deserves in high-level critical discussions about games, despite its regular cadence of major updates. The opening gameplay loop is so satisfying that for many of my peers, whether they regularly play video games or not, it's only a matter of time before they boot up a new world again. While you can never play the game for the first time again, if you haven't checked it out in a couple years, you might be surprised by the amount of new blocks, materials, and mobs they've added in recent updates. And if you've never played before, the Switch 2 launch is as good a time as any to see what all the fuss is about.

According to recent reports, the card game incarnation of Arkham Horror remains one of the best narrative-driven and horror-themed tabletop games around, and it's an easy recommendation if you're looking for something engaging to dive into on Halloween night. Rooted in the monsters and mysteries of the Cthulhu Mythos, this living card game is built on major core sets and expansions. But unlike a TCG, each new installment has the same cards included, fueling the cooperative adventures you'll undertake together with your fellow players. Last year Arkham Horror: The Card Game did something of a soft relaunch for a chapter 2 of its narrative, and that new core set is an ideal place to jump on  play. Players each control an individual investigator as they explore arcane and weird mysteries, confront monsters, and unfold plots of cultists, ancient entities, and forbidden lore. For fans of cosmic horror storytelling, it's an easy pick.

Sources indicate that bad signal or dead zones? Download your concerns before you leave and read anywhere.
